"If that is so, I ask the Master to lead me through the meaning of these words. The Master said: "Where have you come from? Yunqing said: "I am simply abiding; where have I come from?"
Chongfu Monastery in Guohuan, Quanzhou. Zen Master Wenju Huirì was the son of the Huang family of Fuzhou. He possessed extraordinary qualities from birth.

Upon reaching adulthood, he served as a jailer in the county prison; however, he frequently abandoned his duties to visit Master Shenguang of Guan and Master An of Xiuyuan, whom the officials were unable to restrain.
Later, he went to pay his respects to Zen Master Tankong at the Wansui Pagoda and received the tonsure.
He did not wear the *kāṣāya* robe nor had he received full ordination; he wore only a sash made of variegated silk.
He went again to Shenguang, who said, "I am not your teacher. Go and pay respects to the West Hall. The Master took a small green bamboo staff and entered the Dharma Hall of the West Hall.
Seeing him from afar, the Master of the Hall smiled and said, "Go to the Nirvāṇa Hall. The Master responded with an assent and entered, wheeling his bamboo staff.
At that time, there were about five hundred monks afflicted with a contagious disease. The Master used his staff to point at them one by one, and each rose as soon as he was pointed at.
The King of Min honored him deeply and established a monastery for him to reside in. Thereafter, many miraculous traces appeared. He passed away during the Qianning era of the Tang dynasty.
When Xuefeng arrived with his assembly at Master Fujiang of Taizhou, he asked, "There are currently two hundred people here who wish to spend the summer retreat;
would this be permissible? The Master took his staff and drew a line, saying, "If you can say 'it cannot be,' then it will be allowed. Xuefeng then desisted.
A monk asked Master Lushui of Luzhou, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "Do you see the flower garden railing in front of the courtyard? The monk was speechless.

Chan Master Yuanming of Wenshu Monastery in Guangzhou was the son of the Chen family of Fuzhou. Having attained the essential meaning under Daomai, he later traveled to Xuefeng to seek further instruction;

there he found that the Dharma has no differing flavors. He once visited Mount Wutai and beheld a manifested transformation of Mañjuśrī, whereupon he established a monastery according to the site and named it after Mañjuśrī.
During the Kaibao era, the State Councilor for Military Affairs Li Chongju went on inspection to protect the region.
In the south, Li [Yuan] entered a monastery and, upon seeing an image of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, asked a monk, "Why does Kṣitigarbha have his hand extended?
The monk replied, "The jewel in his hand was stolen by a thief. Li then asked the Master, "If it is indeed Kṣitigarbha, why did he suffer at the hands of a thief?
The Master said, "He has been caught today. Li bowed in thanks.

Venerable Master Yan-yang of Xinxing in Hongzhou, whose name was Shanxin, was a successor of Chan Master Zhaozhou Sheng. When he first visited Zhaozhou, he asked, "What is it like when one brings nothing at all?
Zhaozhou said, "Put it down. The Master said, "Since I am bringing nothing at all, what is there to put down?"

"What is it? the Master asked. The monk said, "I cannot let it go; please take it away. Upon these words, the Master attained great enlightenment. Later, while residing there, a monk asked, "What is the Buddha?
The Master said, "A clod of earth. The monk asked, "What is the Dharma? The Master said, "The ground is shaking. The monk asked, "What is the Sangha?
The Master said, "Eating porridge and eating rice. A monk asked, "What is the water of Xinxing? The Master said, "The face."
Formerly, while at Jiangli, he was asked, "What is it to manifest form in response to things? The Master said, "Bring me the bed over here.
The Master always had a snake and a tiger that followed him; he would take food from his own hand and give it to them.

A monk asked Zen Master Huijue of Guangxiao Monastery in Yangzhou: "The flower of awakening has just blossomed and fills all of Sahā; since the Patriarch’s seal came from the West, what matter should he have discussed?

The Master said: "When sentiment arises, wisdom is obstructed. The monk said: "This is the meaning of the Teachings (Śāsana). The Master said: [This is the meaning of the Teachings.]* *Note: The repetition of the Master's response indicates that the dialogue concludes here.*
"What clothes are you wearing? [The Master asked. "When a single blow breaks through empty space, how is it? The Master said, "If you are weary, then rest.
The Master asked the Chancellor Song Qichou, "Do you understand how to speak? Song said, "If it were 'speaking,' one could not even touch upon it.
The Master said, "Is it that there is something one cannot touch upon? Or is it that there is nothing one can touch upon? Song said, "Neither is it like that."

[The monk] said, "Ma? The Master said, "It is that which cannot be grasped, is it not? Song had no reply. The Master led the assembly out and, upon seeing a pillar, joined his palms and said, "How do you do, World-Honored One?
A monk asked, "The Master is the pillar. The Master said, "To cry until the blood flows is of no use;
it is better to keep one's mouth shut and pass through the remainder of spring. [A monk] asked, "From afar you have come to seek the Master; what is your intention? The Master said:
The authorities were strict and did not permit him to stay. He said, "Is there no other expedient? The Master replied, "For now, you may stay overnight in the fire-storage room.
When the Master arrived at Chongshou, Fayan asked, "Where have you recently come from? The Master said, "Zhaozhou.
Fayan said, "I have heard that Zhaozhou has the story about the cypress tree in front of the hall; is this true? The Master said, "No. Fayan said, "Everyone who comes and goes..."
It is said that when a monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? the Master [Nanquan] replied, "The cypress tree in the courtyard.
"How can you say it does not exist, Venerable Sir? the monk asked. The Master said, "The former master truly did not say such a thing.
Do not slander the former master, Reverend. Layman Zhang asked, "What can be done about old age? The Master said, "How old are you? Zhang said, "Eighty. The Master said, "That is enough."
"It means 'old age. The man asked, "What is its ultimate nature? The Master said, "Even at a thousand years of age, it is still not finished.
A layman asked, "I have slaughtered oxen throughout my life; do I have any sin? The Master said, "There is no sin. The man asked, "Why is there no sin?"
The Master said, "Kill one and receive one in return.
A monk asked Zen Master Feng of Guoqing Monastery in Longzhou, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different? The Master said:
The rain nourishes the three types of grass so they flourish; the spring breeze does not wrap one’s head. [A monk] asked, “Ultimately, is this one or two?
The Master said, “Auspicious clouds rise in competition; the rocky caves remain unimpaired. [Another] asked, “What is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, “The table and stand, the chair, the brazier, and the windows. [Another] asked, “What is an ordained person? The Master said, “Copper heads and iron brows; bird beaks.”
Lüshen asked, "What is the fundamental duty of one who has left the household life? The Master said, "In the morning, 'I hope you have had no ill'; at night, 'May you be well.
Lüshen asked, "Before Niutou saw the Fourth Patriarch, why did the hundred birds bring him flowers?
The Master said, "It is like people from Shanfu sending money and goods to an iron ox. Lüshen asked, "After he saw him, why did they no longer bring flowers? The Master said, [The same]."
A wooden horse travels eight hundred *li* before dawn. [A monk] asked: "How does one subdue the mind throughout the twelve periods of the day?
The Master said: "To strike ice seeking fire; one would not encounter it even after eons. [Another] asked: "The twelve divisions of the teachings are for the purpose of silencing a child's crying.
Setting aside this 'silencing the crying,' I ask the Master for a single phrase. The Master said: "A two-horned woman atop a solitary peak. [Another] asked: "What is the Buddha?"
Regarding the general meaning of the Dharma, the Master said: "Śākyamuni is the Ox-Headed Jailor; the Patriarch is the Horse-Faced Attendant.
When asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? the Master said: "Striking the west wall with the east wall. When asked, "What is the phrase that cannot be broken?
the Master said: "Not separated by even a hair’s breadth. At that time, people looked toward him from afar.
A monk asked Chan Master Muchen Conglang of Wuzhou, "When the crane is released from its cage and departs amidst the snow, what then?

The Master said, "I say it is not of a single color. Because of this, the monk asked, "If it is indeed the indestructible diamond body, why did you fall over? The Master replied, "Because of the falling of the diamond. The monk then asked, "Since it is already the indestructible diamond body..."
"Why have you fallen to the ground? The Master struck the meditation seat and said, "Walking, standing, sitting, and lying down.
When the Master was about to pass into nirvana, he spoke a verse: "For thirty years I have dwelt at Mumen; Throughout this time, not a single moment of effort was feigned.
If someone asks me the meaning of the West's arrival, How shall I respond? I raise my eyebrows."
Chan Master Xinjian of Wuzhou did not ordain junior disciples. A monk asked him, "Master, you are advanced in years; why do you not keep a young attendant to serve you?
The Master said, "If there is one who is blind and deaf, seek him out for me. When the monk took his leave, the Master asked, "Where are you going?
The monk replied, "To Kaiyuan Temple in the prefectural seat. The Master said, "I have a message to entrust to the Abbot of that temple."
“Can you take this away? He replied, “I would be honored. The Master said, “I suppose you can do nothing about it either.
A monk asked Master Duofu of Hangzhou, “What is the single grove of bamboo at Duofu?
The Master said, “One stalk, two stalks leaning. The monk said, “I do not understand. The Master said, “Three stalks, four stalks curved. [The monk] asked, “What is the *nà* (patch-robed monk)?”
Regarding the matter of what is beneath the robes, the Master said, "There are many who harbor doubts about this. [The monk] asked, "Why is it so?
The Master said, "Hiding one's head within the moon.
When Master Ximù of Yizhou was ascending the hall, a layman raised his hand and said, "The Master himself is precisely 'one head'."
"Donkey! The Master said. "I, this old monk, have been ridden by you. The scholar was speechless. Three days later, he returned and reported, "I was robbed by bandits three days ago.
The Master picked up his staff and drove him out. At other times, the Master would suddenly call out to his attendant;
when the attendant responded, the Master would say, "The night is deep and quiet; let us deliberate with him."
Chan Master Changshui Xiangyan’s Dharma heir, Chan Master Changtong of Xuedou in Mingzhou, was a native of the Li family in Xingzhou. He went to visit Changsha, who asked him, “Where are you from?
The Master replied, “A man from Xingzhou. Changsha said, “I say you did not come from there. The Master said, “Does the Master [not agree]?”
"Have you ever lived here? he asked. The monk remained silent. Only then did the Master allow him to enter the room. After the monk had settled there, a monk asked, "What is the secret chamber?
The Master said, "It does not admit even a breath of wind. The monk asked, "Who is the person within the secret chamber? The Master said, "All the sages seek to behold it, yet they do not see it.
The monk bowed, and the Master said, "A thousand sages cannot conceive of it; ten thousand sages cannot discuss it. Even when heaven and earth perish," [the chamber remains].

It is indestructible. Whether empty space encompasses all or not, nothing can be compared to it; throughout the three periods of time, it never arises. A monk asked, "What is the place from which the Buddhas of the three periods of time emerge?
The Master said, "He does not consent to acknowledge that you exist within the three periods.

After the monk had been silent for a long while, the Master asked, "Do you understand? "If not, then for the time being, take up the investigation within the state where even the Buddha cannot be found. At such a time, one must always...
When consciousness is exhausted and effort has vanished, even a sudden flash of thought that arises is already an injury to others; how much more so the case with words and phrases?
On the seventh month of the second year of the Tianyou era, he passed away. His stupa was erected in the southwest corner of the temple.
Master Zhuyou was a Dharma successor of Master Shiti.
Once, while serving his master, an attendant requested that he take a bath. The Master said, "Since you do not wash away dust, nor do you wash the body, how will you proceed?
The attendant replied, "The Master should go first; I shall bring the soapwort. The Master laughed heartily.
A newly arrived monk stood before the Master; after a short while, he departed. The Master said, "What grounds for justification do you have?
The monk returned again. The Master said, "You have found your justification. The monk asked, "And what of it after you have justified yourself? The Master said, "It can be buried away."
The monk cried out, "O Blue Heaven! O Blue Heaven! The Master said, "Just now you were like that, but even now it is still not right. The monk then went out.
One day, seeing the attendant carrying his bowl toward the hall, the Master called to him. The attendant responded, "Yes? The Master asked, "Where are you going?
The attendant replied, "I am going to the hall for the midday meal. The Master said, "How could I not know that you are going to the hall for the midday meal? The attendant [remained silent].
The monk said, "Aside from this, what else would you say? The Master said, "I am simply asking you about your fundamental matter.
The monk said, "If the Master asks about my fundamental matter, I am actually going to the hall for the midday meal. The Master said, "You do not fail in being my attendant."
A monk asked Master Shengguang of Taizhou, a successor of Chan Master Zihu Zong, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "Lychees of Fuzhou;
*stathoa* trees of Quanzhou. The monk asked, "What are the two characters for 'Buddha-dharma'? The Master said, "If you wish to speak, then speak. The monk said: [proceeded to speak].
"Please teach me the Way. The Master said, "The pierced-eared barbarian monk smiles and nods his head. Longhua Zhao came forward; the Master seized him and asked, "What is it?
Zhao said, "Do not err. The Master then let go of him. Zhao said, "I have long admired the Radiant Light (Śubhaprabha).
The Master remained silent. Zhao then took his leave. As the Master saw him off at the gate, he said, "After this parting, where shall we meet again? Zhao gave a shout.
[The Master] rebuked him and departed.
Master Fushí of Zhāngzhōu ascended the hall and said: "I, this mountain monk, have opened a divination shop. It can determine people's poverty or wealth and settle their life or death. A monk asked:
"Setting aside life and death, as well as poverty and wealth, and not falling into the five elements—please, Master, speak directly. The Master [replied]: [He laughed and departed.]
He said: "Gold, wood, water, fire, and earth.
A monk asked Master Zitong, "What is the realm of Zitong? The Master said, "Can you put sand into your eyes?
The monk said, "Very well done! But I do not even recognize the realm of Zitong. The Master said, "I do not conceal this matter from you. That monk—
As he was about to go out, the Master descended from his meditation seat, seized him, and said, "Today we have a fine case;
I have not yet managed to get a single coin's worth of it into my hands. The monk replied, "Fortunately, I am a monk. The Master pushed him away and said, "Calamity does not come alone."
When the Venerable Rirong Yuan was visited by the Senior Monk Huo, the Master clapped his hands three times and said, "A fierce tiger stands in the gateway;
who is its match? Huo replied, "A swift hawk soars toward the heavens; who can catch it? The Master said, "Both are difficult to withstand."
Huo said, "Stop for now; there is no need to resolve this public case. The Master brandished his staff and returned to the abbot’s quarters.
Huo was speechless. The Master said, "This fellow is dead!"
The monk Daowu of Guannan in Xiangzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Chang of Guannan.
Once, while passing through a village and countryside, he heard a shaman performing music for the gods and saying, "The conscious spirit is non-existent.
At that moment, he attained sudden enlightenment. Later, he visited Chan Master Chang to have his realization certified. He subsequently traveled to the gate of Deshan.
The flavor of the Dharma became even more profound. After he settled there, whenever he ascended the hall, he would wear a lotus-patterned hat, don a cassock, and hold a ritual tablet.

As the drum was beaten and the flute blown, he would exclaim: "Lord Lu Sanlang! The conscious spirit knows, the unconscious spirit does not know! The spirit comes from the void and returns to the void! Then he would descend from his seat.
At other times he said: "The drum of Guannan is struck; the song of Deshan is sung. A monk asked him:
"What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master took up a fan and bowed, saying, "Aho! At another time, he held a wooden sword across his shoulder and performed a dance.
A monk asked, "Where did you get that sword in your hand? The Master threw it to the ground. The monk then placed it back in the Master's hand.
The Master asked, "Where did you get it? The monk had no reply. The Master said, "I grant you three days to provide an answer."

The Master offered a turning phrase, but the monk had no reply. The Master himself took his place, brandishing a sword across his shoulder and dancing, saying, "One must act like this before it can be achieved.
When Zhaozhou visited the Master, the Master was wearing a leopard-skin loincloth and holding a *jiliao* staff, waiting beneath the triple gate with one foot raised.
As soon as he saw Zhaozhou, he greeted him with a loud shout and stood there. Zhaozhou said:
"Wait here attentively. The Master then gave a single bow and departed. [A monk] asked, "What is the house style of the Master?
The Master descended from his meditation seat, performed a woman’s bow, and said, "Thank you for coming from afar; there is nothing with which to serve you.
Wait until you ask Guankui; what will he say? Guankui replied, "The Unranked. The Master asked, "Is it like empty space? Guankui said, "This butcher!"
The Master said, "If there were birth that could be killed, one would never grow weary.
When the Monk Luohan of Zhanzhou first visited Guannan, he asked, "What is the source of the Great Way?

Guannan struck him once with his fist, and the Master immediately attained realization. He then composed a song, saying: "In the seventh year of the Xiantong era, I first studied the Way; wherever I went..."
Encountering words, he spoke of not recognizing them; a knot of doubt swirled within his heart like a basket. For three springs he found no joy, dwelling only among the forests and springs.
Suddenly encountering the Dharma King seated upon his mat, he laid bare his doubts before the Master. The Master rose from the mat as a *nāga*.
Baring his shoulder and striking a single punch against his chest, he shattered the mass of doubt like a startled wildcat. Raising his head, he saw the sun just beginning to rise;
from that moment on, he has been steady and firm, remaining perpetually joyful.

He hears only the full rumbling of a satisfied belly, and no longer wanders east or west to carry his alms bowl. He further composed a verse, saying: "A guest at leisure within the universe, among men..."
I am a wild monk; let others laugh as they will. I roam freely wherever I go.
Chan Master Liao Ran of Mount Moshan, a nun and successor of Chan Master Dayu of Gaoyuan, said to herself when the Venerable Guankui Xian arrived: "If we are truly equals..."
He stood there; when [the Master] did not stop him, he pushed over the meditation seat and entered the hall.

The Master sent an attendant to ask, "Have you come from traveling the mountains, or have you come for the sake of the Buddha-dharma? Xī replied, "I have come for the sake of the Buddha-dharma. The Master then ascended the seat, and Xī went up to pay his respects.
The Master asked, "Where did you come from today, Senior? He replied, "From the crossroads. The Master said, "Why didn't you cover it over? Xiu was speechless.
(Moshan spoke on his behalf, saying, "How could you have reached this place? Only then did he prostrate. The Master asked, "What is Moshan? The Master said, "It does not show its crown."
[The monk] asked, "What is the Master of Mount Mò? The Master said, "Neither male nor female. Xī then shouted, "Why do you not transform yourself?
The Master said, "I am neither a spirit nor a ghost; what would I transform into? Thereupon, Xī submitted to his teaching and served as a garden head for three years.
When a monk arrived to pay his respects, the Master said, "You look quite worn out. The monk replied, "Even so, you are still my teacher."
"Son of a lion," the Master said. "Since you are a son of a lion, why are you being ridden by Mañjuśrī?

The monk was unable to answer. [The Master] asked, "What is the mind of the ancient Buddhas? The Master said, "The world collapses and perishes. [The monk] asked, "Why does the world collapse and perish?"
The Master said, "It would be better to have no self at all.
Regarding the Dharma heir of Master Tianlong of Hangzhou, Master Juzhi of Mount Jinhu in Wuzhou: when he first resided in his hermitage, there was a nun named Shiji who came wearing...
Carrying her sunshade and holding her staff, she circumambulated the Master three times and said, "If you can speak the Way, I shall remove my sunshade.
She asked this three times, and the Master remained without reply. The nun then departed. The Master said, "The sun is already late; why do you not stay for a moment?
The nun replied, "If you can speak the Way, I shall stay. Again, the Master had no reply. After the nun had gone, the Master remarked, "Though I possess the physical form of a man, yet..."
"You lack the spirit of a true man. It would be better to abandon this hut and go to various regions to seek out wise teachers.
That night, a mountain deity said to him, "You need not leave this place; a Bodhisattva in human form will come to preach the Dharma for you, Master."
More than ten days later, Dàtiān Lóngshàn Wǔhuáng arrived at the hermitage. The Master went out to welcome him and prostrated, then related the previous events in detail.

Longshen raised a single finger to indicate his meaning, and the Master attained great enlightenment on the spot. From then on, whenever a student came to inquire about the Way, the Master would simply raise a finger;
he had no other teaching or proclamation. There was a young attendant boy who, whenever he saw someone asking a question, would likewise raise a finger.
It was true. People said to the Master, "The Monk’s boy also understands the Buddha-dharma; whenever anyone questions him, he always raises his finger just as you do, Master.
One day, the Master secretly tucked a small knife into his sleeve and asked the boy, "I have heard that you understand the Buddha-dharma—is this true?
The boy replied, "Yes. The Master asked, "What is the Buddha? The boy raised his finger. The Master severed the boy's finger with the knife. The boy—
He cried out and ran away. The Master called to the boy; the boy turned his head back. The Master asked, "What is the Buddha?

The boy raised his hand, and not seeing his own fingers, he attained sudden and great enlightenment. As the Master was about to pass away, he said to the assembly, "I obtained the 'one-finger Zen' of Tianlong;

I have used it throughout my life and it is never exhausted. Having finished speaking, he entered nirvana. (Changqing spoke on behalf of the assembly: "Fine food does not satisfy one who is already full. Xuansha said: "I...")

At that time, had he seen it, he would have snapped off the monk’s finger. Xuangjue said, "Tell me, when Xuansha spoke thus, what was his intention? Yunju Xi said, "As for Xuansha speaking thus, did he approve him or not?

If he approved him, why did he say 'snap off the finger'? If he did not approve him, where does Juzhi’s fault lie? Caoshan (Xingshan) of former times said, "Juzhi’s way of taking it upon himself was crude; he recognized only a single device and a single realm as being uniform. This clapping of hands and striking of palms is his own strange peculiarity at West Garden.

Xuangjue further said, "Tell me, did Juzhi actually attain enlightenment or not? If he attained enlightenment, why did you say his way of taking it upon himself was crude? If he did not attain enlightenment, yet you also said that 'one-finger Chan' is inexhaustible. Tell me, what do you say about Caoshan?"
Where does the meaning lie?
[He was] the Dharma heir of the Venerable Master Chen of Muzhou, the fifth generation under Nanyue.
While serving as the Prefect of Muzhou, Minister Chen Cao was at a vegetarian feast. Picking up a steamed bun, he asked a monk, "Is there such a thing as this in Jiangxi and Hunan?
The monk replied, "What did you just eat, Minister? The official said, "I struck the bell to thank it for its resonance."

Furthermore, during a vegetarian feast for the Sangha, the Master personally distributed the steamed buns. One monk extended his hand as if to receive one, but the Master withdrew it. The monk was speechless. The Master said, "As expected, as expected. He then asked the monk, "I have a matter; can you discuss it with me, Venerable? The monk replied, "Shut that dog's mouth! The Master slapped his own mouth and said, "I, this humble one, am at fault. The monk said, "One who recognizes their error must surely reform. The Master said: "Reform? What error do I have? The monk said, "You have already committed an offense by slapping your own mouth. The Master said, "If I had not slapped my own mouth, would you have been able to say 'I am at fault'? The monk said, "I am at fault. The Master said, "If you are at fault, then you should reform. The monk said, "I will reform. The Master said, "What error do you wish to reform? The monk said, "I wish to reform my previous statement. The Master said, "If you wish to reform your previous statement, then you should reform your current statement. The monk said, "I will reform my current statement. The Master said, "What error do you wish to reform? The monk said, "I wish to reform my saying 'I am at fault. The Patriarch asked, "What principle have you seen that you prostrate yourself? The Master replied, "When I was with Shitou, it was like a mosquito on an iron ox.
The Patriarch said, "Since you have realized this, protect and maintain it well yourself. He served him for three years. One day, the Patriarch asked, "Lately..."
"What is it like when one sees this place? The Master said, "When skin and flesh have fallen away entirely, there remains only the single reality.
The Patriarch said, "What you have attained may be called 'harmonizing with the essence of the mind' and spreading it through the four limbs.
Since this is so, take three strands of bamboo and bind your belly; go dwell in the mountains wherever you please. The Master said, "Who am I that I would dare speak thus?"
He stayed at the mountain. The Patriarch said, "It is not so. There has never been one who practices constantly without abiding, nor one who abides constantly without practicing.
To seek benefit is to find no benefit; to seek to act is to find nothing to do. You should become a vessel for others; do not remain here for long.
The Master then took leave of the Patriarch and returned to Shitou. One day, while sitting upon a rock, Shitou asked him, "You have been here..."
"What do you do? he asked. Wuzhu replied, "I do nothing. Xuedou said, "If that is so, then you are idly sitting. Wuzhu said, "If it were idly sitting, then it would be doing something.
Xuedou said, "You say you do nothing—what is it that you do not do? Wuzhu replied, "Even the thousand sages do not know. Xuedou praised him with a verse:
"From the beginning we have lived together, yet I did not know your name; Spontaneously following along, you simply walk this way. Since ancient times..."
"Even those of superior virtue do not recognize it; how could ordinary people in their moments of haste possibly understand it?
Later, Shitou offered this saying: "Words and active engagement have no connection [to it]. The Master said, "Neither words nor active engagement have any connection [to it].
Shitou said, "In my place here, a needle cannot pierce. The Master said, "In my place here, it is like planting flowers upon a stone. Shitou approved of this. Thereafter, [the Master] resided at...

Daowu asked, "What did you do in your previous life, Master? The Master replied, "I was simply weak and frail; I just passed the time that way.
Daowu asked, "On what basis can you say such a thing? The Master said, "I never even opened a book. (Shishuang’s variant says: "I never once unrolled a scroll.")
The scroll had not yet been unrolled when the head monk announced, "The bell has been struck; we request the Master to ascend the hall. The Master said, "Go and carry my alms bowl for me.
The monk replied, "For how long has it been since the Master became handless? The Master said, "You have merely donned the *kāṣāya* in vain.
The monk asked, "I am simply like this; what about you, Master? The Master said, "I have no such followers as these. Thus he spoke.

The Master said, "I have a broken-legged cauldron that I need him to carry up and down. Yunyan said, "In that case, I shall lend you a hand.
The Master then desisted. While the head gardener was planting vegetables, the Master said, "Planting is not an obstacle."
"Do not let the roots of what you have planted sprout. Daowu said, "If you do not allow the roots to sprout, what will the great assembly eat?

The Master said, "Do you have a mouth? Daowu had no reply. While Daowu and Yunyan were standing in attendance, the Master pointed to two trees on the mountain—one withered and one flourishing—and asked Daowu, "Which is the withered one?
Which is the flourishing one? Daowu said, "The flourishing one. The Master said, "..."
"Vividly so in all places; let the brilliant light depart. He then asked Yunyan, "Which is it: the withered or the flourishing? Yuyan said, "The withered.
The Master said, "Vividly so in all places; let it be released into withered stillness. Gao the Śrāmaṇera suddenly arrived.
The Master said, "Which is it: the withered or the flourishing? Gao said, "As for the withered, let it wither of its own accord; as for the flourishing..."
Tao Rong. The Master looked toward Daowu and Yunyan and said, "It is not so, it is not so. He asked, "How can one avoid being deluded by various sensory objects?

The Abbot [was present]. The Head of the Monastery followed behind him and asked, "Since you, Preceptor, have consented to speak for the sake of the assembly, why do you not utter a single word?
The Master said, "The Sutras have masters of the Sutras; the Treatises have masters of the Treatises. How can they blame old monk me? The Master asked, "What is Yunyan doing?
Yunyan replied, "Carrying manure. The Master said, "And what about that other one? Yunyan replied, "He is here. The Master said, "..."
"Where are you going? he asked. "I am going to carry things for another," he replied. The Master said, "Why do you not teach him to walk side by side?
"Do not slander him, Master," he said. "It is not right to speak thus," the Master said. "How should one speak? he asked. "Have you ever carried anything for him? the Master asked.
While the Master was seated, a monk asked, "What are you contemplating so intently? The Master said, "I am contemplating that which cannot be contemplated.
The monk asked, "How can one contemplate that which cannot be contemplated? The Master said, "It is not contemplation. Another asked, "When a student intends to return to his hometown, what then?
The Master said, "Your parents' entire bodies are covered in red sores; they lie amidst a thicket of thorns. You—"
"Where do you go? [The monk] said, "In that case, I shall not return. The Master said, "You must indeed return.
If you return to your hometown, I will give you a prescription for ceasing the consumption of grain. [The monk] said, "I ask for it at once.

The Master said, "At the two formal assemblies, you must not chew so much as a single grain of rice. [The monk] asked, "What is nirvana? The Master said, "Before you have even opened your mouth, call it..."
"What are you doing? The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Hunan. The Master said, "Is the water in Lake Dongting full yet?
He replied, "Not yet. The Master said, "It has been raining for so long; why is it not full? The monk was speechless. (Daowu said, "It is full. Yunyan said, "It is limpid and still.

A monk from Jiangxi approached. The Master struck the meditation seat three times with his staff. The monk said, "I roughly know where this leads.
The Master threw down the staff; the monk was speechless. The Master called to his attendant to serve tea, saying, "This will give this monk a hard time traversing the prefectures and counties.
The Master asked Layman Pang, "Can this matter be contained within the One Vehicle? The Layman replied, "I..."
The layman said, "I simply seek advancement day by day; I do not know if I am capable of wearing it. The Master said, "Layman, have you not seen Shitou?

"One Vehicle. [A monk] asked, "The fundamental principle has been lost today. The Master said, "Yes, yes. He ascended the hall and said: "The Patriarch taught only that we should protect [the mind].

Yunyan asked, "What thing is making a noise? The Master drew the blade and suddenly made a cutting motion toward his own mouth. (Dongshan raised this up and said to the assembly: "Look at how Yaoshan laid down his body for this...")

He asked the head cook, "How long have you been here? The cook replied, "Three years. The Master said, "I do not know you at all.
The cook was bewildered and left in a fit of indignation. The Master asked him, "What is the most urgent matter regarding body and life? The cook replied, "Do not sow mixed seeds.
The Master asked, "With what then shall I make offerings? The cook replied, "One who has nothing. The Master then ordered the master of offerings to go out on a begging tour for sweet rice.
Someone asked him where he had come from, and he replied, "From Yaoshan. Gan said, "What have you come for? He replied, "To teach and transform.

Gan said, "Have you brought medicine with you? He replied, "The practitioner—what illness does he have? Gan then offered two ingots of silver, intending that if there were someone in the mountains, he would return with these items;
if not, he would simply leave them. The host then returned and submitted his report. The Master asked, "Have you returned?"

"How fast? The host said, "I asked about the Buddha-dharma and received two ingots of silver. The Master ordered him to repeat those words. After the host had repeated them, the Master said, "Return them to him quickly;
your son has been stolen by a thief. The host immediately returned them. Gan said, "There was someone there from the beginning," and so he added more silver as an offering.
(Tongan Xian said: "Had I known the attendant would ask in such a way, I would never have said, 'Yaoshan has come. He then asked a monk: "I hear it is said...")
"Do you understand arithmetic? He replied, "I dare not say so. The Master said, "Then try calculating for this old monk. The monk had no response.

(Yunyan raised this question to Dongshan, saying, "How would you do it? Dongshan said, "Please tell me the Master’s birth month. The Master wrote the character for "Buddha" (佛) and asked Dowu, "What character is this?
Dowu said, "The character for Buddha. The Master said, "A talkative fellow! [Another monk] asked, "My own matter is not yet clear; I beg the Master for instruction. The Master...
After a long silence, he said: "It would not be difficult for me to speak a single phrase for you now, provided that you could see it immediately upon hearing it;
that would still leave some margin. But if you enter into deliberation, you will instead create my own fault.

It is better, therefore, that we each keep our mouths shut to avoid implicating one another and the assembly. At the night assembly, no lamps were lit. The Master gave this instruction: "I have one..."
"The ox gives birth to a calf; I shall tell you immediately. A monk said, "The ox has given birth to a calf, yet you, Master, do not say so.
The Master said, "Attendant, bring a lamp. The monk withdrew and joined the assembly.

(Yunyan related this to Dongshan, who said, "This monk indeed understands, yet he refuses to prostrate. He asked the monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Nanquan. The Master said, "While there...")
"For how long? He replied, "Roughly through winter and summer. The Master said, "In that case, you have become a water buffalo.
He replied, "Though I am among them, I have never entered their dining hall. The Master said, "Are you sucking the southeast wind? He replied, "Master, do not be mistaken;
the person who picks up the spoon and holds the chopsticks is right here. He then asked about the time before Bodhidharma had arrived.
"Does this land still possess the intent of the Patriarchs? The Master said, "It does. The monk asked, "If it does, why has the Patriarch come again?
The Master said, "Precisely because it exists that he has come. While reading a scripture, a monk asked, "Master, you usually do not permit others to read scriptures;
why then do you read them yourself? The Master said, "I am merely trying to cover my eyes. The monk said, "I am studying..."
"Has the Master attained it yet? The Master said, "If you look at it, even cowhide must be pierced. (Changqing said, "What fault is there in the eyes?
Xuangjue said, "Now tell me, did Changqing understand Yaoshan’s meaning, or did he not? A monk asked, "In the shallow grass of the level field, the deer gather in herds;
how does one shoot the leader of the herd? The Master said, "Watch the arrow! The monk threw himself down and lay prostrate. The Master said, "Attendant, drag this fellow out!"
The "dead man" (the monk) then ran away. The Master said, "What limit is there for this fellow who plays with a lump of mud?
Li Ao, the Prefect of Langzhou, asked, "What is your surname, Master? The Master replied, "It is precisely now.

Li did not understand and instead asked the monastery attendant, "I just asked the Master his surname, and he said, 'It is precisely now. I do not know what his surname is. The attendant said, "It is thus."

[The Master] replied, “Then his surname is Han. When the teacher heard this, he said, “To be so unable to distinguish between good and evil—if it were summer, when answering him, you would say his surname is Heat.
One night, as the Master was walking up and down on the mountain, the clouds suddenly parted and he saw the moon.

He let out a great roar, which echoed for about ninety li to the east of Liyang. All the residents there claimed it came from their own neighbors; the next morning, they took turns blaming one another.
When he arrived at Yaoshan, the assembly said, "Last night, the Master let out a great roar from the mountain peak. Li composed a poem for him, which says:
"Having chosen this secluded dwelling, it accords with my rustic sentiments; Throughout the year, there is neither sending off nor welcoming.

Sometimes I ascend straight to the solitary peak’s summit, And beneath the moon, I tear through the clouds and let out one long cry. On the sixth day of the eleventh month in the eighth year of the Taihe era, he approached the end of his life.

He cried out, "The Dharma Hall is collapsing! The Dharma Hall is collapsing! The assembly all took up pillars to prop it up, whereupon the Master raised his hand and said, "You do not understand my meaning," and then he entered nirvana.

His stupa was erected in the northeastern corner of the monastery. During the Tang dynasty, Emperor Wenzong posthumously conferred upon him the title Great Master Hongdao (Master of Expansive Way), and the stupa was named Huacheng (City of Transformation).
Chan Master Tianran of Danxia in Dengzhou had originally studied the Confucian classics. As he was about to enter Chang’an to take the imperial examinations, he happened to stay overnight at an inn.
Suddenly, he dreamed that white light filled the room. An interpreter said, "This is an auspicious omen for the realization of emptiness.

By chance, a Chan practitioner asked him, "Where are you going, worthy sir? He replied, "I am going to select an official post. The Chan practitioner said, "How does selecting an official compare to selecting a Buddha? He replied:
"Where should one go to choose a Buddha? The meditator replied, "Now the Great Master Ma has appeared in the world in Jiangxi;

this is the field for choosing a Buddha. You, O virtuous one, may go there. He then went directly to Jiangxi. Upon first seeing the Patriarch, the Master [Ma] used his hand to push back the front of the other's head-wrap (*fuhou*).
The Patriarch [Huineng] looked at him for a long time and said, "Nanyue Shitou is your teacher. Having received this instruction, he returned to Shitou.

Previously, he had intended to offer himself [to the master]. Shitou said, "Go to the fodder shed. The Master bowed in thanks and entered the quarters of the novices, where he served in the kitchen in turn for three years.
One day, Shitou addressed the assembly, saying, "Tomorrow, clear the weeds in front of the Buddha Hall.
When the next day arrived, the assembly and the novice attendants each prepared spades and pickaxes to clear the weeds; the Master alone, however, filled a basin with water.
He washed his head with water and knelt before the stone image. The statue looked at him and smiled, whereupon it shaved his hair and preached the precepts to him.
The Master then covered his ears and departed. He went again to Jiangxi to visit Mazu;
without even bowing in greeting, he entered the monks' hall and sat astride the neck of the sacred monk (śāstṛ). The assembly was startled and immediately informed Mazu, who went there in person.

Entering the hall and looking at him, [Nanyue] said, "My son is Tianran (Natural). The Master immediately descended from his seat, prostrated, and said, "I thank the Master for bestowing this Dharma-name.
Thereupon he was named Tianran. The Patriarch asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Shitou. The Patriarch said, "The path at Shitou is slippery; did it cause you to fall?
The Master said, "If I had fallen, I would not have come here. He then took up his staff and traveled to observe the various regions.
He resided on the Huading Peak of Mount Tiantai for three years. He then traveled to Jingshan in Yuhang to pay homage to National Teacher Guoyi.
During the Yuanhe era of the Tang dynasty, he went to Longmen and Xiangshan in the capital city of Luoyang, where he became friends with Master Funiu.
Later, while at Huilin Monastery, he encountered a great cold; taking a wooden Buddha, he burned it for fire. The monastery head reprimanded him, saying, "How can you burn my wooden [Buddha]?"
The Master [Huangbo] used a wooden staff to brush away the ashes and said, "I burned this to obtain the *śarīra* (relics). The host said, "How can a wooden Buddha have *śarīra*?
The Master replied, "If there are no *śarīra*, then take two more statues and burn them. Thereafter, the host's eyebrows and beard fell out.

Later, the Master went to visit National Teacher Zhong and asked the attendant, "Is the National Teacher here? [The attendant] replied, "He is indeed here, but he does not see guests. The Master said:

[The Master] said, "It has been born from something exceedingly deep and remote. [The attendant] said, "Even the Buddha-eye cannot see it. The Master said, "A dragon begets a dragon cub; a phoenix begets a phoenix chick.
When the National Teacher awoke from his sleep, the attendant informed him of this, whereupon the National Teacher struck the attendant with twenty blows of the staff and sent him away.
The Master heard this and said, "It is no mistake that you are the National Teacher of Nanyang. The next day he went again to pay his respects;
as soon as he saw the National Teacher, he spread out his sitting mat. The National Teacher said, "No need, no need. The Master stepped back, and the National Teacher said, "Just so, just so."
The Master stepped forward again. The National Teacher said, "Not so, not so. The Master circumambulated the National Teacher once and then departed.
The National Teacher said, "The time since the Sage has passed; people are mostly indolent. Thirty years hence, such a man as this will be difficult to find."
The Master went to visit Layman Pang and saw his daughter, Lingzhao, washing vegetables. The Master asked, "Is the Layman here?
The girl set down her vegetable basket and stood with her hands folded. The Master asked again, "Is the Layman here? The girl picked up the basket and walked away.
The Master then turned back. A short while later, the Layman returned; the girl recounted the previous conversation. The Layman said, "Danxia was here."
"Ma! The woman said, "He has gone. The master said, "A red soil coating on a cow's udder. On another day, he visited Layman Pang and they met at the gate.
The master asked, "Is the Layman here? The Layman replied, "When hungry, one does not choose one's food.
The master said, "Is Old Pang here? The Layman replied, "Heaven! Heaven! and then went straight into the house. The master said, "Heaven! Heaven! and then [went inside].
[The Master] returned. On the way back to Mazu’s place, he encountered an old man with a young boy.
The Master asked, "Where do you dwell? The old man replied, "Above is heaven; below is earth. The Master said, "What if heaven were to collapse and the earth were to sink?
The old man cried out, "Heaven! Heaven! The boy let out a single sigh. The Master said, "Without a father, there would be no [son]."
He gave birth to a son. The old man then took the boy with him into the mountains. The Master asked, "Pang, how was our meeting yesterday compared to today?
The Layman replied, "If you can bring up yesterday's matter according to the Dharma, I will make it into a 'patriarchal eye' (zongyan). The Master said:
"Can the Eye of the School still accommodate Master Pang? The layman said, "I am within your eye. The Master said, "My eyes are narrow; where can you find a place to settle?
The layman said, "How can these eyes be narrow? How can this body be settled? The Master then desisted.
The layman said, "If you can provide another phrase, this dialogue will be complete. The Master remained silent.
The layman said, "Among all these, this one particular phrase is something no one can utter. Later, as the Master and Layman Pang were walking along, they came upon a pool of water.
The layman pointed at it and said, "Even with such a thing before us, you still cannot discern it. The Master replied, "Truly, it cannot be discerned. The layman said, "..."
He then scooped up water and splashed two handfuls onto the Master. The Master said, "Not so! Not so! The layman said, "It must be so! It must be so!
The Master then scooped up water and splashed three handfuls onto the layman. The Master said, "At this very moment, what can be done?
The layman said, "There is no external thing. The Master said, "Those who gain the advantage are few. The layman said, "Who is it that falls into disadvantage?"
In the third year of the Yuanhe era, he lay across the Tianjin Bridge. When the Imperial Resident, Lord Zheng, came out and rebuked him, he did not rise.

When the official asked the reason for this, the Master replied slowly, "I am a monk of no concern. The Resident was struck by his extraordinary character and offered him bundles of silk and two sets of robes, providing him with daily rations of rice and flour.
The people of Luoyang flocked to him in faith. In the spring of the fifteenth year, he addressed his disciples.
He said, "I am contemplating a place among the forests and springs where I may spend my final years. At that time, his disciple Qijing selected Nanxiang Danxia Mountain to construct a hermitage.
Within three years, seekers of the profound Way arrived until the assembly numbered over three hundred. He established a great monastery and ascended the hall, saying:
"You, all you people, must by all means protect this single spiritual essence. It cannot be fashioned or described by names. Furthermore—
I speak of whether one has attained realization or not. When I saw Shitou in the past, he too taught only that one must strictly protect oneself.
This matter is not something you can discuss in idle talk. Each of you has your own patch of ground;
what more is there to doubt regarding Zen? Is it something you can understand? How could there be a Buddha to be accomplished? As for the very word "Buddha," never...
"Delightful to hear! You should examine this for yourself: skillful means, compassion, joy, and equanimity are not obtained from without, nor do they reside within the mind.
Skillfulness is Mañjuśrī; expedient means is Samantabhadra. What more do you intend to pursue?"

Do not labor in vain seeking after things and fall into emptiness. Nowadays, students are in a state of constant clamor and agitation, all of them engaged in Zen meditation and inquiring about the Way.
Here in my place, there is no Way to be cultivated and no Dharma to be realized. Whether it be a single sip of drink or a single grain of food, each has its own allotted portion.
Do not harbor doubts. Everywhere, there are those who are like this. If you recognize Śākyamuni, he is just an old ordinary person.
You must examine this for yourself; do not let one blind man lead a crowd of blind men as they walk together into a fire pit.
It is like playing double-six in the dark at night—how can you avoid calamity? Be careful. A monk arrived to pay his respects at the foot of the mountain.
Upon seeing the Master, he asked, "Where has Mount Danxia gone? The Master pointed to the mountain and said, "In that dark blue expanse.
He asked, "Is this not it itself? The Master replied, "A true lion cub turns with a single nudge. He then questioned a monk.
"Where did you stay overnight? he asked. The monk replied, "I stayed overnight at the foot of the mountain. The Master said, "Where did you eat? The monk replied, "I ate at the foot of the mountain.
The Master said, "Does the person who gave you food to eat possess eyes or not? The monk was speechless. (Changqing asked Baofu, "One who gives food to another has a share in their gratitude;

why do you say they do not possess eyes? Baofu said, "Both the giver and the receiver are blind men. Changqing said, "If one exhausts their spiritual capacity (*ji*), would that still constitute blindness? Baofu said, "Tell me, am I blind?")

"Is that so? Xuangjue challenged him, saying, "Tell me, did Changqing understand Danxia’s meaning, or was he merely using his own family wealth? In the sixth month of the fourth year of the Changqing era, he addressed his disciples, saying:

He prepared a bath and said, "I wish to bathe before I depart. Thereupon, he donned a bamboo hat, took up his staff, and put on his sandals; with one foot still hanging down, it did not even reach the ground when he passed away.
His disciples erected a stupa for him, posthumously conferred upon him the title Chan Master Zhītōng, and named the stupa Miaojue.
A monk from Jiangling came to visit Chan Master Dachu (also known as Dacun) of Tanzhou. The Master asked, "When did you set out from Jiangling? The monk held up his sitting cloth (*kaṣāya*).
The Master said, "Thank you for coming from so far; go on down. The monk circled the meditation seat once and then departed.
The Master said, "If it were not for this, how could one know the true measure of your eyes? The monk clapped his hands and said, "It would kill me with grief!"

[The monk] said, "I have mistakenly judged the various quarters. The Master said, "You have grasped the principles of the Chan school very well. [The monk] related this to Danxia. Danxia said, "Regarding the Dharma-way of Dachuan, you have attained it;

however, here with me, it is not so. [The monk] asked, "I do not know how it is done here. Danxia said, "It is still three steps ahead of the great prefectures. The monk bowed. Danxia said, "Many have mistakenly judged the various quarters.
Dongshan said, "Were it not for Danxia, it would be difficult to distinguish jade from stone."
When Chan Master Baotong Dadian of Lingshan in Chaozhou first visited Shitou, Shitou asked, "Which of these is your mind?

The Master replied, "The one that perceives these words is it. Shitou then shouted at him and sent him out. After ten days had passed, the Master asked again, "Since the former was not it, apart from this, what else is the mind?
Shitou said, "Setting aside raising the eyebrows and blinking the eyes, bring forth your mind."
"Bring it here," the Master said. Xuedou replied, "There is no mind to bring. The Master said, "So there is originally a mind;
why do you say there is no mind? To say there is no mind is nothing but slander. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment.

On another day, while standing in attendance, Xuedou asked, "Are you a monk who studies Zen, or a monk who merely tramples through the prefectures and counties? The Master replied, "I am a monk who studies Zen. Xuedou asked, "What is Zen? The Master—
Yangshan said, "Raising the eyebrows and blinking the eyes. Dongshan said, "Setting aside raising the eyebrows and blinking the eyes, present your original face to me.
Yangshan said, "I request the Master to examine me, setting aside raising the eyebrows and blinking the eyes.
Dongshan said, "I have already set it aside. Yangshan said, "I have presented it. Dongshan said, "Since you have presented it, what do you think of my mind? Yangshan said, "It is no different."
The Head Monk said, "This does not concern you. The Master said, "Fundamentally there are no things. The Head Monk said, "You, too, have no things.

The Master said, "Since there are no things, that is the true thing. The Head Monk said, "The true thing cannot be grasped; such is the intent of your mind’s perception and measure. You must guard and uphold this most carefully.
After the Master took up residence, students gathered from the four directions. He ascended the hall and said: "Now, as for those who study the Way..."
One must recognize one's own original mind; only by manifesting the characteristics of this mind can one see the Way.

I have often seen people of the present age who merely recognize a raised eyebrow, a blink of an eye, a single word, or a moment of silence as a sudden seal of approval, taking these to be the essence of the mind. This is truly a failure to understand.
I shall now speak clearly for all of you; each of you must listen and receive it with attention.

Simply eliminate all false mental activities, conceptualizations, views, and measures, and that which remains is your true mind. This mind has no interaction whatsoever with external objects or with the state of maintaining silence and stillness.
This very mind is the Buddha; it does not require cultivation or refinement. Why is this? Because it responds to conditions and reflects accordingly with spontaneous clarity.
Coldly [the mind] acts of its own accord. If one exhaustively seeks the locus of this activity, it is utterly unfindable. To call this "wondrous function" is precisely the original mind;
it must be guarded and sustained with great care—it cannot be treated lightly. A monk asked, "When those within [this state] meet face-to-face, what is it like?
The Master said, "Already, they are not 'within'. The monk asked, "What then is it to be 'within'? The Master said, "Do not make such a question. [This concludes the section on] Han Wengong.

The official went to visit him one day and asked, "How old are you, Master? The Master held up his rosary and said, "Do you understand? The official replied, "I do not. The Master said, "One hundred and eight [beads] for day and night. The official did not comprehend this and returned home. On the following day he came again; arriving at the gate, he saw the Head Seat (Śrāmaṇera) and asked him about the meaning of the previous conversation. The Head Seat clicked his teeth three times. When the official saw the Master, he [repeated the same action]. The Master said, "You have understood. The official was greatly enlightened. He bowed and departed. Later, he composed a verse: "One hundred and eight beads, Day and night, revolving.

The Master holds them up; I click my teeth three times. If you wish to know the meaning, Look at the Master’s face. Upon seeing this verse, the Master sighed and said, "This man has truly attained the Way. The official later served as the Prefect of Huainan. One day, while traveling, he encountered the Master on the road. The official dismounted from his carriage and bowed. The Master said, "Prefect, why do you bow? The official replied, "Because I am a layman. The Master said, "Layman, why do you not bow? The official had no answer. The Master said, "You have been a monk for thirty years, yet you still do not understand the meaning of 'day and night, one hundred and eight.

The official was deeply ashamed. He returned to his residence and sent a messenger to invite the Master to come and stay. The Master accepted the invitation. After staying for some time, the official asked, "What is the meaning of the previous matter? The Master said, "It is like a person who has lost their way and wanders in confusion; they do not know where they are going. The official said, "I am still confused. The Master said, "If you wish to understand, you must first abandon all conceptualizations and attachments. The official bowed in gratitude. This story illustrates how the Master used the mundane to reveal the sacred, guiding the official toward the realization of the ultimate truth through the simple act of counting beads.

The official asked the same question as before. The Master also tapped his teeth three times. The official said, "So, it turns out the Buddha-dharma is not of two kinds. The Master asked, "What is your reasoning?
The official replied, "Just now, when I asked the Head Seat, he answered in exactly the same way. The Master then summoned the Head Seat and asked, "Was it you who answered in this manner?
The Seat replied, "It was. The Master immediately struck him and expelled him from the monastery. One day, Official Wen again addressed the Master.
The official said, "My duties as military governor are many and complex. Regarding the essential points of the Buddha-dharma, I beg the Master for a single word.

The Master remained silent for a long time. The official was at a loss. At that moment, Sanping was serving as attendant; he struck the meditation seat three times. The Master asked, "What is this? Sanping replied: [silence].
"First move it with concentration; afterwards, pull it out with wisdom. The Master then said, "The patriarchal style of our Preceptor is lofty and steep.
My disciple has found a point of entry through the side of the attendant. A monk asked, "The waves of the sea of suffering are deep; what shall serve as the boat or raft? The Master said:
He made a boat and raft out of wood and said, "In this way, one may cross over. The Master said, "The blind remain blind as before; the mute remain mute as before.
One day, while walking along the corridor with his itch-scratcher, he encountered a monk who came forward to pay his respects.
The Master struck him across the mouth with the itch-scratcher and asked, "Do you understand? The monk replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Old wild fox Dadian!"
He had never disappointed anyone.

Shitou asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Lingnan. Shitou said, "Has the one shop at the head of Dayu Ridge completed its work of merit yet?"

The Master said, "He has been accomplished for a long time; he simply lacks the 'dotting of the eyes' (the final realization). Daitō said, "Do you not wish for the dotting of the eyes? The Master replied, "I request it at once.
Daitō then lowered one foot. The Master prostrated himself. Daitō asked, "What principle have you perceived that you prostrate yourself?
The Master said, "According to what I have seen, it is like a single drop of snow upon a red-hot furnace. (Xuánjué said: Now tell me, how is this?)

The monk with a beard and eyes responded; the one without eyes also responded. If he had eyes, why [did he respond]? Please explain how he was "anointed in the eye. If he did not have eyes, it is said again: "He has been accomplished for a long time.

Do you grant permission for such a one? The Master said, "Meeting him is not meeting him; if you meet him, there must be something. The monk—

The Master then stepped back three paces. The monk, however, circled the meditation seat once. The monk said, "Not only is the eye of the school made clear, but the lineage of the teacher is also well-founded.
The Master then struck him three times and asked, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From the Stone Controlling Hermitage on Mount Jiuhua.

"What is it? he asked. [The Master] said, "He does not understand; you do not understand. He asked, "Where are the eyes of the Venerable Elder?
The Master said, "If the Hermitage Master had come in person, he would have had to receive a beating today as well.

He said, "Master, you see only the sharpness of the chisel’s tip; you do not see the keenness of the adze’s head. When Li Xingpo arrived, the Master asked, "Do you remember the events when we were in Jangzhou?
The old woman replied, "It would not be for you, Master, that I would not know them. The Master said, "Much is empty and little is real.
The old woman said, "What is there to hide? The Master said, "I pity that you are a woman; I let you go with your staff. The old woman said, [and departed].
"I shall never see any fault in the Venerable Elder," she said. The Master asked, "Where does the old monk’s fault lie?
The woman said, "The Master has no fault; how could I possibly have a fault? The Master asked, "What about one who has no fault?
The woman then raised her fist and said, "In this way, everything becomes a perversion. The Master said, "Truly, there is nowhere to hide. Seeing a monk, the Master seized him and said:
The Lion Cub was a member of the jackal clan. A monk made a gesture with his hand as if flicking a brow. The Master said, "Even so, you still lack the roar.
The monk seized the Master, who said, "You are particularly fond of employing this particular maneuver. The Master gave him a slap. The monk clapped his hands three times.
The Master asked, "If you see someone of like mind, would you be willing to act thus? The monk replied, "Ultimately, it does not depend on anyone else."
The Master made a gesture of twitching his eyebrows. The monk said, "You still lack a roar. The Master said, "I suspect it does not depend on anyone else.
Seeing the monk bowing in greeting, the Master said, "Every step is a place of your own realization; do you know this yet?"
The monk said, "I do not know. The Master asked, "If you knew, what could I possibly do for you? The monk bowed. The Master said, "I am not fit for you;
you are the one who is truly fine."
Chan Master Tianwang Daowu of Jingzhou was the son of the Zhang family of Dongyang in Wuzhou. His divine countenance was exceptionally outstanding, and he possessed innate wisdom from childhood.

At the age of fourteen, he earnestly sought to leave the household life, but his parents would not permit it. He consequently reduced his intake of food and drink, eating only once a day until his physical form became emaciated and haggard.
His parents, having no other choice, finally granted him permission; he then relied upon a virtuous master in Mingzhou.
He shaved his head and beard. At twenty-five, he went to Zhulin Monastery in Hangzhou to receive full ordination and diligently cultivated the pure conduct (*brahmacarya*).
He was renowned for his courage; even amidst wind, rain, darkness, or night, he would sit in meditation among burial mounds with body and mind tranquil, free from all fear.

One day, while traveling to Yuhang, he first visited Guoyi of Mount Jing, where he received the teachings of the Mind-Dharma. He served him with devotion for five years, after which he went to study under Mazu.
Reprinting the previous commentary: The Dharma has no divergent teachings; having relied [upon his master] for two summer retreats, he went to visit Shitou and asked:
"Setting aside concentration and wisdom, by what dharma do you instruct people? Shitou said: "In my place here, there are no servants—what is there to set aside?
[The monk] asked: "How can one understand this? Shitou said: "Can you grasp empty space? [The monk] said: "If that is so, then it is not..."
"From this day forward," [the Master] said. The Head asked, "I do not know at what time or from which direction you have come.

He replied, "Daowu is not a person from that direction. The Head said, "I knew well enough where you had come from. He asked, "Why does the Master falsely accuse me with stolen goods? The Head said, "Your very body is right here.
He asked, "Even though it is so, how ultimately will you instruct those who come after?"

Tou said, "Tell me, who is the 'person of the future'? At this, the Master attained sudden enlightenment; he completely exhausted his former grasping at realization that had arisen beneath the words of the two previous masters.
Later, he settled at Mount Ziling in Dangyang, Jingzhou, where disciples followed one after another in endless succession.
The men and women of the capital flocked there like an echo responding to the wind. At that time, the head monk of Congye Temple reported the situation to Master Lian, who welcomed him into the city.
To the left of the prefecture was Tiantang Temple, a renowned monastery that had been destroyed by fire.
Its presiding monk, Lingjian, planned to restore it and said, "If we can obtain Master Wuzhu as the spiritual leader for this transformation, he will surely bring us blessings."
Thereupon, he went secretly in the middle of the night to offer a sorrowful plea, arriving by means of a shoulder-litter.

At that time, the Governor of Jiangling, the Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Lord Pei, bowed his head and inquired about the Dharma with the utmost courtesy and diligence. The Master had never before welcomed or seen off guests; regardless of their rank, whether noble or humble, he would simply have them sit and bow to them.
Lord Pei’s devotion increased all the more, and from this, the Dharma path at Shitou flourished. A monk asked: "How is it?"

"This is a profound and subtle teaching," [the student] said. The Master replied, "Do not say that I am skilled at explaining the Buddha-dharma. The student asked, "What can be done about the doubts and stagnations of this student?
The Master said, "Why do you not ask the old monk? The student replied, "I have already asked just now. The Master said, "Go; this is not where you should remain.
In the fourth month of the Dinghai year of the Yuanhe era, the Master manifested illness and instructed his disciples to announce his passing in advance.

The Master said, "I am not the Buddhas. [The monk] said, "Since you are not the Buddhas, why do you nevertheless establish 'my Way'?
The Master said, "Just now I temporarily called him in; now I have sent him out. [The monk] asked, "Why did you send him out?"

[The monk] went out. The Master said, "If you had not been sent out, dust would have arisen in your eyes. [The monk] asked, "Since one cannot find it anywhere, is this not being a sage? The Master said, "What kind of sage is that? [The monk] said, "When Niu-tou had not yet seen the Fourth Patriarch, was he not a sage? The Master said, "He was a sage, but he was not a Buddha. The monk asked, "Why was he not a Buddha? The Master replied, "Because he had not yet attained the Way. The monk asked, "How can one attain the Way? The Master said, "If you do not seek the Way, you will naturally attain it. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'not seeking'? The Master said, "If you do not seek, you will not encounter it; if you do not encounter it, you will not realize it; if you do not realize it, you will not see it; if you do not see it, you will not know it; if you do not know it, you will not understand it; if you do not understand it, you will not be enlightened; if you are not enlightened, you will not be liberated; if you are not liberated, you will not be free from birth and death; if you are not free from birth and death, you will not transcend the three realms; if you do not transcend the three realms, you will not escape the cycle of suffering. Therefore, you must cut off all seeking and let go of all thoughts. When you reach the point where there is no thought, there is no seeking; when there is no seeking, there is no encountering; when there is no encountering, there is no realizing; when there is no realizing, there is no seeing; when there is no seeing, there is no knowing; when there is no knowing, there is no understanding; when there is no understanding, there is enlightenment; when there is enlightenment, there is liberation; when there is liberation, there is freedom from birth and death; when there is freedom from birth and death, you transcend the three realms; when you transcend the three realms, you escape the cycle of suffering. This is called attaining the Way. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'attaining the Way'? The Master said, "Attaining the Way means attaining the nature of the Way; attaining the nature of the Way means attaining the body of the Way; attaining the body of the Way means attaining the mind of the Way; attaining the mind of the Way means attaining the wisdom of the Way; attaining the wisdom of the Way means attaining the liberation of the Way; attaining the liberation of the Way means attaining the nirvana of the Way; attaining the nirvana of the Way means attaining the ultimate cessation of all suffering. The monk asked, "What is the ultimate cessation of all suffering? The Master said, "It is the state where there is no subject and no object, no self and no other, no gain and no loss, no right and no wrong, no birth and no death, no coming and no going—this is the ultimate cessation of all suffering. The monk bowed and withdrew. The Master said, "This is what is meant by 'the Way is not far, but people themselves create distance. The monk asked, "What is meant by 'people themselves create distance'? The Master said, "Because they give rise to thoughts and seek outside themselves, they create distance. The Master said, "By realizing that thoughts are originally empty and non-existent, one naturally stops giving rise to them. The monk asked, "How can one cease seeking outside? The Master said, "By realizing that the Way is within oneself and not elsewhere, one naturally ceases seeking. The Master said, "By observing that thoughts arise and pass away like clouds and mist, having no fixed substance, one realizes they are originally empty and non-existent. The monk asked, "How does one realize that the Way is within oneself and not elsewhere? The Master said, "By observing that the nature of the Way is inherently complete and perfect, lacking nothing, one realizes it is within oneself and not elsewhere. The monk asked, "If the nature of the Way is inherently complete and perfect, why do sentient beings suffer in birth and death? The monk asked, "How can one suddenly turn back and recognize one's own original nature? The Master said, "By casting off all delusions and attachments, and by relying on the teachings of a true master to receive guidance, one can suddenly turn back and recognize one's own original nature. The monk asked, "What is the function of a true master? The Master said, "A true master uses various skillful means to guide students, enabling them to cut off delusions and realize the Way. This is the function of a true master. The monk asked, "How does one cut off delusions? The Master said, "By realizing that delusions are originally empty and non-existent, one cuts them off. The monk asked, "How does one realize the Way? The Master said, "By realizing that the Way is originally complete and perfect, one realizes it. The monk asked, "What is the difference between cutting off delusions and realizing the Way? The Master said, "Cutting off delusions is the beginning; realizing the Way is the end. When delusions are cut off, the Way is realized. There is no difference between them. The monk asked, "What is the ultimate goal of practice? The Master said, "The ultimate goal of practice is to return to the source and restore the original nature, to transcend all phenomena and dwell in the realm of the unconditioned. This is the ultimate goal of practice. The monk asked, "How does one dwell in the realm of the unconditioned? The Master said, "By letting go of all mental activities and entering a state of profound stillness and silence, one dwells in the realm of the unconditioned. The monk asked, "What is the state of profound stillness and silence? The Master said, "It is a state where the mind is like empty space, without thought or perception, without grasping or rejecting, without coming or going—this is the state of profound stillness and silence. The monk asked, "Is this state of profound stillness and silence the same as the state of a Buddha? The Master said, "It is the same as the state of a Buddha, but it is not yet the state of a Buddha. It is the state of a Bodhisattva who has reached the final stage of practice. Only when one has fully realized the nature of the Way and attained the great awakening can one be called a Buddha. The monk asked, "What is the great awakening? The Master said, "The great awakening is the realization that the nature of the Way is identical to the nature of all sentient beings, that there is no distinction between self and others, and that all phenomena are ultimately empty and quiescent. This is the great awakening. The monk asked, "After attaining the great awakening, what should one do? The Master said, "After attaining the great awakening, one should return to the world to benefit sentient beings, using various skillful means to lead them to the Way. This is the duty of a Bodhisattva. The monk asked, "How does one benefit sentient beings? The Master said, "One benefits sentient beings by teaching them according to their capacities, by removing their afflictions, and by guiding them toward liberation. The Master said, "The essence of the teachings is the Dharma-nature, which is eternal, immutable, and beyond words.
