The Master said, "It is like biting a hard stone. The monk asked, "What is the single burner of incense in the ancient temple? The Master said, "No one has smelled it for generations. The monk asked, "As for those who smell it, how is that?
The Master said, "It does not reach any of the six sense faculties. The monk asked, "I have long heard of Jiumi..."
[The monk] asked, "Having arrived here, why do you not save those who are deluded? The Master said, "Ācārya, you do not know how to save those who are deluded.
A monk asked Zen Master Wenshu of Hunan, "Why was it that Sengyao could not capture the true likeness of Master Zhigong?
The Master said, "Not only Sengyao; even Zhigong himself could not capture his own likeness. The monk asked, "Why could Zhigong not capture his own likeness?"
The Master said, "The colors and patterns have not been brought. [The monk] asked, "Has the Master, too, failed to capture them?
The Master said, "I, too, have failed to capture them. [The monk] asked, "Why has the Master failed to capture them? The Master said, "It does not borrow its color from me."
[The student] asked, "How can I depict this? [The Master] said, "One does not settle for what is tight.
[The student] asked, "What is it like to be within the secret chamber? The Master said, "One does not sit atop the ox of form."
When Chan Master Shizhu of Fengxiang Prefecture was traveling on pilgrimage, he arrived at Dongshan.
At that time, Master Qian gave this instruction: "There are four kinds of people: one who has surpassed the Buddhas and patriarchs in speech but cannot take a single step;
one who has surpassed the Buddhas and patriarchs in practice but cannot utter a single word; one who can both speak and practice; and one who can neither speak nor practice."

"Who, then, is that person? The Master stepped forward from the assembly and said: "The one who has surpassed the Buddhas and Patriarchs in speech but cannot practice it—this is simply because he lacks a tongue and is not permitted to act.
The one who has surpassed the Buddhas and Patriarchs in practice but cannot speak a single word about it—this is simply because he lacks feet and is not permitted to speak.
The one who can both speak and practice—it is simply that the container and its lid fit each other perfectly."
When someone says that one cannot speak and cannot act, it is like seeking life by cutting off one's own breath; this is like a child born of a barren woman wearing a cangue and shackles.
Yunshan asked, "What about your own portion, Master? The Master said, "In my own portion, all is encompassed and penetrating;
it stands out clearly and is manifest. Yunshan asked, "As for Minggong Xiù on the sea, what about him? The Master said, "Two illusory people meeting."
Clapping his hands, he laughed "he-he.
Chan Master Cunsou of Datong Monastery on Qiyanshan in Hezhong Prefecture initially lectured on the sutras and śāstras;
later, in the hall of Shishuang, he forgot the trap (the means). After he took up residence there, a monk asked, "What is the place where you, Master, gained strength? The Master said, "No."
Occupying the position of Master, how could he sit upon a white ox-cart? A monk asked, "What is it like before the lotus has emerged from the water?
The Master said, "Are you not asking about the lotus after it has emerged? The monk was speechless. The Master rarely spoke in his daily life, responding only when questioned.
He was posthumously titled Chan Master Zhenji.
Chan Master Xuantai of Nanyue was profound, serene, and spoke little. He never wore silk or fine fabrics; thus, he was known at the time as "Tai the Coarse-Robed One" (Taibunuo).
When he first met Deshan, he ascended the Dharma hall. Later, he visited Shishuang and subsequently entered his room [as a disciple].
For twenty years, he served as the scribe, befriending Guanxiu and Qiji. Afterwards, he resided at a hermitage called Jingangtai, where he vowed never to establish a formal gate for disciples.

His disciples from all quarters who came to him for instruction all treated him with the etiquette due to a friend. He once observed that Mount Heng was being severely damaged by local mountaineers who practiced slash-and-burn agriculture (*shaya*), which caused great harm.

He therefore composed the "Ballad of the Slash-and-Burn Mountain" (*Shayanshao*), which says: "Children of the slash-and-burn mountain, children of the slash-and-burn mountain, you have no sense at all.
Year after year you hew down the peaks of the green mountains. Among them, the colors of Mount Heng are the most beautiful—its cypress and pine trees..."
The sharp axe destroys the upright branches; the numinous birds and wild cranes have no place to rely. White clouds retreat as blue smoke flies;

monkeys and apes find their paths cut off as they emerge from the cliffs. The roots of *zhi* and *shu* herbs are lost, while the weeds grow lush. Year after year, once felled, they are again cleared away.
"A thousand autumns ultimately cannot restore the original state. It was further said: "This year’s planting was not much; next year they shall cut down even more on the slopes facing the sun.
When the situation within the imperial domain reached such a state, no one knew how to address this principle. The news spread far and wide until it reached the Nine Layers [of the Palace].
An imperial edict was issued to prohibit the practice, so that the monasteries within Mount Tai were no longer subjected to spreading fires; this was due to the Master's efforts.

As he was about to manifest his passing into extinction, he summoned a monk and ordered him to prepare firewood. He left behind this verse: "This year I am sixty-five; The four elements are about to depart from their lord.
The Way is of itself profound and mysterious; Within it, there is neither Buddha nor Patriarch. There is no need for shaving the head, Nor is there any need for bathing.
A single mass of fierce fire— Ten thousand times sufficient, a hundred thousand times enough. He sat upright with one leg pendant and passed away. His remains were collected after cremation.

The monk asked, "And after he appeared? The Master said, "A golden crow turns its back to the sun. [The Master] said, "This cannot be fathomed by ordinary sentiment."
"How is it at this time? The Master asked. Fengxue replied, "The wit of the tongueless child is exhausted. Fengxue went to visit the Master.

The Master asked, "When the stone horn pierces the path through the clouds, what is your intention as you carry your staff? Fengxue said, "Red clouds enshroud the jade elephant; the peaks embrace the mountains while the light shines upon the streams and sources.
The Master said, "You have come along with me. Fengxue said, "Even the Master must lower his voice. The Master said, "Sit for a moment and drink some tea."
Chan Master Pumen of Longhu in Shaowu Commandery was the crown prince of Emperor Xizong of the Tang dynasty. From childhood he abstained from meat;
as an adult, he had no interest in governing the world. Although Emperor Xizong doted on him, he employed every means to mold and direct him, yet in the end could not change his mind.

At the beginning of the Zhonghe era, when Emperor Xizong fled to Shu, the Master cut off his hair and wandered away, with no one knowing his whereabouts. He went to visit Shishuang and asked: "The Patriarch..."
The Master asked about the matters of the separate transmission: "Would you be willing to entrust them to me? Baoshuang said, "Do not slander the Patriarchs.

The Master said, "The principles of the world are grand and flourishing; how could they be something fabricated? Baoshuang said, "Is this not a reality? The Master asked, "What is your own understanding of this?"
Fangshuang said, "Wait until the mountain over the altar nods its head, and I shall speak to you. At these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment. He took his leave and traveled to Shaowu.
Outside the city, he saw a mountain that was lush, profound, and beautiful; he cleared away the weeds and reached a place where smoke was rising, where a practitioner of asceticism resided.
Upon seeing the Master arrive, the practitioner said, "The Master of the Dharma shall flourish here," and after bowing deeply, he departed. The Master...
After he had lived there for over ten years, one day an old man came to pay his respects. The Master asked, "Where do you dwell? What do you seek by coming here?
The old man replied, "I dwell on this mountain; however, I am not a human, but a dragon. Because I have failed in my duty regarding the rain, the heavens have sentenced me to death.
I pray that you will grant me your protection. The Master said, "You have offended the Supreme Deity; what power do I have to exert on your behalf?"
Although he could easily change his form, the old man suddenly vanished from where he was. Looking beside him, [the Master] saw a small snake crawling into his sleeve.
At dusk, thunder and lightning shook the mountains as wind and rain broke out simultaneously; yet the Master sat upright and remained unshaken.
When dawn came and the weather cleared, the snake slipped out of his sleeve, fell to the ground, and departed. After a short while, the old man bowed and wept, saying: "Were it not for Your Great..."
The Master was compassionate. Thinking that this mountain had been defiled by blood and filth, he considered how he might repay such kindness.
He then hollowed out a space beneath a cliff to create a spring, saying, "This spring shall serve as a provision for the many assemblies of the future. It is now known as Longhu (Dragon Lake).

When the local people heard of these events, they contributed both wealth and labor to build a monastery together. Monks flocked there like clouds; the Master propagated his teachings for over thirty years.

As he approached the time of his passing, he struck the bell to assemble the community and spoke this verse: "I fled the hardships of the world to leave the household life; The Master pointed out for me a place of rest.
I have dwelt on this mountain and gathered the assembly for thirty years; Ordinarily, I did not wish to bestow this lightly.
Today I shall explain it clearly to you; When I close my eyes, listen all together. He passed away peacefully and was interred at his home mountain.
He was posthumously titled Chan Master Yuanguo.
The scholar Zhang Zhuo, having been directed by the Great Master Chan Yue to visit Shishuang, was asked by Shishuang, "What is your surname, scholar?

He replied, "My surname is Zhang and my name is Zhuo. Shishuang said, "Even 'cleverness' (qiao) cannot be found; from where does 'clumsiness' (zhuo) come? At these words, the official suddenly attained realization.
He then presented this verse: "Radiant, silent illumination pervades as many grains of sand as there are in the Ganges; Ordinary beings and sages, all living creatures, are my own family.
When not a single thought arises, the entire body is fully revealed; As soon as the six sense organs stir, they are shrouded by clouds. To sever afflictions is to increase one's illness once more;
To strive toward True Suchness is likewise a deviation. Accord with worldly conditions without hindrance; Nirvana and birth-and-death are equal to flowers in the sky."
Chan Master Yuan’an of Mount Luopu in Lǐzhōu was a dharma heir of Chan Master Jiashan Hui. A native of Línyóu in Fèngxiáng, he left home at the age of seven and received full ordination.
He mastered the sutras and śāstras and sought the Way from Linji, subsequently serving as his attendant. Linji once praised him before the assembly, saying: "Lin..."
"A single arrow beneath Jie’s gate—who would dare face its point? Having received this seal of approval, the Master considered himself sufficient.
One day, while standing in attendance, a presiding lecturer visited Jie. Jie asked:

"Suppose there is one person who has attained clarity through the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings, and another person who has not attained clarity through the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings. Now tell me, what of these two people?"
"Are they the same or different? The Master said, "If you can understand it, they are the same; if you cannot understand it, they are different.
The Teacher said, "What kind of place is this to speak of 'same' or 'different'? Jie looked at the Teacher and said, "And what about you? The Teacher then gave a shout.
Ji sent the Master off on his way back and asked him, "Were you not the one who just now shouted at the old monk?
The Master replied, "Yes. Ji then struck him. Later, when the Master took his leave of Ji, Ji asked, "Where are you going? The Master said, "I am going to the South.
Ji drew a line with his staff and said, "If you can pass over this, then go. The Master then shouted. Ji struck him again. The Master then... [acted].
He paid his respects and departed. The next day, Linji ascended the hall and said, "In the gate of Linji, there is a red-tailed carp;
shaking its head and wagging its tail, it has gone south. I know not in whose pickle jar it will be drowned.

After the Master had finished his travels, he went directly to Jia Shan to establish a hermitage, remaining there for a year without visiting Jia Shan. Jia Shan then composed a letter and dispatched a monk to deliver it.
The Master received him and sat back down. He extended his hand again, seeking [the letter], but the monk had no reply. The Master struck him and said, "Go back and report this to the Abbot.
When the monk returned and reported it, Mount [Shishuang] said, "If this monk had opened the letter, he would certainly have come within three days."
"If you do not open this book, this person cannot be saved. The Master indeed arrived three days later. Upon seeing Jia Shan, he did not prostrate;
instead, he stood facing him with his hands joined at his chest. Jia Shan said, "A rooster nesting in a phoenix's nest is not of the same kind;
get out! The Master said, "I have come from afar to pay my respects; I beg the Master for a single reception. Jia Shan said, "Before my eyes there is no *śrāmaṇera*. In this place...
"No old monk," the Master said, and he gave a shout. Xishan said, "Stop, stop! Do not be so hasty and reckless. The clouds and moon are the same; the streams and mountains are each different.
It is not that you cannot cut off the tongues of all people under heaven, but how can you, O *śrāmaṇera*, make a tongueless person speak?
The Master paused in thought, and Xishan struck him. From this, he took the teaching to heart. (Xinghua spoke on his behalf: "Just know how to become a Buddha; do not worry about sentient beings. 1.

Ri asked Shanshan, "How does one realize the place where neither Buddha nor Māra reaches? Shanshan said, "The candle illuminates the images for a thousand li; yet in the dark room, the old monk is lost.
He asked again, "When the morning sun has already risen and the night moon has not yet appeared, what then?

Shanshan said, "The dragon holds the pearl in its mouth; the swimming fish pay it no heed. As Shanshan was about to pass away, he uttered this final word: "Look, look! This is the branch of the Stonehead lineage."
[The mountain] was immediately extinguished. The Master said, "Not so. The Mountain asked, "Why? The Master said, "In his own home, he has his own green mountains.
The Mountain said, "If it is truly thus, then our lineage shall not fall. When Jia Shan passed away, the Master arrived at Cenyang and encountered an old friend.
While discussing matters concerning Wuling, the friend asked, "In the blink of an eye several years have passed; where did you flee from the turmoil? The Master [replied].
[The Master] said: "It is right here in the midst of the marketplace. [The questioner] asked: "Why not go to a place where there are no people? The Master said:

"What difficulty is there in a place where there are no people? [The questioner] asked: "How can one escape within the marketplace? The Master said: "Though one is in the midst of the marketplace, for the time being people do not recognize [the truth];

therefore, others cannot fathom it. He asked again: "Buddha after Buddha correspond with one another; Patriarch after Patriarch transmits to one another. Why do they not bestow [this teaching] upon each other?"
"How is it when the music ends? The Master said, "The rustic elder at the front gate does not speak of court affairs. The monk asked, "What matters should he discuss?

The Master said, "Unless one meets someone else, I will never open my fist. The monk asked, "If there is someone who has not come from the court, would you still discuss the realization upon meeting him?
The Master said, "A mechanism beyond measure is merely a vain matter for the eyes to witness. The Master subsequently went to Fengyang.

At Mount Luopu, he established a dwelling as a place for leisurely practice; later, he moved to Su Creek in Langzhou. Monks from all quarters flocked to him like surging waves. Entering the hall, he said:
"The final phrase is where one first arrives at the secure barrier; it locks off the vital passageway, allowing neither ordinary person nor sage to pass."
Ordinarily, I tell people: "Let the world below rejoice as it pleases; I alone am unwilling to comply.

If one wishes to know the superior stream of practitioners, they do not take the words and teachings of the Buddhas and Patriarchs and paste them upon their foreheads—like a tortoise carrying a map, which only brings about the omen of its own destruction, or a phoenix entangled in a golden net, wondering when it will soar into the mists of heaven. One must, directly, clarify the essence beyond the literal meaning.
Do not seek the standard within words. Therefore, even a stone man whose mechanism resembles yours can sing the *bāgē*;

if you were like that stone man, you would surely respond to the *xuěqǔ*. The single path pointed out by the Southern Master is known to be superficial by the wise. A monk asked: "When one sees it instantly upon a flash, what then?
The Master said: "The morning star divides the colors of dawn; how does it compare to the brilliance of the sun? He asked again: "In such a case..."

"If one does not establish oneself when coming this way, and does not extinguish oneself when going that way, what then? The Master said: "The wood-seller values his firewood; the silk-clad man considers himself light. A questioner asked:
"It is said that making offerings to hundreds of thousands of Buddhas is not as good as making offerings to a single mindless practitioner (*amanojña*).
I do not yet understand: what fault do the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas have, and what virtue does the mindless practitioner possess? The Master said: "One..."
"A single white cloud stretches across the mouth of the valley; how many returning birds have utterly lost their nests? "Question: What is it like when the sun has not yet risen? The Master said:
"When the waters of the vast ocean are exhausted, the dragon still hides; when the clouds rise to the azure heavens, the phoenix still flies.

"Question: What is the matter of original nature? The Master said: "A single grain remains in the wild field; though the seedlings are not weeded, they flourish of themselves. [The student] asked: "If they are not weeded..."

"Do not let it be buried by the grass; otherwise, there will be nothing left. The Master said, "The flesh and bones differ from common weeds; even tares and darnel cannot ultimately hide them. Question:
"What is it like for one who does not harm the life-force of things? The Master said, "Flowers bloom in the eyes and mountain shadows shift;

the deluded wander in vain. Question: "What is it like when one does not speak of the past or the present? The Master said, "The numinous tortoise has no divination marks; the empty shell need not be drilled. [The student] said: "..."
"But what can one do with an empty shell? The Master said, "When seeing is exhausted, there is no locus for mental activity; therein, neither the heterodox nor the orthodox can be established.

[The student] said, "If that is so, then there is no place of rest. The Master said, "The profound manifestation begins before form appears; vain effort is exhausted by the application of ornamentation."

Question: "If the dragon’s mechanism does not emit mist, how can there be the benefit of nourishment? The Master said: "The Way is fundamentally nameless; it possesses neither light nor darkness. Question:
"As for that matter which is not caught by light or darkness, how is it? The Master said: "It is easy to bring up within words, but difficult to grasp beyond the mind. Question:
"When one is not born into the family of the Tathāgata and does not sit upon the Lotus King throne, what is it like? The Master said: "Tell me."
“How heavy is the brazier? [The monk] asked, “Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different? The Master said, “In the lion’s den there are no other beasts;
where the elephant king walks, the tracks of foxes are severed. [The monk] asked, “When they are all brought forth at once, what then? The Master said, “...”
Presenting the raw jade without knowing the occasion is merely a vain effort that invites having one's feet cut off. He asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Jingnan.
The Master said, "If there is a person who goes in such a manner, do you encounter him? The monk said, "I do not encounter him. The Master said, "Why do you not encounter him?

The monk said, "If I were to encounter him, my head would shatter into pieces. The Master said, "The three-inch tongue of this *śrāmaṇera* is very well-guarded. Yunmen saw [this story] while in Jiangxi.
The monk then asked, "Are these words still current? He replied, "They are. The Gatekeeper said, "Luopu has retreated three thousand li.
[The monk] asked, "How is it when one acts in the inconceivable? The Master said, "The green mountains constantly lift their feet; the white sun does not shift its wheels."
Question: "What is the matter of standing alone in a withered and desolate field? The Master said: "A heron leaning against a snow nest may still be distinguished;
a crow alighting on black lacquer is difficult to discern. Question: "What is the guest within the host? The Master said: "Constantly asking the way when meeting people."
The Venerable One remained lost in long-standing confusion. He asked, "What is it like when both guest and host are raised together?

The Master said, "A withered tree has no horizontal branches; a bird finds it difficult to set foot upon it. He asked, "How is it when one is perpetually in a state of dim obscurity? The Master said, "A jewel is cast into a mixture of sand."
The Master said, "Consciousness is naturally distinct. [The student] said, "If that is so, then even when extending one's hand, one does not encounter the Teacher.

The Master said, "Do not mistake the cry of a crane for the song of a nightingale. [The student] asked, "Everyone understands the three dots of the character *yuan* (round); what is the 'house style' of Luopu like?"
The Master said: "A single stroke of thunder, and the sound of the cloth drum vanishes. [The student] asked: "What is it like when it is exactly midday?
The Master said: "Midday still lacks half; only when the sun sets does it become full. If you wish to understand the meaning within this, place the head on the tail of the ox."
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "The rustling bamboo by the window does not grow cold of its own accord despite the frost.
As the monk was about to offer further words, the Master said, "I hear only the sound of the wind striking it; how many thousand stalks must there be?

Ascending the hall, he said, "Sun Bin has closed his shop, yet there is still a diviner who comes forward. A monk said, "I ask the Master to perform a divination for me. The Master said, "In your house..."
When the Patriarch died, the monk had no reply. (Fayan, acting on his behalf, clapped his hands three times. [The monk] asked: "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey?

The Master struck the meditation seat with his whisk and said: "Do you understand? He replied: "I do not understand. The Master said: "A sudden peal of thunder startles the universe; yet the shrimp at the bottom of the well does not lift its head.
[The monk] asked: "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said: "Snow covers the solitary peak."
"Not white. "Both grow like stone bamboo; the bamboo must sprout. "Is it true that the Dharma-body is unconditioned and does not fall into any numerical categories?
The Master said, "It would be better to cherish your eyebrows. "How can one avoid this fault?

The Master said, "A clay tortoise may last for a thousand years, yet it will never understand how to follow the clouds and cranes. "It is truly as if even Sun Bin were subjected to emasculation. The Master said, "No."
"A bull with its nostrils pierced—what way is there to resist it? The monk then let out a bellow like a cow. The Master said, "This beast! The monk then gave a shout.
The Master said, 'Tucking the tail while baring the teeth—this is still not the work of a true master. He asked: 'If one lets go at the edge of a ten-thousand-fathom precipice, what then?'"
"How does one avoid being lost at the moment of death? The Master said, "Mount Sumeru tied with a lotus fiber. The monk asked, "What kind of realm is that?
The Master said, "The heart of the upturned lotus atop the flagpole of the world-system. The monk said, "If so, then one proceeds in profound stillness and clarity.
The Master said, "Turning the body once more upon the summit of Mount Sumeru. The monk said, "If so, then one proceeds with intense urgency and earnestness."

"It is like a melody faintly heard, barely worth listening to, yet it is blown by the wind into another tune. A monk asked: "That which neither Buddha nor Mara reaches..."

"How can one discern the locus? The Master said, "Yajñadatta’s head was not lost; it was his failure to recognize it in the mirror. "Question: What is the means to rescue oneself from birth and death?
The Master said, "Holding onto water to prolong life by chance, one does not hear the wondrous celestial music. "Question: From what do the four great elements arise?
The Master said, "The clear water is without waves; bubbles are stirred up by the wind. [The questioner] asked, "When the bubbles subside and return to the water..."
"How is it? The Master said, "Neither turbid nor muddy; fish and dragons leap as they please. "Question: How can one transcend birth and death?
The Master said, "In a single thought, forget all artifice; the Great Void is without blemish. "Question: What is the Way? The Master said, "To maintain artifice is to remain stuck in traces;
to remove the stump, and the path is open. "Question: What is that which cannot be contained within the Great Canon of Teachings? The Master said—

Departing, he boards a boat to cross the five lakes. Raising the oar, the stars and moon vanish; pausing the rowing pole, the sun’s orb stands solitary. Unmooring the cables, he leaves the shore of error;

Question: "Movement is the sprout of the Dharma King; stillness is the root of the Dharma King. I do not ask about the root and the sprout; what is the Dharma King? The Master raises his whisk.
The Master said, "This is still merely the sprout of the Dharma King. The teacher said, "If the dragon does not emerge from its cave, who can do anything about it?
An attendant said to the teacher, "Dharma Master Zhao has composed the *Four Treatises*, which are truly extraordinary.

The teacher said, "Master Zhao is indeed extraordinary; however, he has nonetheless failed to see the Patriarchs. The attendant was speechless. (Fadeng spoke on his behalf, saying: "Where, O Monk, is [the Patriarch]? Yunju Xi said: "Where is Master Zhao?")
"It is not seen where the Patriarch resides; is it that he has so many words? It is also said: 'Master Zhao had how many words? Question: "What is the path of the living mechanism?
The Master said: "Striking the void produces a sound; striking wood produces no sound. The Master’s dharma teachings spread throughout all quarters like two mountains opening wide.

In the eighth month of the first year of the Guanghua era, he instructed his attendants, saying: "In the way of renunciation, one does not retain superfluous possessions. This is the time for sowing seeds."
One must certainly practice economy and reduction. All matters concerning construction and maintenance shall be entirely suspended. Time flows swiftly, and the Great Way is profound and mysterious;

Chan Master Yuelun of Huangshan in Fuzhou was the son of the Xu family of Fudang. Initially, he visited Sanfeng, but their karmic conditions did not harmonize.
Later, hearing that Master Laishan was flourishing there with great transformation, he went to call upon him. Laishan asked, "What is your name? The Master replied, "Yuelun."
Sansheng drew a circle and said, "How does this compare to that? The Master said, "If you speak such words, Master, there will be many in all quarters who will not accept them.
Sansheng asked, "What do you say, Dharma-heir? The Master replied, "Do you see the lunar disc?"
Mount [Shan] said, "If you speak thus, there are many people here who do not approve of those from other quarters.
The Master then submitted himself to his guidance and began to inquire. One day, Jia Shan called out in a loud voice, "Where are you from? The Master replied, "I am a man from Min.
Jia Shan asked, "Do you recognize this old monk? The Master replied, "Does the Abbot recognize this student? Jia Shan said, "No."
"However, you must first repay this old monk for the price of his straw sandals; only then will I repay you for the price of Luling rice.
The Master said, "If that is so, then I do not know the Master, nor do I yet understand what the price of Luling rice is. Deshan said, "A true lion cub indeed knows how to roar.

Shan ascended the hall and said: "The Patriarch came from the West specifically to sing this matter.

It is simply that people do not realize it, but instead rush outward in search of it—seeking pearls by casting themselves into the waters of the Red River, or searching for jade at Mount Jing. Therefore it is said: 'That which enters through the gate is not the family treasure.

"The stone ox frequently spits forth mist through the three springs; the wooden horse’s neighing fills the roads. Question: "How can one see one's original face?
The Master said: "There is no need to hang up a stone mirror; when dawn breaks, the rooster crows of itself. Question: "As for the One Vehicle of the Patriarchal School..."

The student requested the Master to deliberate upon this phrase. The Master said: "Huangfeng is uniquely liberated beyond all things; as the years pass and months go by, it is cold and piercing. The student asked:

The Master replied, "Monkeys and birds cry out through ancient times; emerald hues are shrouded in thin mist. The monk asked, "What is the essence within that realm?"

Yin replied, "I dare not say so. The Master asked, "How many mouths do you have? He replied, "My whole body is it. The Master asked, "Where do you usually defecate?
He replied, "I defecate in the mouth of Shaozhou. The Master said, "That works if there is a mouth of Shaozhou; but what if there is no mouth of Shaozhou?"
"Where do you intend to defecate? Because [Zhaozhou] was speechless, the Master struck him. Layman Zun Bunan went to visit the Master.

They met at the foot of the mountain, and Layman Zun asked, "To which place does the road to Shao Mountain lead? The Master pointed his finger and said, "It goes toward the green, dark expanse of Muna.
Layman Zun stepped forward, seized him, and said, "I have long heard of Shao Mountain; is it truly as such? The Master said:
"It is so. What business do you have with me, Preceptor? Zun said, "I intend to ask a question; will you answer it, Master?
The Master said, "Look at you—you are not made of *jintaya* (the material of divine arrows); how could you draw your bow to shoot Wei-chi?
Zun said, "The phoenix flies straight into the misty heights; who fears the wild sparrows in the woods? The Master said, "The painted drum before the hall is for you to strike as you please."

His life came to an end. He never failed to meet people with his full presence. In the first month of the first year of the Dàshùn era of the Táng dynasty, he initially announced to the assembly:

"I originally pledged to remain here for ten years; now that my work of transformation is complete, I shall depart immediately. After the midday meal, he struck the bell, sat upright, and passed away.

The Master said, "You, Reverend, see only one peak; you do not see the nine peaks. The monk asked, "What are the nine peaks?
The Master replied, "The water is swift and the waves are coarse."

The monk asked, "How then can one escape? The Master said, "Green mountains do not obstruct the flight of white clouds. Another asked:

Li Zhi is like the son of a barren woman going away.

"Is this not different from the Way? The monk asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "Try to tell me. The monk replied, "If one has no wound oneself, do not inflict one upon them.

Chan Master Wuyin of He Mountain in Jizhou was the son of the Wu family in Fuzhou. At the age of seven, he left home to become a monk under Xuefeng.
Having received full ordination according to his age, he went to visit Jiufeng. Jiufeng asked, "You have come from afar; you follow the assembly with such earnestness.
What realm do you perceive that allows for cultivation? By what path can one achieve liberation? The Master replied, "The deep darkness is cleared away, yet the blind remain blind.
Jiufeng then permitted him to enter the inner quarters. Later, while residing at Heshan, his disciples gathered in great numbers, drawing students from all directions.
When Emperor Jiaokuan summoned Master Li of Jiangnan and questioned him, saying, "Where have you come from, Monk? the Master replied, "From Heishan.
The Emperor asked, "Where is that mountain? The Master said, "People come to pay court at the Phoenix Palace, yet the mountains and peaks never move.
The Ruler held him in high esteem and ordered him to reside at Xiangguang Monastery in Yangzhou. Later, he requested to retire to the mountains and took up residence at Cuoyan.
At that time, Shanglan Monastery was also vacant, and they invited the Master to come and propagate the Dharma there; he was titled Chan Master Chengyuan.
A monk asked, "A student has newly entered the monastic community; I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said, "I shall not spare you.

The Master said, "I ask you. [The monk] replied, "I have not yet discerned the fundamental principle; how can I fully comprehend it? The Master said, "The head is large and the tail is pointed.

The Master said, "If the law is exhausted, there will be no people. [The monk] said, "I do not fear having no people; please—"
The Master exhausted the Dharma. The Master said, "Heshan has been toppled. A monk asked, "'Practicing and studying' is called 'hearing'; 'ceasing study' is called 'the neighbor.

[The monk] did not ask. [The monk asked: "What is that which is neither mind nor Buddha? The Master said, "Heshan knows how to beat the drum.

The Master said, "It would rather be that my own body does not exist. A monk asked, "When the Venerable One plucked his eyebrows and struck his eyes while looking at King Aśoka, what was that?
The Master said, "Even now, it is just like this. The monk asked, "How should a student understand this? The Master said, "Is it not so?"
At Mount Mālīci, [the Master] asked: "The Maṇi-jewel palace has four corners, yet one corner is always exposed.

On the second day of the third month in the first year of the Jianlong era, he manifested a slight illness.

On the second day of the third month, he took leave of the assembly, saying, "Later students do not yet know Heishan; recognize him now! Be careful! Having finished speaking, he passed away. His posthumous title was...
Chan Master Faxing.
When a monk asked Chan Master Mou of Letan in Hongzhou, "What is the place where the student exerts effort? the Master said, "This is precisely the place where one exerts effort.
Upon ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What is the meaning behind Baizhang rolling up his mat? The Master said, "Be careful."
He then descended from his seat.

When they had finished clearing the slash-and-burn field, Nanquan asked, "What about the matter after the fire has burned? The Master replied, "An iron snake cannot penetrate it.

After he took up residence there, a monk asked, "How is the matter that does not pass through the throat, lips, or mouth? The Master said, "Wait until you have used a single spade to cleave Mount Jūnzō;

even then, I will not speak to you. Another asked, "There is a poisonous snake on the South Mountain; how can one approach it? The Master said: [The text here implies the Master’s response was to remain silent or to demonstrate non-duality].
"Day. Not only the *ācārya*, but even a thousand sages cannot approach it. The questioner asked, "I have heard that there is a 'Single Sword' koan in the South.
What is this Single Sword? The Master said, "Do not meet its edge. The questioner asked, "What if its head falls off? The Master said, "..."
"I say that when one does not meet the point of the blade, what head could there be? The man bowed in thanks and departed. When asked, "Before one's parents were born, where did that person stand?
the Master said, "The hexagram signs have not yet arisen; Sun Bin lost his calculation. When asked, "What is the summit of the great thousand-fold world?
the Master said, "It does not level with the other peaks. At the end of the summer retreat, the Master entered the Huading Peak of Mount Tiantai.
He concealed his traces, and no one knew where he ended his life.
Regarding the Dharma successor of Master Yungai Yuan of Tanzhou, Chan Master Zhihan of Mount Yungai, a monk asked: "What is the surging wave upon the summit of Mount Sumeru?"
Tian asked, "Master, Mañjuśrī is truly making a commotion. The Master said, "What is the matter within the state of absolute reality?
The Master said, "I do not display great compassion before the stimulus. Tian asked, "What is it like for a person on 'that side'? The Master said, "No shadow is revealed before the blade's edge;
once the phrase is over, no trace can be found."
A monk asked Zen Master Wo-long of Silla State, “What is the mark of a great man?
The Master said, “He does not extend his hand from within the purple silk curtain. The monk asked, “Why does he not extend his hand? The Master said, “Because it would not be noble.

A monk asked, “How should one apply the mind throughout the twelve periods of the day? The Master said, “A monkey eating fur-bugs. A monk asked, “What is the meaning of the deep pool? The Master said—
[The student] said, "The silken line hangs down but does not reach; at Pan Creek, one casts the hook in vain. [The student] asked, "What is that which lies beyond the depths?
The Master said, "The golden crow cries in the day; the jade hare leaps in startled alarm within the moon."
A monk asked Zen Master Deng of Tiantai in Pengzhou, "Where has the ancient Buddha gone?
The Master said, "The central mansion is lofty; year after year, numinous sprouts emerge. The monk asked, "How is it when the ancient mirror has not yet been polished?
The Master said, "No effort is applied. The monk asked, "How is it after it has been polished? The Master said, "It does not reflect. The monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Red."
On the lotus seat, no celestial crown was seen.
A monk asked Zen Master Silla Gusanjang, successor to [Master] Xinghua Cunjiang:
"When both black and white have perished, what is it like when the Buddha-eye opens? The Master said:
[The student] said, "I fear you will remain within. [He asked,] "What is the Prince at Birth? The Master said, "He cannot be led out from the deep palace.
[The student] asked, "What is the Prince Born at Dawn? The Master said, "He does not take his place within the palace.
[The student] asked, "What is the Prince Born Last? The Master said, "Everywhere there is no mark; he does not deploy the mechanism of the ten thousand men."
A monk asked National Teacher Baeryam of Silla, “What is Chan? The Master said, “An ancient tomb is not made into a home.
The monk asked, “What is the Way? The Master said, “The tracks of carriages and horses are but vain toil. The monk asked, “What are the Teachings?
The Master said, “They cannot be fully contained within the palm leaves.”
A monk asked Zen Master Daerim of Silla State, "The ancients said: 'Upon reaching Tongguan, one simply stops.

Does this mean one stops once understanding has been attained, or does one stop before understanding has been attained? The Master said, "It is simply because it is the livelihood within the path of delusion.

The monk asked, "If one leaves behind the path of delusion, can one still attain that livelihood? The Master said, "One may realize its essence, but one cannot abide within it. The monk said, "Since..."
[The student] said, "This is the realization of the essence. Why should one not attain it? The Master said, "What kind of person is the one who realizes the essence?
[The student] asked, "How is it within that state? The Master said, "Do not act as if you are noble. [The student] asked, "What is meant by 'pure in all places'?"
The Master said: "When jade branches are cut, every inch is treasure; when sandalwood is split, every fragment is fragrant.
He asked, "How is it that there is no obstruction within activity? The Master said: "A single mass of white clouds flies about in disarray."
Chan Master Chengjue Jing of Mount Yungai in Tanzhou, successor to Chan Master Zhongyunge, was asked by a monk: "When the land is peaceful and clear, to whom does the merit belong?
The Master said: "Under the Silver Terrace Gate, no congratulations are offered. The monk asked: "What is it like when one turns over merit and yet has no rank? The Master said: "The King."
The domestic affairs were as usual. [A monk] asked, "What are the matters beyond the threshold? The Master said, "After the sound of the painted drum has ended, the general does not nod his head.
Chan Master Shiyin of Heishan in Jizhou was asked by a monk, "Before the Prince has yet ascended the throne, who shall govern and transform the realm?"
The Master said, “Outside the imperial gate, the frontier regulations are not enforced; the General himself brings about an era of Great Peace.

[The student] asked, “If that is so, then would the merit of his governance and transformation still not be appropriate? The Master said, “There is indeed what is appropriate. [The student] asked, “What is it that is appropriate?
The Master said, “The lands of the ten directions all belong to the King. [The student] asked, “When one seeks the source over a long period of time, why is it not seen? The Master said, “Because...”
[The monk] took too many steps. [The Master] said, "If that is so, then you do not seek it. The Master continued, "That would be like avoiding drowning only to throw yourself into fire.
[The monk] asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master replied, "One who takes it upon themselves is no adept."
A monk asked Chan Master Congshi of Zhaxi in Youzhou, "What is the Way? The Master said, "Within this, there is no purple or black.
The monk asked, "What is Chan? The Master said, "It does not connect with the white clouds. The Master then asked a monk, "What have you come here for?"
The monk said, "I have come to draw near. The Master said, "Though you may let the white clouds soar toward the mountain peak, how can the green mountains fail to knit their brows?
Chan Master Yanbin of Mount Wuya in Qizhou, successor to Chan Master Lupu An, was asked by a monk: "Before one has yet taken human form, what is one doing?"
[The Master] said: "A three-legged stone ox gallops over the hill; a single branch of auspicious grass is distinguished before one's eyes. [Question:

"What is it like when one enters directly with a lone horse and a single spear? [Master: "Even if you were Xiong Xin, skilled at wielding the spear, you would still be a hundred paces behind King Qin.
[Question: "One has fought long on the battlefields; why is it that fame and merit are not achieved? [Master: "Two hawks follow..."
The arrow fell. Li Guang’s reputation was not in vain. [A monk] asked, "Who is it that pierces the willow at a hundred paces?

The Master said, "If the General had not crossed the Bridge of Convenience, the gold-tipped arrow would have been laboriously drawn from its notch. [Another monk] asked, "When the rainbow drinks from the roots of the clouds, what then?
The Master said, "The Golden Wheel Emperor descends to Jambudvīpa; upon his iron crown, the golden flower is extraordinary. [The monk] said, "Precisely at such a moment..."
"What is the situation now? The Master said, "Nowadays, one does not sit in the Hall of Spiritual Radiance; the painted drums have ceased their music, and the eight-rowed dance has ended.
Chan Master Chuanchu of Qingfeng in Fengxiang Prefecture was a native of Jingzhou. One day, Luopo asked him, "Where have you come from, Attendant?
The Master replied, "I have come from sweeping the snow. Luopo asked, "How deep is the snow? The Master replied, "The trees..."

Baishui asked, "I have heard it said that Luopu has a 'path of vital energy' (shengji yilu). Is this true? The Master replied, "It is true.
Baishui said, "Cease the path of life and come upon the path of maturity. The Master said, "On the path of life, there are countless dead people; on the path of maturity..."
"Not one who lives attached. Shui said, "This is Lopu’s bottom; what about yours?
The Master said, "Not only Lopu, but even Jia Shan could do nothing about it. Shui said, "Why could Jia Shan do nothing about it? The Master said:
He did not see the single path of the life-force of the Way. After he had attained realization, a monk asked: "Before Buddhas and demons have appeared, where do you respond?
The Master said: "Listen, all you venerable ones, to my response. You say the Great Matter is already clear; why then is it as if one has lost one's parents? The Master said:
"Without the spring breeze, the flowers will not bloom; yet once they have bloomed, the breeze blows them away. [The monk] asked: "How is it?"
"This is one color. The Master said, "There is not a single drop of water; the surging waves resemble silver mountains.

He was unaware of pain or itch. [The monk] asked, "What is the one phrase for a person of clear understanding? The Master said, "A spirited horse does not move an inch;

Chan Master Shanjing of Yong’an Monastery in Jingzhao Prefecture was the son of the Wang family of that commandery. His mother dreamed of a golden image and became pregnant upon waking.
In his youth, the Master studied Confucian learning and became widely versed in all manner of discourse. At the age of twenty-seven, he suddenly grew weary of the world’s floating illusions.
He traveled incognito to Mount Zhongnan, where he received the tonsure under Chan Master Guangdu.

During the Tianfu era of the Tang dynasty, he went south to visit Lopu, who recognized his potential and permitted him to enter the inner quarters of the community. He was subsequently appointed to oversee the garden, diligently managing all communal affairs.
One day, a monk took his leave of Lopu, who asked, "With mountains on all four sides, where will you go, O Kalyāṇamitra? The monk had no reply. Lopu said, "The limit..."
"You have spoken well for ten days; I shall now depart with you. That monk practiced walking meditation (*caṅkrama*) while searching in the dark, when he happened to enter the garden.
The Master asked him, "Venerable, since you were to have departed, why are you here now? The monk explained the reason in detail and earnestly requested that the Master speak on his behalf.
The Master said, "How can dense bamboo obstruct the flow of water? How can a high mountain hinder the flight of wild clouds? His words were thus.

The monk was filled with joy and leaped up. The Master instructed him, saying, "You must not say that these words were spoken by such-and-such a person. The monk then reported this to Baofu. Baofu asked, "Who said those words?
The monk replied, "Such-and-such a person said them. Baofu said, "That was not your own speech. The monk explained in detail how the head gardener had instructed him.

That evening, when Baofu ascended the hall, he addressed the assembly, saying, "Do not underestimate the head gardener; in days to come, there will be five hundred people sitting beneath his seat. Later, he came to dwell [there].
Huangbo was well. There were over five hundred monks remaining, which indeed accorded with the prediction of Luopo. A monk asked, "When one knows there is [the Way] but cannot attain it, what then?
The Master said, "What is there to know? The monk said, "It cannot be that there is nothing. The Master said, "If so, then you ought to be able to speak of it.
The monk said, "To speak of it is not non-existent; however, the words are biased. The Master said, "The water is frozen, so the fish find it hard to leap. The mountain...
The cold flowers bloom late. A monk asked, "What is the家风 (house style) of the Master? The Master said, "A wooden horse faces the setting sun;
entering the grass, it leaves no trace. A monk asked, "What is the single color? The Master said, "It is easy to distinguish flour in the snow, but difficult to discern soot in ink.
A monk asked, "What is the matter beyond the patched robe? The Master said, "The dragon and fish do not leave the sea; the moon in the water..."
"Do not swallow the light. Question: "When it cannot be known by wisdom and cannot be cognized by consciousness, how is it?

The Master said: "A crane and a heron, heads together, tread upon the snow and sleep; startled by the bright moon, both hesitate. Question: "How was it before Niu-tou had seen the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said:
"In the extraordinary landscape, the numinous pine is admired by all who behold it. Question: "And after he saw him? The Master said: [Silence].
When the leaves have fallen, the branches are broken; when the wind comes, it finds no resonance. [The student] asked, "How does one give birth to the family of the Tathāgata?

The Master said, "Donning the robes and gazing toward the dawn, one remains unenlightened for kalpas. [The student] asked, "What is it like after enlightenment? The Master said, "Not even a single phrase can be grasped."
He asked, "What is it to not sit upon the Tathāgata’s seat? The Master replied, "The stone maiden with her arms around her head returns late;
there is no trace left within the Jeta Grove assembly. The Master traveled to Bǎodào to avoid the chaos of Emperor Shaozong’s flight from the capital.

In the winter of the Bingwu year of the Kaiyun era of the Han dynasty, he struck the *gandi* to assemble the monks, gave his final instructions, entered the abbot’s quarters, and passed away reclining on his right side facing east.
He was posthumously titled Chan Master Jingwu (Pure Enlightenment).
When a monk asked Chan Master Zhudu of Dengzhou, "If one does not encounter the Teacher within the seas, who is the Lord within the realm?
The Master replied, "The golden rooster always announces the dawn; it is simply that people do not hear it. He further asked, "What is the bright mirror in the darkness? The Master [replied]...
[The student] said, "I do not understand. [The Master] asked, "I have not yet discerned what it is that you are illuminating. The Master said, "What thing is there that is not illuminated?

[The student] asked, "What is the ground of ultimate reality (*bhūtatathatā*), where not a single speck of dust is received? And how is it that within the gate of Buddha-activity (*buddhakārya*), not a single dharma is abandoned?
The Master said, "In true permanence, dust does not stain; the ocean receives the flow of a hundred rivers. [The student] said, "Please, Master, answer from beyond sound and form. The Master said:
A wooden man constantly engages in dialogue; though he possesses a nature, he cannot speak.
When Chan Master Jieding of Dongxi in Jiazhou first questioned Luopu: "The moon-tree has no branches, yet it provides long-lasting shade;

I pray that you, Master, will directly point to the wondrous, profound mystery. Luopu said: "In the place where the myriad phenomena flourish, things do not rely upon one another; the clear water forms a thousand waves."
"A solitary peak stands apart by itself. At this, the Master understood the essential meaning. Later, while residing there, a monk asked, "Why was the snake charmer swallowed by the snake?
The Master replied, "How many times did he knock at the gate before being called out? He thrust his body straight inside to see for himself.
An official asked, "Since this is a pure monastery, why do you beat the fish drum? The Master said, "One must strike it all the way through to the blue heavens."
[The Master] said: "Outside [the gate], one avoids seeing those who were marked on the forehead at Dragon Gate.

A monk asked Zen Master Wo Long of Jingzhao Prefecture: "The brilliant sun accords with the celestial horizon; the pearl-light shines upon the old capital. The ferry crossing connects to the Dharma-ocean;
what is your intention today? The Master said: "When the precious sword is brandished, how could it be confined by light or darkness?"

Chan Master Tongxuan Shiwei of Fucing Monastery in Quanzhou, successor to Chan Master Xiaoyao Zhong, was asked by a monk: "The branches spread across the ridges; you truly inherit the lineage of Xiaoyao.
Now that you have ascended the jeweled throne, we pray you will thunder the Dharma drum. The Master said: "Xiaoyao dwells far beyond all things; beyond all things, the rosy clouds do not reach."
Dongshan asked, "What is the essential meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Standing in the snow was not yet the toil; severing one's arm was finally the point.
Dongshan said, "If that is so, then 'one flower opens into five petals, its fragrance reaching down to the present.
The Master said, "When the cause is perfected beyond the three realms, the fruit is fully known throughout the ten directions."
A monk asked Chan Master Baiyun Wuxiu of Jingzhao Prefecture, "How does one subdue a fierce tiger encountered on the road?
The Master said, "Take refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha. The monk asked, "What is the realm of Baiyun? The Master said, "A sea traveler grieves by the tower under the moonlit night."
Chan Master Jingwu of Yong’an on Mount Lu, successor to Chan Master Panlong Wen, was asked by a monk: “What is the matter of leaving home? The Master said:
“To let go with both hands at a precipice ten thousand fathoms high. The monk asked: “What is the matter of not leaving home? The Master said: “Utterly distinct from the snow.”

A guest asked, "When the birds nest peacefully on the mountain ridges, it is unlike Xu You hanging his single gourd from a tree. When the six gates of the senses do not open, how does one convey the message?
The Master said, "With whom do you, Venerable, associate outside? A guest asked, "When one sheds the head of the cage and unloads the burden from the shoulder, what then?

The Master said, "Changing bones and washing the intestines to enter the Purple Barrier; at Yanmen Pass, one must strictly avoid picking up reeds again. A guest asked, "Regarding the succession of the patriarchs..."
"What do the various sages show to people? The Master said, "There is a distinct ancestral dragon’s mode of transformation, far surpassing the phoenix’s roost and transcending the rising dust.
[The student] asked, "What is the person who knows how to act as a guest? The Master said, "Even precious carriages and rare finery are cast aside."
"Who could, throughout kalpas, stand at another’s door? When asked, 'What is the meaning of the Westward Coming?
the Master said: 'The mud ox roars from the bottom of the sea; the wooden horse neighs amidst the clouds. When asked, 'Among all hands sifting gold, who is the one who obtains it?

the Master said: 'The Yellow Emperor never traveled to the Red Water; the divine pearl was found by the *wangxiang*, yet it remains utterly void. When asked, 'What is it like when snow covers the reeds and flowers? the Master said:"
It is said: "Though the frozen ice may manifest auspicious colors, once the great sun shines forth, it causes people to lose their way.
When Chan Master Shandao of Mount Muping in Yuanzhou first visited Luopo, he asked: "Before even a single bubble has arisen..."
"How does one discern the course of the water? Pu said, "Shift the boat to become familiar with the water's flow; raise the oars to distinguish the waves.
The Master did not find this resonant, so he went to consult Panlong, asking the same question as before. Panlong said, "Shift the boat without leaving the water;

raise the oars and you will immediately lose the source. From this, the Master attained awakening. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said, "The head of a stone ram."
Looking toward the east, he asked, "What is the True Dharma Eye? The Master said, "The hole in the staff.
He asked, "What is the Immovable Honored One? The Master said, "Wandering aimlessly. He asked, "What is the single phrase of Muping? The Master said, "It fills the void.
[The student] said, "I do not ask about filling the void; what is the single phrase? The Master struck him. Whenever there was...
A newcomer arrived, but was not permitted to pay his respects; instead, he was first ordered to carry earth. After carrying three loads, the Master showed him a verse, saying:
"The South Road slopes toward the low East Mountain; Newcomer, do not decline these three turns of mud. Alas, you have traveled this path for many days;
Though it is clear before your eyes, you remain deluded. The Master’s crown protrusion (uṣṇīṣa) had a spiral pattern. Li of Jinling, hearing of his reputation, invited him to come and made offerings.
[He] raised [him] and treated him with the etiquette due to a teacher. [Shishuang] once asked, "What is Muping? The Master said, "No need for axe or hatchet.
[Shishuang] asked, "Why no need for axe or hatchet? The Master said, "Muping. Chan Master Fayan composed a verse in his praise, which says:

"The man from within Muping Mountain, Ancient in appearance and sparse in speech. We gaze at each other as fellow travelers on a road; In discussing our minds, the autumn moon is bright. Tattered robes..."
The thread is not the silkworm; there is a bird that assists the song. The city gates come today; a single bubble has already been understood.
After his passing, his disciples erected a stupa for him, and he was posthumously titled Chan Master Zhenji (Tranquil Truth).
A monk asked Chan Master Chongfu Zhi, "It is said that making offerings to hundreds of thousands of Buddhas is not as good as making offerings to a single mindless man of the Way.
I wonder, what fault do the Buddhas have, and what virtue does the mindless man of the Way possess?

The Master said, "When the snow is deep, it is best to stay near the fire; when the body is warm, one perceives spring as slow. The monk asked, "What is it like when a poor man offers a pearl? The Master said, "What?"
[The Master] arrived at his dwelling. A monk asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "There is a portion for turning back the carriage.
Chan Master Longxi of Shanfu ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is the seamless stupa?
The Master said, "The adornment of the hundred jewels is now complete; how long has it been since the four gates were opened wide? The Master then said, "Even if one were to explain it like this..."
The Seamless Stūpa. Yet even so, the old monk cannot help but drive in a wedge. How can one avoid it? The assembly remained silent.
The Master said, "Go down.
This was the Dharma successor of Chan Master Lun of Huangshan.
Chan Master Tongquan (some editions read Tōng) of Yingzhou went to visit Huangshan. Huangshan asked, "The gates of heaven are closed; throughout the ten directions there is no path.
If someone can speak, they may wave their hand and leave Changjiang. The Master said, "The hibernation chamber remains unopened;
the dragon has no dragon-phrase. Huangshan said, "Is it you who speak thus? The Master said, "If it is right, speak directly that it is right; if it is not, speak directly that it is not."
Shishan said, "Waving my hand, I exit the Zhang River. Shishan asked again, "When it is said that 'Wherever Bian He goes, the Jing Mountains are beautiful;
the jade seal is passed on by the Son of Heaven,' what then? The Master replied, "The numinous crane does not rest beneath the forest trees;
the rustic elder does not prize the years of Great Peace. Shishan deeply approved. After he took up residence there, a monk asked, "What is the matter that has been transmitted? The Master—
He said, "The dragon spits forth water that grows forever; the fish swallow bubbles that are never-ending. He asked, "Please, Master, clarify this for me.
The Master said, "Beat the drum and turn the prow; the oars pierce the moon within the waves."

A monk asked Master Wenshu of Tanzhou, the Dharma successor of Chan Master Shaoshan Pu: "What is the matter before Mount Zhurong? The Master said, "Auspicious grass grows before the cliff. The monk asked:
"When a Benevolent King ascends the throne, the myriad people receive his grace. When you, Reverend, appear in the world, what auspicious signs are there?"
The Master said: "Ten thousand miles to Changsha, piloting an iron boat. [The student] asked: "What is this original adornment? The Master said:
"The scenery upon the chrysanthemum fields; the traveler’s path stretches long."
A monk asked Zen Master Miyō of Yaoshan, "I beg the Master to grant instruction regarding the words spoken in the secret chamber. The Master said, "In the south the waters are broad;
in the north the winds are many. The monk said, "I do not understand. I pray the Master will point it out again. The Master said, "It is easy for a bird to roost at the foot of a forest."
It is difficult for people to avoid the pitfalls of right and wrong.
Once, while Chan Master Shanben of Jialing Peak in Xiangzhou—a successor of Chan Master Siming—was bathing, a monk asked him: "The Master is a person free from defilement; why [is this so]?"

He finished bathing. The Master said, "The water of samādhi is full and serene; here one bathes this stainless person. He asked, "Are the intent of the Patriarchs and the intent of the Teachings the same or different?
The Master replied, "On the peak of Vulture Mountain, green grass reaches the heavens; in the Deer Park, foxes and rabbits cross paths."
The Dharma heir of Chan Master Tengxia of the seventh generation under Qingyuan, Chan Master Yaoshan of Lishui, ascended the hall and said:
"Now, a Bodhisattva who studies Prajñā has no fear of gain or loss. There is a matter..."
[The assembly] approached. At that time, a monk asked, "The descendants of Master Yaoshan request that you, Venerable Sir, proclaim the Dharma.

The Master said, "Ten thousand functions cannot pick it out. The monk asked, "Why cannot ten thousand functions pick it out? The Master said, "Its conditions lie along the riverbanks and mountain valleys.
The monk asked, "What is the house style of Yaoshan? The Master said, "Falling leaves are not as they were at first. The monk asked, "When the Dharma-thunder roars, what then? The Master—
[The student] asked, "The universe has never thundered. [The student] asked, "Why has it never thundered? The Master said, "Throughout the entire Sahā world, there has never been a roar.
[The student] asked, "What is the matter with that which does not roar? The Master said, "No one in the whole country knows."
A monk asked Zen Master Zang of Nantai Temple on Mount Heng, successor to Zen Master Yungai Jing:
"I have traveled from afar to seek refuge with you, Master; I pray that you will grant me an audience. The Master said:
Without opening the door, he asked, "What is the realm of Nantai? The Master said, "When the pine melody brushes by, the rock is not spotted;
beneath the solitary peak, the layers of earth cannot be made even. He asked, "Who is the person within the realm? The Master said, "Wild fruits are planted before the cliff."
When receiving guests who came and went, [a monk] said, "If that is so, then we thank the Master for his offerings. The Master asked, "What is its flavor?
A monk asked, "What is the Dharma Hall? The Master said, "It has no walls. A monk asked, "What is it like when one disregards all conditions? The Master remained silent for a long time.

This is the direct meaning of the School of the Patriarchs. The Master said: "A monk from the West ten thousand *li* away does not enter the waves.
Chan Master Wuya Bin’s successor, Chan Master Xinggu of Mount Dadian in Anzhou, was asked by a monk: "When a deceased monk undergoes transformation, where does he go?"
The Master said, "Last night at the third watch, we performed the ritual at the Southern Suburb. [Someone] asked, 'What is the meaning of Vimalakīrti’s silence?
The Master said, 'A dark, black stone ox, transcendentally never leaving its door. [Someone] asked, 'What is that matter over there? The Master said:"
The lacquer-black cowherd boy does not extend his hand; beside the silver cage, wild clouds fly past the cranes.
At Mount Wuya in Qizhou, Zen Master Xinglang was asked by a monk: "Before one has yet taken human form, what has one been doing?
The Master said: "The stone ox on the sea sings a three-beat song; a single red thread is divided within the palm. [He was then] asked about Kāśyapa.
[The Master] wore the robe of the "Upward-Going" (Xiángxíng). Who is fit to wear it? The Master said: "The Son of Natural Formlessness does not don the robe that transcends the mundane.
A monk asked West River (Xīchuān) Lìngkān Chán Master, a successor of Qīngfēng Chù Chán Master: "What is the place where all Buddhas emerge? The Master said: "The place of emergence."

"It is not the Buddha's doing; when spring comes, the grass turns green of its own accord. A monk asked, "When one is in a state of mere mundanity (*lùlù*), how is it? The Master said, "Try taking one step forward and see.
A monk asked Zen Master Duānjǐ of Mount Zígé in Jīngzhào Prefecture: "When the four marks have all been exhausted, what stands?"
"Zheng. The Master asked, "Where have you come from? [The monk] asked, "What is it like when the Wei River flows directly east? The Master said, "It has been without interruption from the beginning."
A monk asked Master Huazhou Kaishan Huidiao, "What practice must one perform to not contradict the thousand sages?

The Master said, "Sublime conduct is peerless; when the mind is profound, the essence is naturally distinct. The monk asked, "When there are ears but they do not approach clear water to wash, and there is no mind—then who acts for the seclusion of the white clouds?
What is it like at such a time? The Master said, "There is no tree upon which to hang a thousand pieces of gold. The monk said, "Hang it! The Master said, "It is hung."
"What is it like afterward? The Master said, "Profound and remote; it is difficult for people to discern. "Who is the teacher amidst the dust?
The Master said, "Reaching everywhere within the thicket of brambles; moving freely and at will within the grove of sandalwood. "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "The moon hidden in the clear pool; golden radiance at high noon."
A monk asked the Chan Master Chuanfa of Youzhou, "Are the meaning of the Teachings and the meaning of the Patriarchs the same or different?
The Master said, "Golden threads bloom upon the flowers; white clouds deepen within the ancient cave. The monk asked, "Why do others have many disciples, while you have none?
The Master said, "Dragons hide on the islands of the sea; phoenixes do not perch in thatched huts."
A monk who had taken refuge with Chan Master Gui of Jingzhong Monastery in Yizhou asked: "What is it like when the lotus flower has not yet emerged from the water?
The Master said: "The buds fill the pond. The monk asked: "What is it like after it has emerged? The Master said: "The leaves fall, and one does not know autumn. Another asked:
"What is it like when, without relying on a life-preserving skin bag, one immediately ascends the vast ocean? The Master said: "The red-beaked bird flies beyond the three realms."
Lümao also understood how to brew tea. [A monk] asked, "What is the person who is autonomous?
The Master said, "He goes directly through the sword-trees and frosty forests. [The monk] asked, "What is the person who is not autonomous? The Master said, "Śākyamuni is behind you, O Layman."
A monk asked Zen Master Qingmian of Mount Qingfeng, "The grape wine has been aged for a long time; for whom is it opened today?
The Master said, "Only the drinker knows. Another asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Not a single drop in Lake Anavatapta;
yet the four seas flow on and on."
During the Song dynasty, Emperor Taizong once visited Xiangguo Monastery. Seeing a monk reading a scripture, the Emperor asked, "What scripture is this?
The monk replied, "The Benevolent Kings Sutra. The Emperor said, "Since it is my own sutra, why is it in your hands?"
The monk had no reply. (Xuedou spoke on his behalf: "Heaven has no partiality; it aids only virtue. By chance, the precious stupa was opened, and the Emperor questioned a monk, saying, "Who are you?
The monk replied, "I am the master of the stupa. The Emperor said, "Why do you act as the master of my stupa? The monk had no reply. (Xuedou spoke on his behalf: "The entire nation knows this.
One day, because a monk came for an audience, the Emperor asked, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From the Wolun Hermitage on Mount Lu. The Emperor—

The Emperor said, "I have heard that those who dwell deep in the clouds do not face the court. For what reason have you come here? The monk had no reply. (Xuedou, acting on his behalf, said: "It is difficult to escape the ultimate transformation.
When the monk entered the presence again, he reported, "Does Your Majesty remember us yet? The Emperor said, "Where did we meet?"

The monk addressed the Emperor, saying, "Since our parting at Vulture Peak, it has been until this very day. The Emperor asked, "What proof do you have? The monk had no reply. (Xuedou, acting on his behalf, said:

"I, this poor monk, have come specifically for this purpose. The imperial temple had suffered from a fire, and the Tripitaka scriptures were all reduced to ashes. The monk wished to request that they be granted by imperial decree.
The Emperor summoned him and asked, "In the past, Fotudeng was not burned; why is it that he is burned now? The monk had no reply. (Xuedou spoke on his behalf:
"Your Majesty has not forgotten the entrustment. The Emperor once dreamed of a divine being who told him, "I request that Your Majesty give rise to the Bodhicitta.

Consequently, at the early court audience, he proclaimed to his attendants, "How does one give rise to the Bodhicitta? The attendants had no reply. (Xuedou spoke on their behalf: "Truly, this is rarely heard in antiquity or today. Zhi.
Master Ji presented the "Diagram of the Three Realms" to the Emperor. The Emperor asked, "In which realm am I? Master Ji had no reply. (Baoning Yong spoke on his behalf:

"Your Majesty, where would you not be called Honored One? One day, after the court session had ended, the Emperor held up a bowl and asked Chancellor Wang Sui, "Since it cannot be lifted at the head of Dayu Ridge, why is it now in my hands? Wang Sui had no reply.

In the third year of the Zhenghe era of Emperor Huizong, the patrol officer of Jiazhou submitted a report: "Along the roadside within our jurisdiction, there is a large ancient tree that has been broken by the wind.
Inside it is a monk in meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), his beard and hair covering his body and his fingernails encircling him."

The Emperor issued an edict ordering that he be carried into the capital by palanquin. He commanded Tripitaka Master Sengzhici of the Western Heaven to rouse him from his samādhi using a golden *kaṅkā* (gong).
Upon emerging, the Master asked, "In what era do you live? He replied, "I am Huichi, the younger brother of Dharma Master Huiyuan of Donglin.
While traveling to Mount Emei, I entered this samādhi beneath a tree. Is Dharma Master Huiyuan free from ailment? The Tripitaka Master said, "Dharma Master Huiyuan was a man of the Jin dynasty."
Seven hundred years have passed since he passed away. Daochi remained silent and did not speak again. Daocang asked, "Since you have arrived here, Master, where do you intend to go?

Daochi replied, "I shall enter meditative concentration once more at Chenliu County. The Emperor composed three verses and had a portrait painted for circulation. The verses read: [The verses follow.]
For seven hundred years, this ancient adept—within his state of meditative concentration, who could possibly know his news? How can he compare to one who departed westward with but a single shoe;
what need is there to labor over life and death like wood encased in bark? To hide a mountain in a marsh is also to hide one's person;

when the world has no place to hide, the Way becomes accessible. Send word to Zhuang Zhou: cease your conjectures. Within the tree is not the man who carries the burden. The body of sentient beings is not...
This is insentient. Each and every person is the body within samādhi. If you can realize that Bodhi originally has no tree, there is no need for the arduous toil of questioning Huineng.
Emperor Xiaozong summoned Chan Master Lingyin Foguang and questioned him, saying: "Śākyamuni Buddha entered the mountains to practice..."
"The Way is accomplished in six years. What is it that is accomplished? I pray that the Master will explain this clearly. He replied, "I thought Your Majesty had forgotten.
