Chan Master Daopu Hongjiao of Shuilong Mountain in Quanzhou was the son of the Zheng family of Fudang. He first resided at Wufeng. Upon ascending the hall, he said:
"Do not say that this empty mountain has no one to attend to you," and he immediately returned to his quarters.

A monk asked, "All words and phrases do not exceed the summit of the great chiliocosm; I wonder, what is it like beyond the summit? The Master said, "All words and phrases are not [beyond the summit]."
Qianding asked, "What is the Great Thousandfold World? The Master said, "Maheśvara Heaven is still but a Small Thousandfold World.
He asked a beginner who had recently entered the monastic community, "In the gate of expedient means, I beg the Master for instruction.
The Master struck the door-bar. The monk asked, "Is there anything further above this? The Master said, "There is. The monk asked, "What is that which is further above?"
Incident: Master [Nanyue] struck the door-bar once more.
Chan Master Jinlun Kegoan of Nanyue was the son of the Xue family of Fudang. He went to attend upon Xuefeng. Xuefeng said, "Come closer.
As the Master approached and prostrated himself, Xuefeng gave him a kick. The Master suddenly attained awakening. He served [Xuefeng] for twelve years.
He traveled through various monasteries again. Upon arriving at [Huangbo] later, he ascended the hall and said: "When I was at Xuefeng, I encountered his one kick;
until this very day, my eyes have not opened. I do not know what kind of realm that was. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the West? The Master said, "It is not so.
After the evening assembly, as the Master descended from the hall, he called out to the assembly. When the assembly turned their heads, the Master said, "Look at the moon! The assembly...
He then looked. The Master said, "The moon is like a drawn bow; little rain, much wind. The assembly had no reply.
He asked, "An ancient said, 'Vairocana has a teacher; the Dharmakāya has a master. Who is the teacher of Vairocana and the master of the Dharmakāya?
The Master said, "One must not place a bed upon a bed. He asked, "What is the matter of daily life? The Master clapped his hands three times. The monk said, "I, your student..."
[The monk] had not yet grasped this meaning. The Master said, "What more are you waiting for? A monk asked, "Regarding the ancestral vehicle (zongcheng) from above, how do you guide people?
The Master said, "I have not yet drunk tea today. The monk said, "Please give me instruction, Master. The Master said, "It is already past.

A monk asked, "I do not ask about the direct principle; please point to it indirectly. The Master said, "Go and take the cat away. A monk asked, "Where have you come from? [The monk] replied, "From Huaguang."

The Master then pushed him out and closed the door; the monk was speechless. [Another] asked: "When meeting a person who has attained the Way on the road, one does not respond with either speech or silence;
I wonder, what would you use to respond? The Master rebuked him, saying, "Get out! He then asked a monk, "What is the matter of face-to-face encounter?"
[The monk] said, "I ask that the Master examine me. The Master said, "If you speak thus, does it accord [with reality]?

He replied, "It would be improper to do so intentionally. The Master said, "This is another matter entirely. He asked, "What is the single path of the spiritual source? The Master said, "Why try to step over it?
The Head Monk of Xuefeng sent a letter inviting him, saying, "The Abbot of the mountain is advanced in years; why does the Elder not return there once more?"
When the monk had crossed the ridge once, the Master sent back a letter saying, "Wait until the Monk of the Mountain Head has some further insight; then you may enter the ridge again.
A monk asked, "What is Xuefeng’s insight? The Master said, "I am also startled."
Chan Master Xuantong of Dapu Mountain in Fuzhou was a native of that same prefecture. A monk asked, "How can one obtain the pearl from beneath the chin of a black dragon?
The Master clapped his hands and winked at him. The monk asked, "Regarding the matter prior to the employment of skillful means, how is it?
The Master then pushed the monk out. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "A fellow who bites on a bone. [He] went out.
[The monk] departs. [Another] asks: "What is it like when one brushes away the dust and sees the Buddha? The Master says: "Come off that shackle and let us discuss it.
A monk asks: "I am urgently seeking refuge; I pray the Master will receive me. The Master says: "You dull-witted fellow!"
Chan Master Jiaoran of Changsheng Mountain in Fuzhou was a native of that region.
Having long relied upon Xuefeng, one day while he was cutting down a tree with a monk, Xuefeng said, "Stop when you reach the heartwood. The Master said, "Cut it away!
Xuefeng said, "The ancients transmitted mind-to-mind; why do you say 'cut it away'? The Master threw down his axe and said, "Transmitted. Xuefeng struck him with his staff.
He departed with his staff. A monk asked Xuefeng, "What is the first phrase? Xuefeng remained silent for a long while.
The monk reported this to the Master (Linji), who said, "This is the second phrase. Xuefeng then sent the same monk back to ask again, "What is the first phrase?"

The Master said, "Heaven! Heaven! Once, during a communal work session (*pǔqǐng*), Xuefeng asked, "An ancient said, 'Who knows that beneath this scholar’s cap lies none other than a man of former sorrows'?
What was the intent of that ancient? The Master tilted his bamboo hat sideways and said, "Whose words are these?
Xuefeng asked the Master, "One who upholds the sutras is able to shoulder the Tathāgata. What is it to 'shoulder' [him]?"

Xuefeng was carrying the Tathāgata when his teacher took the Xuefeng statue and placed it upon the meditation seat. During a communal work session (*pingsheng*), Xuefeng was carrying a bundle of rattan vines.
On the road, he encountered a monk and immediately threw them down. As the monk attempted to pick them up, Xuefeng kicked him over.
Upon returning, he said to his teacher, "I felt quite swift today in kicking that monk. The teacher replied, "The Master should have taken that monk’s place in the Nirvana Hall instead."
Feng then desisted. Xuefeng asked, "When both light and its object have vanished, what is it?
The Master said, "Let Jiaoran pass. Xuefeng said, "I let you pass; how would you say it? The Master said, "I also let the Master pass, Jiaoran.
Xuefeng said, "I grant you twenty blows. The Master then bowed. Later, while residing there, a monk asked, "An ancient said:"
“Ignorance is itself Buddha-nature; there is no need to eliminate afflictions. “How is it that ignorance is itself Buddha-nature?
The Master, his expression suddenly fierce, raised his fist and scolded him, saying, “Today I am going to beat this monk!
“How is it that there is no need to eliminate afflictions? The Master grabbed the man’s head with his hand and said, “This monk brings such karmic retribution upon himself! [The monk] asked.
On the road, he encountered a man who had attained the Way. [The Master] did not respond with either speech or silence. "I do not know what you would have used to respond," [the man] asked.
The Master said, "What could this paper and ink be good for? He was appointed as the Zen Master by the Military Governor of Min, and his final whereabouts are unknown.
Chan Master Zhifu of Ehu in Xinzhou was a native of Fuzhou. A monk asked, "The myriad dharmas return to the One; where does the One return?
The Master said, "It is not only you, Dharma brother, who are in a hurry. [Another] asked, "When empty space preaches the sutras, what does it take as its fundamental principle?"
The Master said, "Ācārya, you are not among the audience; get out. He asked, "Does the son of one who has committed the five heinous crimes still receive his father’s instructions?
The Master said, "Though he may take his own life, he cannot avoid injuring himself. He asked, "Who is the man above the Buddha?
The Master said, "I knew well that you, Ācārya, would be at a loss. He asked, "Why are you at a loss? The Master said, "It is not necessarily small."
"A person attains the sight of the Gentleman. [The monk] asked, "Please tell me the meaning of the preceding phrase.
The Master said, "What are you searching for beneath your own heels? [The monk] said, "I am asking you right now. The Master said, "Look; you cannot change your body.
[The monk] asked, "What was the meaning of Xuefeng’s throwing down his staff? The Master threw his incense-spoon to the ground. The monk said, "I do not yet understand this meaning."
"How is it? The Master said, "Not a good seed. Get out. He asked, "What is the first phrase of鹅湖 (Ehu)?
The Master said, "Say what? He asked, "How is it so? The Master said, "It interferes with my sleep. He asked, "When there is no question and no answer, how is it?
The Master said, "Who would know among those who ask? He asked, "When the deluded child has not yet returned home, how is it? The Master said:
"Not on the road. [The monk] asked, "After returning, what then? The Master said, "I am still lost in it. [The monk] asked, "What is the matter of the source?
The Master said, "What are you looking for on the road? [The monk] asked, "What is the one phrase? The Master said, "Do you understand?
[The monk] said, "In that case, is this not it? The Master said, "Heaven! Heaven! Jingqing asked, "What is that which is right now? The Master—

[The Master] said, "What is more immediate than this? Qing said, "I have recently taken up the responsibility of supporting [the community]. The Master said, "Your words are contrary, yet your meaning is compliant.
One day, the Master did not go to the hall. The attendant came to invite him to the hall, and the Master said, "Today I am at the manor eating oil-cakes until I am full."
The man said, "The Master has never come or gone out. The Teacher said, "You simply go and ask the headman of the estate.
Just as the man was about to leave the gate, he suddenly saw the headman returning, thanking the Master for coming to the estate to eat oil-cakes (*youti*).
Chan Master Wuzhen of Huadu Monastery in Xixing, Hangzhou, was a native of Quanzhou. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey?
The Master raised his whisk. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Go drink tea. The monk asked, "What is one speck of dust?
The Master said, "Nine generations divided within a single kṣaṇa. The monk asked, "How can it contain the entire Dharma-realm? The Master said:
“Where does the Dharma-realm reside? [The questioner] asked: “Valleys and gullies each differ; why do you, Master, clarify their unity? The Master said: “Why are you panting?

[The questioner] asked: “I am a beginner; I beg the Master for instruction on the path of entry. The Master said: “What is it that you find strange about Huadu? [The questioner] asked: “What is the mani-jewel that reflects colors?
The Master said: “Blue, yellow, red, and white. [The questioner] asked: “What is [the jewel that reflects its own color]? The Master said: “It is like a mirror.”
[The Master] said, "It does not follow the colors. [The student] asked, "Blue, yellow, red, or white? The Master said, "Blue, yellow, red, or white.

[The student] asked, "What is the meaning of the coming from the West? The Master said, "Whether it comes from the East or the West. [The student] asked, "How was it before Niu-tou had seen the Fourth Patriarch?

The Master said, "Birds and beasts were all lost in confusion. [The student] asked, "How was it after he saw him? The Master said, "The mountains are deep and the waters are cold. [The student] asked, "Regarding Vimalakīrti and Mañjuśrī in dialogue..."
"What is it you are discussing? The Master said, "There is only the Mirror Lake before my gate; its clear breeze does not alter its waves from former times.
Changzhou Longshou Shaoqing Xingfa Chan Master was the son of the Chen family of Quanzhou.

While attending Xuefeng as they were walking in the mountains, he saw a taro leaf move. Xuefeng pointed to the moving leaf and showed it to him. The Master said, "Shaoqing is very much afraid. Xuefeng—
[The Master] said, "This is what is within your own house. Why do you fear it? At these words, the Master attained realization. He subsequently resided at Longxi.
A monk asked, "An ancient said, 'The Maṇi Hall has four corners; one corner is always exposed. What is the corner that is always exposed? The Master raised his whisk.
The monk asked, "If not a single grain of rice is stored as provisions, how can the hunger of ten thousand people be relieved? The Master said:
[The Master said: "It is like snatching a sword from before a knight-errant. I see that you are no clever fellow. [The monk] asked, "How is it when the ears and eyes do not reach?
The Master said, "You have no such activity. [The monk] said, "If that is so, then I hear. The Master said, "Truly a deaf man!"
Chan Master Xingrenhui of the Qianzong Monastery in Fuzhou was a native of the Wang family in Quanzhou. He ascended the hall and said: "I have studied under the same teacher as Śākyamuni.
Tell me, whom have you studied under? At that time, a monk came forward, prostrated, and intended to pose a question.

The Master said, "Wrong! and immediately descended from his seat. A monk asked: "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said: "Mount Xiong'er has never hidden it. A monk asked: [The text here ends abruptly.]
"I beg the Master for a skillful means regarding the matter right here and now. The Master said, "Were it not for your question, I would not have spoken either.
[The student] asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said, "In broad daylight, there are no idle people."
Chan Master Conggan Chaozheng of Lianhua Yongfu Monastery in Fuzhou was asked by a monk, "In the Confucian gate, the Five Constant Virtues are taken as the ultimate standard.
I wonder, in the Gate of the Patriarchs, what is taken as the ultimate standard? The Master remained silent for a long while. The monk said, "If that is so, then students will act with haste.
The Master said, "A staff would be well-suited for you. Another monk asked, "The scriptures say, 'There is only the One Vehicle Dharma.'"
"What is the Dharma of the One Vehicle? The Master said, "Tell me, what am I doing here?
The monk said, "If that is so, then you do not understand the meaning of the teaching. The Master said, "Even though it is so, I have not failed you.

A monk asked, "If one does not grasp it at the point of questioning, that is still the student’s point of questioning. What about the Master’s point? The Master said, "Go drink tea. He ascended the hall [to preach].
Changqing said, "When the Dharma is exhausted, there are no subjects. Yongfu said, "It is not so. If the Dharma were not exhausted, how could there be subjects?
At that time, a monk said, "I ask the Master to exhaust the Dharma. The Master said, "I do not want you to pay taxes; I am asking about other matters, not this one.
Please show me some compassion regarding this direct path. The Master said, "If it does not please you, then perform three prostrations. He asked the assembly, "What about the clouds?"

The assembly gathered and requested the Master to preach the Dharma. The Master asked, "Do you hear? When the monk replied, "If one were to pause for thought, it would be difficult to reach [the truth]," the Master said, "In reality, it is attained.
He was asked, "The Maṇi Hall has four corners; one corner is always exposed. What is this ever-exposed corner?
The Master said, "It cannot be pointed out further. One day, the Master ascended the hall and stood by his seat, saying to the assembly: "Two..."
The Venerable One did not manifest his transformation simultaneously; he then returned to his quarters.
Chan Master Guiben of Yun’gai Shuangquan Monastery in Xiangzhou was a native of Jingzhao Prefecture. Initially, he visited Xuefeng.
Following the prostrations, [Zhaozhou] sat with his back against the crossbar of a meditation seat at the foot of the peak. At this moment, the Master attained realization.
After he took up residence there, a monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Two Springs? The Master said, "A pity for those two eyebrows. The monk said, "I do not understand.
The Master said, "The labor of Yu was never required; one does not know the matter of the rushing torrents. A monk asked, "What is the very intent of the coming from the West? The Master then—
He grabbed him, and the monk’s complexion changed. The Master said, "There is no such thing here. The Master’s fingers were long and slender, exceptionally distinct from those of others;
he was known as the Great Master of Hand-Examination.
A monk asked Master Linquan of Shaoyang, “What is one speck of dust? The Master said, “Unconsciously it becomes a mountain.
A monk asked Master Nanyuan of Luojing, “What is the non-arising of all phenomena? The Master said, “It has already arisen.
There was a Confucian scholar who had read extensively throughout ancient and modern times; he was commonly called Zhang Baihui. He visited the Master, who asked, “Are you not Zhang Baihui?”
"Do you understand? He replied, "I dare not say so. The Master drew a line in the air with his hand and said, "Do you understand? He replied, "I do not understand.
The Master said, "If you do not even understand one, from where could you have obtained the hundred meetings?"
A monk asked Chan Master Keshou of Dongyan in Yuezhou, “What is the true master of Dongyan? The Master said, “It is open.
The monk asked, “What is your intimate way of acting for others? The Master said, “The great ocean does not harbor a corpse.”
Question: "What is the path that leads upward? The Master raised his robe collar and showed it to him. Question: "The student has come from afar;
we pray the Master will provide us with a skillful means. The Master said: "The skillful means have already been provided."
A monk asked Zen Master Xingzhou of Fahai Monastery in Dingzhou, “When the wind is calm and the waves are still, what is it like?
The Master said, “It blows down the southern wall. The monk asked, “What is the treasure within the Way? The Master said, “It does not reveal its radiance.
The monk said, “Is this not it? The Master said, “If it were, it would be revealed.”
A monk asked Chan Master Tong of Longjing in Hangzhou, "What is the dragon of Longjing? The Master said, "Its spirit is naturally distinct;
the divine artisan cannot paint it. The monk asked, "Why can it not be painted? The Master said, "It stands out from the crowd without horns;
it does not conform to its kind. The monk asked, "Does it also know how to bring forth rain? The Master said, "It universally moistens all things without limit."

Everywhere there were grains forming. [A monk] asked, "Is there still the matter of the School Gate (the Zen tradition) or not? The Master said, "There is. [The monk] asked, "What is the matter of the School Gate?
The Master said, "From the beginning it has had no form or segment; responding to things, it has never been deficient."
Chan Master Zongjing of Longxing Temple in Hangzhou was a native of Taizhou. Initially, he visited Xuefeng and vowed to serve as the head cook (*diantou*).
He labored in this capacity for over ten years. Once, while in the communal hall, he bared one shoulder while nailing up the curtain.

Upon seeing this, Xuefeng remarked, "In the future, when you reside as an abbot, there will be a thousand monks, yet not a single one among them will be a true patch-robed practitioner (*nanzizi*). The Master repented his error and returned to Zhejiang.

He resided at Liutongyuan (Six Supernatural Powers Monastery). King Qian summoned him to reside at Longxing Temple, where there were over a thousand followers, all of whom were practitioners of the Three Studies engaged in lecturing and recitation—exactly as Xuefeng had predicted.
A monk asked, "What is the extraordinary proclamation of the Six Supernatural Powers?
The Master said, "It is being carried away by everyone in the world. The monk asked, "What is the house style of the Six Supernatural Powers? The Master said, "A single piece of coarse cotton robe."

It weighed a little over one jin. [The student] asked, "What is the one path for the student to advance upon? The Master said, "Who dares deceive you? [The student] said, "Is there no expedient means?
The Master said, "That would already be a state of being constrained and suppressed. [The student] asked, "What is the house style of the Master?"
The Master said, "Breakfast is porridge; at noon it is rice. The monk asked, "Please, Master, speak further. The Master said, "This old monk is weary.
The monk asked, "Ultimately, what is it? The Master simply laughed loudly.
Chan Master Chiqian of Nanchan Monastery in Fuzhou ascended the hall and said: "As for famous phrases and wondrous sentences, everyone everywhere has already spoken of them.
Today, is there anyone among this assembly who can transcend the primary meaning? Bring forth a question. If you do, you will not have brought shame upon others.
A monk asked, "What is the primary meaning? The Master said, "Why do you not ask about the second?"

[The student] said, "This is the primary meaning. The Master said, "That has already fallen into the secondary meaning. [The student] asked, "I ask about the melody of the ancient Buddhas; I request that the Master provide the harmony.
The Master said, "I will not harmonize with you for something so confused. [The student] said, "I do not understand why the Master would harmonize with others. The Master said:
"Where have you come from? "From Yuezhou.
Master Shaner Nai, the Zen Master Jianzhen of Yue Mountain, first gained a taste [of the Way] upon his initial visit to Xuefeng.
Later, at the invitation of the King of Min, he sat for a long time during a meal at Qingfeng Lou. Suddenly, looking up, he beheld the sunlight and attained a sudden, profound realization. And...
There is a verse that says: "Ascending the Qingfeng Tower for the official vegetarian feast, On this day, the eyes of my entire life were opened wide.

Only now do I believe that the matters of the distant Putong era Were not brought here from Mount Xiang. He presented this to Xuefeng, who approved it. After he had taken up residence [at Qingfeng],...
A monk asked, "What is the Buddha-body? The Master said, "Which Buddha-body are you asking about?
The monk replied, "The body of Śākyamuni Buddha. The Master said, "His tongue covers the three thousandfold world-system. As he approached his death, the Master presented this verse:

"The visual faculty perishes along with forms; Auditory consciousness vanishes following sounds. Returning to the source has no other principle: Today is the same as tomorrow. Thereupon, he passed away while sitting in the full lotus posture.
Chan Master Xuǎnè of Fúqíng Yúan in Quánzhōu was a native of Gāolì (Korea).
When the local governor, Duke Wáng, asked, "What is the matter within the lineage vehicle? the Master rebuked him. A monk asked, "What is bodhi at every turn?
The Master said, "Dharma brother, you have lost half a year’s worth of provisions. The monk asked, "Why is it so? The Master replied, "It is simply because he sought one *dǒu* from another."
[The Master] said, "Rice. A questioner asked, "What is the pure Dharmakāya? The Master said, "A shrimp and a centipede. A questioner asked, "The teachings say:
'There is but one firm and dense body, which manifests within all atoms. What is this firm and dense body? The Master said, "Donkeys, horses, and cats."
He said, "I beg the Master for instruction. The Master replied, "Even donkeys and horses do not understand this. He asked, "How does one discern and clarify it within each and every thing?
The Master extended one leg and showed it to him.
A monk asked Master Ren of Nantai in Quzhou, "What is the realm of Nantai? The Master said, "I do not know its value.
The monk asked, "Ultimately, what is it? The Master said, "Where are you right now, O *śrāmaṇera*?"
When Master Dongchan of Quanzhou first ascended the hall, a monk asked: "The King of Men has invited the Dharma King to appear in the world;
how should he proclaim the lineage teachings so as not to err from the ancestral style? The Master said: "Can you handle it? The monk said:
"If one does not go down into the water, how can one know there are fish? The Master said: "Do not speak idle words. The monk asked: "What is the ultimate teaching of the Buddha-dharma?"
At the Place of Kindness, the Master said, "A transgression. A student asked, "I have come from afar; I request the Master’s very first phrase. The Master said, "Where have you come from?
A student asked, "What is the matter that is my own portion? The Master said, "Suffering. A student asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, "Fortunately, you are already pitiable enough; you need not insist on seeking it in another land."

Chan Master Congxi of Dàqián Mountain in Hangzhou was a direct disciple of Xuefeng. Having received the seal of realization from his own teacher, he thoroughly understood the essentials of the school.
He often said, "I strike the drum of Guannan and sing the song of Xuefeng.

Later, he entered Zhejiang to visit the King of Qián, who was deeply moved by his spiritual transformation and commanded him to reside on this mountain to propagate the Dharma. A monk asked, "If it were not for the King’s invitation..."
"Since you have gathered here, I request that the Master directly point out the very meaning of coming from the West. The Master said, "That monk over there has passed this way.
The student said, "I do not understand; I beg the Master to point it out again. The Master said, "How can you be so lacking in discernment? [The student asked:
"It is said, 'Building a cart inside the door, one fits the tracks upon leaving. What is 'building a cart inside the door'? The Master said:
[The Master] said, "I do not ask about the making of the carriage; what is the track? [The student] said, "I do not understand. I beg the Master for instruction.
The Master said, "A skilled craftsman applies his craft without revealing the hammer or axe."
A monk asked Master Yongtai of Fuzhou, "I have heard that you, Master, see tigers—is this true? The Master made the sound of a tiger.

The monk made a gesture as if to strike him. The Master said, "You dead man! Another asked, "What is the Buddha of True Nature? The Master clapped his hands and said, "I do not understand, I do not understand."
Chan Master Shoune Miaokong of Longshouchang Monastery in Chizhou was the son of the Lin family of Fuzhou.

A monk asked, "Before reaching the Dragon Gate, how does one find a place to settle? The Master said, "It is difficult to maintain one's life. A newly arrived monk came to pay his respects. The Master asked, "Where have you recently departed from?
The monk replied, "Not departing from the mind-ground (fangcun). The Master said, "It is no easy matter to come here. The monk also said, "It is no easy matter to come here. The Master [nodded].
He gave him a slap on the palm and asked, "What is this mind that has been transmitted? The Master said, "I have instructed you repeatedly not to speak of it to others.
The monk asked, "What is the ancestral vehicle from above? The Master said, "Can it be placed within your mouth, O *jiaoli*?
The monk asked, "Please grant me a direct introduction to the essential point. The Master said, "That is indeed essential."
A monk asked Zen Master Mengbi of Jianzhou, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "I do not deceive you. The monk said, "Is that not so?
The Master said, "You are deceiving him. When the King of Min invited the Master for a meal, he asked, "Have you brought your brush with you?"
The Master said, "This is not the embroidered brush of Mount Xi; I am ashamed it is not the rabbit-hair pen from within the moon.

Since Your Majesty has deigned to inquire, this mountain monk dares not fail to present my response. He asked again, "What is the Dharma King? The Master said, "This is not the family style of Mengbi."
A monk asked Zen Master Yuan Yan of Fuzhou Xijue: "What is the家风 (family style) of Xijue? The Master said:
"It fills the eyes and cannot be fully seen. The monk asked: "The myriad dharmas have no root; I do not know what it is that you teach the student to take up.

The Master said: "Do not speak in your sleep. The monk asked: "I have long dwelt in a dark room and have not yet reached its source. Today I have come before you; I beg the Master for [instruction]. The Master said: [One word missing in original text].
[The monk] bowed. The Master said, "Do not close your eyes and pretend it is night. [The monk] said, "If that is so, then the Udumbara flower has blossomed.
[The Master] said, "That is a concession for the present age. How would you show the supreme ancestral wind? The Master said, "Do you recognize it or not?

[The monk] said, "If that is so, then my doubts have ceased. The Master said, "Do not speak in your sleep before the great assembly. [The monk] asked, "As for Kāśyapa Mātanga entering the Han, it is already..."
Question: "How was it when Bodhidharma came to Liang? The Master said: "Is it mistaken now? [The questioner] said:
"If so, then the principle has produced the Three Vehicles and the flowers have blossomed into five petals. The Master said: "What are you talking about—the Three Vehicles and five petals? Get out!"
A monk asked Chan Master Rutai of Mount Furong in Fuzhou, "What is the ancient melody? The Master remained silent for a long while and then asked, "Do you hear it?
The monk replied, "I do not hear it. The Master presented this verse: "The ancient melody sounds majestic; The rhythm of the present time is the same.
If one were to point with the foremost finger, Even the Buddhas and Patriarchs would lose their tracks."
A monk asked the Reverend Qiehe at Luojing, “What is Qiehe? The Master joined his two hands and struck them together, saying, “Jubao, jubao” (Fengxue said:
“The crane’s cry resounds through the universe; do not let the flock of chickens claim they know the time”). The monk asked, “When a fine horse does not enter Western Qin, what then?
The Master said, “Where would it go?”
A monk asked Master Xichan of Mount Gui in Tanzhou, "At this very moment, how does one draw near?
The Master said, "How do you intend to draw near? The monk said, "Is there no expedient means? The Master said, "The Kaiyuan and Longxing editions of the Great and Small Tripitakas.
[Another monk] asked, "What is swift supernatural power? The Master said, "New clothes become tattered rags. [Another monk] asked, "What is... (The question is incomplete in the source).
[Someone] asked about Huangxian Bridge. The Master said, "How many people has it deceived? [Another] asked, "Without resorting to elaborate talk, what is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, "Do not make the sound of a jackal."
When Chan Master Yanzong of Chaoshan in Jizhou came to visit Zifu, the Master descended from his meditation seat to receive him.
Zifu asked, "How many years has the Abbot lived on this mountain? The Master replied, "A dull bird nests in the reeds; a weary fish rests in the marsh."
[The monk] said, “In that case, you are a true man of the Way. The Master said, “Sit for a moment and drink some tea.
[The monk] asked, “What is Chaoshan? The Master said, “No corpses are left overnight. [The monk] asked, “What is it like to be a person of the mountains?
The Master said, “Planting red lotuses upon rocks. [The monk] asked, “What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, “Above all, avoid violating court protocol.”
A monk asked Chan Master Puming of Mount Puchong in Yizhou, "What is Buddha-nature? The Master said, "You have no Buddha-nature.
The monk said, "All sentient beings, even the crawling insects, possess Buddha-nature. Why is it that I, a student, do not have it? The Master said, "It is because you seek it outwardly.
The monk asked, "What is the pearl of the profound mystery? The Master said, "This is not it. The monk said, "If so..."
"What is this mysterious, dark pearl? The Master said, "It has been lost.
A monk asked Chan Master Yong of Liangjia Hermitage on Shuangquan Mountain in Suizhou, "What was the intent behind Bodhidharma’s nine years of facing the wall?
The Master said, "I could not sleep. The Master asked Elder Huguo, "In the region of Suiyang, as for men..."
The princesses each posed a question, and as each question was distinct, the Elder [Zhaozhou] responded to them individually. The Princess drew a single circle in the air with her hand.
The Master said, "I thank the Elder for your compassion. The Princess said, "I dare not. The Master lowered his head and did not look at her.
She asked, "What is it to suddenly bring all conditions to rest? The Master said, "Adding frost upon snow."
A monk asked Chan Master Chaowu of Baofu Monastery in Zhangzhou, "What is it like when a fish has not yet passed through the Dragon Gate?

The Master said, "Nurturing its nature in the deep pool. The monk asked, "What is it like when it has passed through? The Master said, "As soon as it ascends to the celestial heights, the multitudes find it difficult to follow.

The monk asked, "What is it like after it has ascended? The Master said, "Hanging clouds cover all; their moisture reaches the great thousandfold world. The monk asked, "Is there still [anyone who does not...]"?
The Master said, "There is. [The monk] asked, "What is it that does not receive moisture? The Master said, "A wooden stump directly supporting the great sun.
When the Venerable Fu of Taiyuan was first at Guangxiao Temple in Yangzhou, he was lecturing on the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*. There was a Chan practitioner who interrupted him.

Xue went to listen to a lecture. When he reached the section on the three causes, the Buddha-nature, and the Dharma-body of the three virtues, [the lecturer] spoke extensively on the subtle principles of the Dharma-body.

The Chan practitioner burst into laughter. After the lecture concluded, the Master invited the Chan practitioner to drink tea and said to him, "My own aspirations have always been narrow and inferior."

"I have been ridiculed for interpreting the meaning based on the literal text; I hope you will instruct me. The Chan practitioner said, "I truly laugh at you, Preceptor, for not recognizing the Dharma-body (*dharmakāya*).
The Master said, "In such an explanation, where is there anything that is not correct? He replied, "I ask the Preceptor to explain it once more.
The Master said, "The principle of the Dharma-body is like the great void: vertically it exhausts the three periods of time, and horizontally it spans the ten directions. It pervades...
It threads through the eight directions and encompasses the two polarities of heaven and earth; responding to conditions and meeting with stimuli, there is nowhere it does not pervade.

[The opponent] says, "It is not that the Master of the Seat is wrong in what he says; he simply speaks of matters concerning the limits of the *dharmakāya*. In truth, he has not yet realized the *dharmakāya* itself. The Master said:
"Since this is so, Zen Master, you should explain it to me. The Master asked, "Seat-Holder, do you believe it? The Master replied, "How could I dare not believe?
[The Zen Master] said, "If that is so, Seat-Holder, suspend your lectures for ten days. Within your room, sit upright in quiet meditation;
withdraw your mind and collect your thoughts, casting aside all conditions of good and evil at once. The Master followed these instructions exactly, from the first watch of the night until—

At the fifth watch, hearing the sound of the drum and horn, he suddenly attained realization. He went immediately to knock on the door. The Chan practitioner asked, "Who is it? The Master replied, "It is I.
The Chan practitioner scolded him, saying, "I have instructed you to transmit and uphold the Great Teaching and to preach the Dharma in place of the Buddha.

Why did you come home drunk last night and lie down in the street? The Master said, "Chan Master, I have been lecturing on the sutras all along; I have merely used the noses of my biological parents..."
Kong Niunie said, "From this day forward, I shall never again dare to act in such a manner. The Chan practitioner replied, "Go for now; we shall meet tomorrow.
The Master then ceased his lectures and traveled throughout all quarters, his fame spreading across the land. Once, while traveling through Zhejiang, he attended a Dharma assembly at Mount Jing.
One day, in front of the Great Buddha Hall, a monk asked him, "Have you ever been to Wutai? The Master—
The monk said, "I have been there. The Master asked, "Have you seen Mañjuśrī? The monk replied, "I have. The Master asked, "Where did you see him?
The monk replied, "I saw him before the Buddha Hall at Mount Jing. Later, when this monk traveled to Minchuan, he related this incident to Xuefeng.

Xuefeng said, "Why did you not tell him to come over the mountain pass? Upon hearing this, the Master packed his bags and set out. When he first arrived at Xuefeng, he stayed to rest his staff at the guest house. Because of this—
[The Master] was dividing tangerines with the monks. Changqing asked, "Where did you bring these from? The Master said, "From beyond the ridges.

Changqing said, "It must have been difficult to travel such a long distance; how did you manage to carry them here? The Master said, "Tangerines, tangerines. The next day he went up the mountain. When Xuefeng heard of this, he assembled the community.
Upon arriving at the Dharma Hall, the Master looked around at Xuefeng and then went down to oversee the administrative affairs. The following day—
He went back up and bowed, saying, "I offended you, Master, yesterday. Feng said, "Since you know it was such a matter, let it be.
One day, seeing the Master, Feng pointed at the sun and showed it to him. The Master shook his hand and walked out. Feng said, "Do you not agree with me?
The Master replied, "When you, Master, shake your head, I wag my tail. Where is there any disagreement? Feng [laughed].
[The Master] said, "In every place, one must conceal [the truth]. One day, during the evening assembly, Feng was lying in the central courtyard.
The Master said, "Within the jurisdiction of the Five Prefectures, there is only this old monk who is slightly superior. Feng then rose and departed.
Feng once asked the Master, "I have heard it said that Linji has three phrases; is this true? The Master said, "Yes. [Feng] asked, "What is the first?"
The Master raised his eyes and looked at him. Fēng said, "This is still the second phrase. What is the first phrase? The Master folded his hands and withdrew.
From this time on, Xuěfēng held him in deep esteem; within the teaching hall, they attained mutual understanding, and the way of master and disciple was in perfect accord.
He no longer traveled elsewhere, but remained there to attend to the bathhouse. One day, Xuansha went up to pay his respects to Xuefeng.
Xuefeng said, "There is a little mouse here; it is currently in the bathhouse. Xuansha said, "I shall wait to examine it for you, Master.
Having finished speaking, he went to the bathhouse and encountered the Master (Yunmen) pouring water. Xuansha said, "I have come to visit the Abbot. The Master replied, "We have already met."
The monk said, "In what kalpa did we ever meet? The Master said, "Why do you sleep so much?
The monk then entered the abbot’s quarters and told Xuebafeng, "I have already scrutinized him. Feng asked, "How did you scrutinize him? The monk recounted the previous conversation.
Feng said, "You have been robbed by a thief! Gushan asked the Master, "Before one's parents were born, where was the nose?"
The Master said, "Elder brother, you go first. Guishan said, "I am alive right now; where do you say it is? The Master did not approve.
Guishan then asked, "How about that? The Master said, "Bring me the fan in your hand. Guishan gave him the fan and again questioned him on the previous statement.
The Master shook the fan and did not respond. Guishan, unable to fathom this, struck the Master with a single punch. Guishan then went to Daguang Mountain.
The King invited him. When Xuefeng sent him back to the Dharma Hall, he said, "A single arrow of the Sage has shot straight into the nine-layered city.
The Master said, "He is not yet there. Xuefeng said, "He is a man who has reached the very bottom.
The Master said, "If you do not believe me, wait until I go and examine him myself. He then pursued him halfway and asked, "Elder brother, where did you go?"
The Master asked, "Where do you go? Mount said, "I am going into the nine-layered city. The Master said, "What if you suddenly encounter the three armies surrounding you?
Mount said, "He has his own path that reaches through the heavens. The Master said, "In that case, you have left the palace and lost the hall."
Shan said, "Where would he not be called Honored One? The Master shook his sleeves and turned back. Feng asked, "How was that?
The Master said, "A fine holy arrow; it was broken mid-flight. He then recounted the previous conversation. Feng said, "The fellow's words remain.
The Master said, "This old frozen lump still has a trace of local sentiment. The Master stood before the storehouse when a monk asked, "What about this?"

Nanyue Banruo Weijin Baowen Chan Master was a native of Fuzhou. He studied under Xuefeng and befriended Xuansha; he had penetrated the profound mysteries.
One day he asked Upāsaka Jian, "I have heard that you have written a commentary on the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*; is this true? Jian replied:
"I dare not," [the monk] replied. The Master asked, "How would you annotate the two Mañjuśrīs? He said, "I beg the Master to examine it. The Master then raised his sleeves and departed.
The Master once continued the *Baolin Zhuan* (Record of the Baolin Temple) in four fascicles, recording the lineages and sources of the Chan school from after the Zhengyuan era onward.
He also separately authored the *Nanyue Gaoseng Zhuan* (Biographies of Eminent Monks of Nanyue), both of which circulate in the world today.
A monk asked Chan Master Zhiyuan Xianjiao of Baimiao in Anzhou, a Dharma heir of Chan Master Tanziguoshen: "Who transmits the mind-seal of all Buddhas?"
The Master said, “Master Bodhidharma. [The monk] asked, “How was it that he was able to transmit [the Dharma]? The Master said, “Tell me, who was it that transmitted it?
[The monk] asked, “What is the direct, single path? The Master said, “Cut it off. [The monk] asked, “What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, “Suffering. [The monk] asked, “What is the Way? The Master said, “Universal. [The monk] asked, “What is the student’s own self? The Master said, “It is right here.”
The Master said, “Lost. [The monk] asked, “What is it to have attained such that there are no mountains, rivers, or the great earth? The Master said, “Not giving rise to views.

Chan Master Guicheng of Luohan Monastery in Zhangzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Xuansha Shibei. He was the son of the Li family of Changshan. While still a child, he ate only one vegetarian meal per day and his speech was extraordinary.
Upon reaching adulthood, he entered the service of Great Master Wuxiang at Wansui Temple in his native prefecture and donned the monastic robes.
Xue Deng studied the Vinaya and ascended the platform one day to proclaim the *Prātimokṣa* for the assembly. Having completed the recitation of the precepts, he said:
"To uphold the precepts is merely to discipline the body; it is not true liberation. To rely on the literal text to form an interpretation—how could that awaken noble wisdom?
Thereupon, he sought out the Southern School. He first visited Yunju and Xuefeng, where he questioned them with diligent devotion, yet he still had not attained realization.

Later, he visited Xuansha. A single word from the Master triggered an awakening; his mind was vast and free of delusion. Xuansha asked, "The three realms are mind-only—how do you understand this? The Master pointed to a chair and said, "What does the Master call this? Xuansha replied, "A chair. The Master said, "Then the Master does not understand that the three realms are mind-only. Xuansha said, "I call this a bamboo-and-wood object; what do you call it? The Master replied, "I call it a chair. Xuansha said, "If you call it a chair, then why did you say the Master does not understand that the three realms are mind-only? The Master said, "It is because you call it bamboo-and-wood that I call it a chair. Xuansha laughed and said, "You have truly attained the Way. He then had him serve as the head monk. Later, when the Master was traveling through the region of Fuzhou, he stayed at the residence of a layman. The layman’s wife, who was a woman of great virtue, invited him for tea. She asked, "Master, you were once called the 'Dharma Jewel of the South. Is there still such a person today? The Master replied, "There is. She asked, "Who is he? The Master said, "He is right here in front of you. She then asked about the meaning of "the three realms are mind-only. The Master said, "When you see the flowers blooming in the garden, do you see them or not? She said, "I see them. The Master said, "If you see them, then they are mind-only. She then asked about the meaning of "the ten thousand dharmas are but one mind. The Master said, "When you hear the sound of the wind in the pines, do you hear it or not? She said, "I hear it. The Master said, "If you hear it, then it is mind-only. The woman bowed deeply and said, "I have been living in the world for over forty years, yet I have never heard such a teaching. The Master then composed a verse for her: "The myriad forms are all within the mind; The ten thousand sounds are but the nature of hearing. If you can perceive them as neither coming nor going, Then the ten directions are all the Buddha-dharma. She further requested a name for her residence. [The monk] said, "Throughout the entire world, one cannot find a single person who understands the Buddha-dharma. From that time on, the Master redoubled his efforts to encourage him.

Whenever Sha induced and guided students, causing various samādhis to flow forth, he always charged the Master with assisting in their development. Although the Master remained among the assembly, concealing his brilliance, yet...
His reputation spread far and wide. At that time, Wang Gong, the Governor of Zhangzhou, built a vihāra named Dizang and invited the Master to expound the Dharma.
Once, while the Master was planting rice in the fields, he saw a monk and asked him, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Nanzhou. The Master said, "How is the Buddha-dharma there?
The monk replied, "It is a matter of endless debate and discussion. The Master said, "How can that compare to my place here, where we plow the fields to earn our food?"
[The monk] said, "But what about the three realms? The Master said, "What do you call 'the three realms'?
He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? [The monk] said, "From the South. The Master said, "What words or phrases did the teachers there use to instruct their disciples?
[The monk] said, "They say that although gold dust is precious, it cannot enter the eye. The Master said, "I say that Mount Sumeru is in your eye. One day—
Zhongta was serving as an attendant to Xuansha. Xuansha struck Zhongta with a staff and said, "Is this the name, or is it the essence?
Zhongta did not respond. Xuansha then asked the Master, "How do you understand this? The Master said, "This monk received a blow from the staff and does not know its origin."
The monk reported, "Baofu has already passed away. The Master said, "Now that Baofu has passed away, Dizang shall enter his stupa.
(A monk asked Fayan, "What was the meaning of the ancients? Fayan said, "Heaven! Heaven! Later, he moved to Lohan Temple and extensively expounded upon the profound essentials.

He ascended the hall and said: "The mysterious and wondrous of our school—is it simply like this? Or is there something else extraordinary? If there is something else extraordinary, you should bring it forward."
Look here: if there were no "going," one could not take these two characters and treat them as the very vehicle of the school (zongcheng).

What are these two characters? They are the "vehicle of the school" (zongcheng) and the "vehicle of the teachings" (jiaocheng). As soon as you speak of the vehicle of the school, it becomes the vehicle of the school;

as soon as you speak of the vehicle of the teachings, it becomes the vehicle of the teachings. O Zen masters, the vehicle of the Buddha-dharma has, from the beginning, been established by your own mouths.
To establish names and designations, and to engage in grasping and verbalizing, is precisely this. In an instant, one speaks here of the "level" and the "real," of the "perfect" and the "permanent.
O Zen masters, what do you call the level and the real? What do you take to be the perfect and the permanent? Having traveled on pilgrimage to other houses, you ought to distinguish these principles;
do not allow yourselves to be buried by them. Do not merely store some fragments of sound, form, names, and designations within your hearts.
[The Master] said, "Head! You say you understand and that you are well able to discern. But what exactly do you understand? What exactly do you discern?
That which is retained in memory is merely names; that which is discerned is merely sounds and forms. If it were not these sounds, forms, names, and words..."
How do you further maintain and discern this? The wind blowing through the pine trees is sound;
the croaking of a frog or the cawing of an old crow is also sound. Why not listen there and make your selection?
If you have some conceptual framework or mental image regarding that, then as for the Master’s own words—how much conceptualization is there? Do not mistake them, Upādhyāya. Thus it is said:
Now, these sounds and forms resound vibrantly. Do they reach you or not?
If they do reach you, then your numinous nature, the adamantine secret, must undergo destruction and departure. Why is this so? Because sound penetrates and shatters your ears.
Form pierces through your eyes; the causal conditions immediately block them up. Illusory delusions run about and kill you. Sound and form are such in their essence that they cannot be contained.
If they do not reach you, from where else could sound and form come? Do you understand? Try to discern for yourself whether they reach you or do not reach you.
A short while later, it is said again: "This is perfect, eternal, level, and real. What kind of person is it that acts thus?

"What do you say? You are not yet a man from a village of the Huangyi barbarians who understands how to speak like this. It was those ancient sages, being somewhat unconventional, who assisted and manifested [the truth] for one another.
People of the present day fail to recognize what is good and what is evil; they immediately settle upon 'perfection' and claim, 'I have a distinct lineage and a profound, mysterious teaching.
They would say that Śākyamuni Buddha had no tongue and was not worth a fraction of you. Thus they pat their own chests with pride. But if we were to discuss it—"
The sins of killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct, though grave, are still light; they still have a time of cessation.

But this slander of the Prajñāpāramitā blinds the eyes of sentient beings, causing them to enter the Avīci Hell and swallow iron balls—do not treat this as a trivial matter. Therefore, the ancients said:
"The fault lies with the master who transformed you; it is none of your business. Take care. A monk asked, "What is the single phrase of an Arhat?
The Master said, "If I were to speak it to you, it would immediately become two phrases. The monk asked, "If someone who does not understand comes, will you still receive him?
The Master said, "Who is it that does not understand? The monk said, "You have already spoken just now. The Master said, "Are you not merely disheartening yourself?"
A monk from Baofu arrived. The Master asked, "How is the Buddha-dharma there? He replied, "At times he addresses the assembly, saying:
'I block your eyes so that you cannot see; I block your ears so that you cannot hear; I sit upon your mind.'"
[The Master] said, "I cannot teach you how to discern it. The Master asked, "I am not blocking your eyes; what do you see? I am not blocking your ears;
what do you hear? I am not sitting upon your mind; how do you discern it? (Dongchan Qi said:

"Upon hearing this, that monk suddenly attained realization and never traveled elsewhere again. Do you, Venerable One, understand now? If you do not, what is it that you see every day? He asked: "The character 'yi' (以) is not formed; the character 'ba' (八) is not..."
"Yes. [The student] asked, "I do not yet understand what these characters mean. The Master said, "Do you truly not understand?
He replied, "I truly do not understand. The Master said, "Look at the footnote below. [The student] asked, "What is the right livelihood for a śramaṇa? The Master said, "Can you eat it?
He asked, "If I wish to eat this food, what skillful means should I employ? The Master said, "Stuff your mouth shut. [The student] asked, "What about... (The text ends here).
"This is the tradition of my lineage," the Master said. The monk asked, "Did you not tell me? The Master replied, "Why do you ask why I did not tell you?
This is the tradition of my lineage. The monk asked, "What is the body of the Dharma King? The Master said, "What kind of body are you right now?
The monk said, "In that case, there is no body. The Master said, "How painful! He ascended the hall. As soon as he sat down, two monks prostrated themselves at once.
[The student] prostrated. The Master said, "Both are wrong. [The student] asked, "What is the phrase that cannot be broken? The Master said, "Break it!

[The student] asked, "When a Buddha appears in the world, he does so for the sake of all sentient beings. For what purpose do you, O Master, appear today? The Master said, "Where have you encountered a Buddha?
[The student] said, "If that is so, then the fault is mine. The Master said, "Be careful to withdraw. [The student] asked, "What are the various sages?"
[The Master] said, "The profound principle is that the four corners lie flat on the ground. [The student] asked, "When one is unwilling to acknowledge the Great Matter, what then?
The Master said, "It depends on you. [The student] asked, "What is the eye of the ten directions? The Master said, "Blink your eyebrows and see.

[The student] invited Baofu for a meal and sent someone to deliver a message, saying, "I request the Master’s compassion to deign to accept my invitation. Baofu said, "For whom would there be compassion? The Master said, "For the one who..."
Yet to speak thus is entirely lacking in compassion. While enjoying the moon, he said, "The clouds move;
it will rain. A monk said, "It is not the clouds that move; it is the wind that moves. The Master said, "I say that neither the clouds move nor does the wind move.
The monk asked, "But earlier, Master, you said the clouds moved. The Master replied, "Who is at fault? The Master saw a monk and raised [this case].
The Master said, "Do you understand? A monk replied, 'I thank the Master for his compassion in showing this to me.
The Master said, 'When you see me raise my whisk, you say I am showing it to you. Every day you see mountains and rivers—do they not show themselves to you?
Furthermore, when a monk comes and I raise my whisk, that monk praises it and prostrates. When he sees me raise my whisk, he simply prostrates.'"
He prostrated and offered praise. [The Master] swept the floor and set down his broom. Why did he not offer praise? Question:
The teachings state, "If one sees that all marks are no-marks, one sees the Tathāgata. What is meant by "no-mark"? Master: "A lantern. Question:
"What is leaving the household life? Master: "Whom do you call a master? Question: [Addressing a monk,] "Where have you come from?"
[The Master] said, "Qinzhou. The monk replied, "What object have you brought? [The Master] said, "I have brought no object.
The Master said, "Why do you speak falsely before the assembly? The monk had no reply. The Master then asked, "Does Qinzhou not produce songbirds?

"Please, Master, speak. The Master said, "How will you ask? [The student] asked, "When many hands sift gold together, who is it that obtains it?

The Master said, "Raising a hand across a thousand miles; cease your efforts and look as you please. [The student] asked, "The flowers are exquisite by the flying peaks; what is the matter before the Terrace of the Immortal Realm?

Chan Master Daohui of Shengshan Bailong Monastery in Fuzhou was a native of that province. He ascended the hall and said:
"Without even lifting a foot, who is it whose majestic light shines? Do you understand? If you say, 'The place where I go is inherently thus,' then I am glad there is no connection at all.

[The student] said, "I am merely deaf, and my eyesight is also dim. He asked, "When the mind is forgotten and the body is merged, what is it like?
The Master said, "What else do you see in your dreams? He asked, "I, a student, wish to pose a question; I beg the Master to judge it. The Master said, "I will not judge.

[The student] asked, "Why will you not judge? The Master said, "You must know that I am a master craftsman. He asked, "The great assembly has gathered like clouds; I request the Master to proclaim the essence of our school."
The student said, "I have encountered few listeners; my questions do not even touch the edge of the lips. I beg the Master for instruction.

The Master said, "Bring forth a question that does not touch the edge of the lips. The student said, "If it is so, then all living beings will have something to rely upon. The Master said, "Do not engage in idle talk.

The student asked, "Please, Master, answer with a response born of the vital mechanism (*shengji*). The Master said, "Bring paper and brush; I shall write it down for you to take away. The student asked, "What is [it]?"

Chan Master Huizhou Jizhao of Anguo Monastery in Fuzhou (also known as Zhongta) was a native of Putian in Quanzhou.
He was foremost among those who sought instruction within the quarters of Xuansha. Once, he asked, "What is the primary moon? Xuansha replied, "What would you do with that moon of yours?
From this, the Master attained realization. In the second year of the Kaiping era of the Liang dynasty, when Xuansha was about to pass away, the Military Governor of Min...
The Wang family sent their son to inquire after his illness and requested that he secretly reveal who would succeed him in preaching the Dharma. The Shanzhao said, "Qiuzi shall obtain it.
King Wenyi silently took note of this final instruction and then asked Drum Mountain (Gushan) who was fit to hold the seat of the Dharma at Wolong.
Drum Mountain named twelve venerable elders from the city who possessed the full eye of the Dharma; all were capable of appearing in the world [to teach]. King Wenyi likewise...
He remained silent. On the day of the opening of the hall, when the officials and the monastics had assembled at the Dharma feast, the King suddenly asked the assembly, "Who is the Venerable Qiú?
Thereupon, the people pointed out the Master. The Wang family then invited him to ascend the seat. After a long silence, the Master said:
"Do not disdain this solitude; do not say it is unworthy. Since its limits are not yet fully understood, how can one attempt to deliberate upon it?"
I usually employ its resonance, merely striking it once or twice to assist others in triggering their realization.

To speak of it in terms of its origin, one could not find a single person in the worlds of the ten directions who could serve as my companion. A monk asked, "By what skillful means does one enter directly into the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, "Entering is itself the skillful means. The monk asked, "From which mountain does the cloud arise? From which ravine does the wind come?"

[The Master] said, "Exerting all one's effort in practice does not depart from the central stupa. He ascended the hall and said, "The circumstances of the rice gruel and meals here are for you, brothers, to proclaim;
yet in the end, they are not permanent. If you wish to attain what is essential and concise, it is rather this: the mountains, rivers, and the great earth shall reveal the Way to you.
Since that Way is eternal, it can also lead to ultimate realization. If you enter through the gate of Mañjuśrī, then all..."
The unconditioned—earth, wood, tiles, and rubble—assist you in triggering the catalyst.

If you enter through the gate of Avalokiteśvara, all sounds and voices—even those of frogs and earthworms—assist you in triggering the catalyst. If you enter through the gate of Samantabhadra, you arrive without moving a step.
These three gates of skillful means are shown to you, like using a single broken chopstick to stir the waters of the great ocean.

Those fish and dragons know that water is their life. Do you understand? If one lacks the eye of wisdom to examine this with discernment, no matter how many hundreds of clever and ingenious methods you employ, they will not lead to the ultimate realization.
A student asked, "I have recently entered the monastery groves, yet I do not understand my own fundamental matter. I beg the Master for instruction.
The Master pointed with his staff and said, "Do you understand? The student replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "I have done so much for you."

Yet this results in suppressing and demeaning others. Do you understand? If we speak from the perspective of one's own fundamental reality, it has never been lacking—whether for those newly entering the monastic community or for the Buddhas of the past. It is like the waters of the great ocean:
from the moment they are first born until their death in old age, all fish and dragons receive an equal share of water to use. This is the unerring, true source.
"Please speak the truth, Master. The Master said, "You speak for me. [The monk] asked, "What if there were someone who could not discern it?
The Master said, "Wait until such a person comes. [The monk] asked, "Do all Buddhas have a teacher? The Master said, "They do.

[The monk] asked, "Who is the teacher of all Buddhas? The Master said, "No one can recognize him. One day, having ascended the hall, the Master remained silent for a long while. A monk came forward and prostrated.
The Master said, "Do not let the skull be crushed. A monk came forward to inquire, saying, "Setting aside your attendants, I request to see you directly.
The Master said, "Try to see by raising your eyebrows. The monk asked, "What about when it is not like this? The Master said, "He has gone to the north of the mountain."

The Master said, "There is a 'sage-measure' (ārya-pramāṇa) present. [The student] asked, "For whom is this measure intended? The Master said, "It is not for the sake of sages."
Chan Master Mingfa of Luofeng in Fuzhou ascended the hall and said: "Every person is fully endowed with it; every person manifests it.
How can one blame this mountain monk? Take care! A monk asked: "The mark of the extinction of all dharmas cannot be proclaimed in words.
What is the mark of extinction? The Master said: "Question and answer are both complete. The monk said: "If that is so, then the *tathatā* dharma-realm has no..."
"There is no other. The Master said, "This merely causes people to grieve. Question: "How was it before Niutou had seen the Fourth Patriarch?
The Master said, "His virtue was so profound that ghosts and spirits revered him. Question: "How was it after he saw him? The Master said, "His entire being is holy and unfathomable.
Question: "What is the single phrase of Luofeng? The Master said, "Suffering. Question: "Who is the person of original nature? The Master said, "Lamentable."
"How sorrowful that the realm of pines and vines is so perilous.

He said, "I have lived in the mountains for thirty years and have gained their strength. At that time, a monk asked, "Master, what kind of strength have you gained from them?
The Master said, "Crossing streams and crossing ridges; leaning eastward and leaning westward. (Zhaqing said, "I do not speak in this way. The monk asked, "How would you speak, Master?")
[He] rejoiced [at this], using his staff to support himself as he walked along the ground).

It is like the three thousand great thousandfold worlds, with their suns, moons, stars, and constellations, and their rivers—the Yangtze, the Yellow, the Huai, and the Ji. All...
Sentient beings enter from one pore into another pore; yet the pores do not become smaller, nor do the worlds become larger.
The sentient beings therein neither perceive nor know this. To make it easy to understand: even you, O Venerable One, do not know this in your daily life.

The hermit Qirú of Mount Dàzhāng in Fúzhōu was a native of that province. From youth, he harbored solitary integrity and resolved to explore the Way of the Patriarchs.
He entered the chamber of Xuánshā and attained an acute realization of its profound principles. Xuánshā recorded, saying: "Your Zen is already of a transcendent caliber."
Later, he did not even have a single person to attend him. From that time on, the Master no longer sought to gather disciples nor maintain young attendants.
He lived in seclusion on Mount Xiaojie, hollowing out a large, rotten cedar tree to serve as a small hermitage, barely enough space for his own body.

Whenever traveling monks arrived, he would respond to their inquiries as they came, without providing any fixed or formal instruction. A monk asked, "When birth and death arrive, how can one evade them?"
The Master said, "When the tally arrives, it is executed. The monk asked, "If that is so, then one will be taken away by birth and death. The Master said, "A-ya! A-ya!
The monk asked, "What is the meaning of holding the mendicant’s staff in the Western Heaven? The Master picked up his staff, struck the ground with it, and shook it.
The monk asked, "I do not yet understand what this signifies. The Master said, "This is Zhang’s beating. As the monk was about to offer further words, [the Master struck him].
The Master struck him with his staff. A monk asked Yun Tai Qin: "What is the true word? Qin replied, "Namo Buddhāya. The Master said instead, "How? How?
The two elders, Qing Huo and Chong Xu, had long heard the Master’s reputation but had never met him.
One day they went to visit him together and happened upon him gathering chestnuts. Qing Huo asked, "How is it, Master? [The Master replied,] "Like a hermitage."
"Where is the Master? The Master asked, "From where have you come? He replied, "From down the mountain. The Master asked, "How did you manage to get here?
He replied, "What place is this? The Master gestured for him to sit and said, "Go and have some tea down there."

The two officials went to visit this master. Upon arriving at his hermitage, they were deeply moved by his lofty discourse. Sitting together with him to the left and right, they did not realize that night had fallen.

Suddenly, they saw wolves and tigers rushing toward the front of the hermitage, yet they naturally circled around him in a state of docility. Thereupon, Huo composed a poem, saying: "His journey is no ordinary journey;
Who knows the sentiment of his coming and going? A single meal remains unsated, Yet ten thousand households find no peace in living. It was not... [The text ends here.]
The Way is difficult to subdue; an empty fist cannot contend with it. Where the dragon roars and clouds arise, he lets out two or three leisurely cries.
The two masters sought him out at Dazhang Mountain and established a hermitage, inviting the Master to reside there. Sitting alone in both locations for fifty-two years, he passed away.
On the day Chan Master Yongxing Shenlu of Mount Lianhua in Fuzhou was invited by the King of Min to open the hall for formal instruction, before ascending the seat, he first stood before it and said:
"Great King and assembly, listen! There has already been a true and authentic proclamation.

Only then did he ascend the seat. A monk asked, "The Great King has invited the Master to appear in this world; I do not yet understand—how does this assembly today compare to that at Vulture Peak?
The Master said, "It penetrates the past and transmits to the present. The monk asked, "What is the Master’s house style?
The Master said, "Within a single hair-tip, the myriad lands are revealed; the sun and moon appear therein."
When the Venerable Master Jing of Tiantai Guoqing Temple first encountered Xuansha, who was addressing the assembly, saying:
"If you all can for a single lifetime act as if you had lost your parents, I guarantee that you will attain thorough penetration. Jing followed up on these words and asked:
"Just as it is said in the teachings: 'One must not use the mind of known objects to fathom the unsurpassed wisdom and vision of the Tathāgata.
But how about this? [Zhao]zhou] Sha said: 'If you say you have thoroughly investigated the mind of known objects to its very bottom, can you still fathom it? "
After the Master entered the faith, he resided at Tiantai for over thirty years without descending from the mountain. He mastered the three studies (śikṣā) and his conduct was solitary and peerless.
Beyond his practice of meditative stillness, he constantly perused the Dragon Canon (the Buddhist scriptures). He was held in high esteem by those both far and near, who called him the "Elder Dajing.
Once someone asked him: "Disciple, whenever I sit in meditation at night, my thoughts fly about; I do not yet understand how to subdue them."
"Regarding this method, I pray that you will deign to grant me instruction. The Master said: "Suppose, while sitting at ease during the quiet of night, your thoughts fly about in confusion.
Take this very mind that is flying about and investigate the place from which it flies. When you investigate and find no place, then where does the thought of 'flying about' exist?
Turn back and investigate the investigating mind itself; then where is the mind that is able to investigate? Furthermore, the wisdom that can illuminate is fundamentally empty."
The objects of conditions are also quiescent. That which is quiescent yet not quiescent is because there is no person capable of bringing about quiescence.

That which illuminates yet does not illuminate is because there is no object to be illuminated. When both object and wisdom are quiescent, the mind and its deliberations are at ease. One does not seek out branches externally, nor does one dwell in meditative concentration internally.
When these two paths are both extinguished, the single nature is serene. This is the essential path for returning to the source.
The Master, having observed the meaning of "illusion" (*māyā*) within the teachings, composed a verse and asked the assembly of students:

"If all dharmas are like illusions, then one who commits various transgressions and evils should incur no blame. Why is it that the karma one has created is not forgotten, such that one must rely on the Buddha’s compassion to provide guidance and conversion?
At that time, the Elder Xiaojing replied: "An illusory person creates an illusion; the illusory wheel of protection (*cakravāḍa*)."

Illusion: karma can summon illusion; that which is to be remedied is the failure to understand. Illusion gives rise to various illusions; the realization of suffering is like an illusion, for illusion is unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*).
