The King said, "From where would one obtain such a mind? The Master said, "How could there be one who is without mind? The King said, "What of that which lies beyond? The Master said, "Please ask about that which lies beyond. The King said, "The Great Master may deceive others, but he cannot deceive me. The Master asked, "Great King, what is it? The King said, "I do not know. The Master said, "If you do not know, then why did you say earlier that you have no mind? The King said, "I am not deceiving you; I truly do not know. The Master said, "If you do not know, then how can you say you have no mind? If you do not know, then you are not without mind. This 'not knowing' is precisely the Buddha-mind. If you can realize this 'not knowing,' then you will see the Buddha-mind. The King was greatly enlightened. He bowed and withdrew. The Master then addressed the assembly, saying, "The Great King has attained the Way. He then composed a verse: "The Great King has attained the Way; He has realized the Buddha-mind. The myriad phenomena are all the Buddha; The ten directions are entirely the Way. The ten thousand dharmas are originally empty; The three realms are fundamentally still. The Dharma-body is vast and boundless; The True Mind is eternally bright. The Master then asked the King, "The sun varies in its appearance by a thousand differences each day—what
The assembly gathered in great numbers and requested that the Master expound the Dharma. The Master said, "How many more are there who have not yet heard it?
They replied, "If that is so, then it does not depend on coming up here. The Master said, "Even if you do not come up, let us set that aside for now; where do you understand it from?

He replied, "If there were a specific place [from which to understand], I would be failing the Master. The Master said, "I only fear you cannot distinguish the refined from the coarse. [He] asked about the nature of discourse.
"As for the Dharma, it should be taught according to the Dharma. What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "What doubt or error is there? Question:
"What was the intent behind the ancients facing the wall? The Master struck him. Question: "Without relying on verbal explanations, I ask the Master to speak directly. The Master said:
Why must one wait further for deliberation?
Chan Master Shaozong Yuanzhi of Kaixian Temple on Mount Lu was a native of Gusu.

When the Prince of Jiangnan visited Hongjing, he entered the mountain to pay his respects and requested the Master to ascend the hall. He instructed a monk to ask: "What is the environment of Kaixian? The Master [responded].
[The Master] said, "The very best is this one line: 'It divides the color of the green mountains. [The Emperor] asked, "What is it like to be a person within the realm?

The Master replied, "Gathering withered firewood to boil mountain water. The National Lord’s respect increased all the more. Later, he passed away at his home mountain, where a spirit-stupa remains to this day.
Chan Master Fatao Zongyi of Qinxin Temple in Hangzhou ascended the hall. After a long silence, he said: "The assembly has not even waited for a single word;
they have already returned to their quarters. Is there anyone capable of continuing this ancestral style?
Is there anyone who can answer this question? If someone can answer it here, I shall join you all in laughter. If no one can answer..."
[The Master] said, “Yes. All people here would laugh at you as strange. Take care. A monk asked, “How can one be plain and honest to avoid seeing empty pretenses?
The Master said, “If your question were appropriate, everyone present would see through it. [The monk] said, “There are those who come with such [understanding], yet they are all not true men.”
"If one does not come in such a manner, is there still a possibility of inheriting the ancestral wind? The Master said, "Come forth with a question that brings out both ends.
[The monk] asked, "Who can discern this? The Master said, "A Persian raising a child.

[The monk] asked, "I beg the Master for a full demonstration regarding the destination of the Buddha-dharma. The Master said, "Just bring forth a complete question. [The monk] asked, "Why then do you pick it up [and set it aside]?"
[The student] asked about "going. The Master said, "What was it you were asking just now? [The student] said, "Had I not met the Master, I would have nearly fallen into wandering confusion.
The Master said, "The gate is shut after the thief has gone. [The student] asked, "How should one deliver the single phrase of the separate transmission?
The Master said, "It is truly a pity. [The student] said, "In that case, even a separate recompense would not be appropriate. The Master said, "That too is idle talk. [The student] asked.
"What is it to be a person who does not court the Son of Heaven and does not envy kings and lords?

The Master said: "Every day, three threads; for many years, a single robe. [The student] asked: "I do not yet know whether such a person can truly carry on the ancestral wind. The Master said: "A magpie comes and speaks upon one's head;
clouds fly before one's eyes. [The student] asked: "I have heard an ancient saying: 'Do not sever afflictions. What is the meaning of this?"

"What? the Master asked. [The monk] replied, "It is also that which incites the karma of a person. [The Master] asked, "How can one avoid inciting karma? The Master said, "Your words have fallen into error.
[The monk] asked, "I request you to dispense praise and punishment. What is the 'Blow-off-its-Sheath Sword'? The Master said, "Perform three prostrations according to the Dharma.
Later, the Master resided at Longce Temple and passed away in peace.
Chan Master Hongyan of Fuzhou Shuilu Monastery ascended the hall.

When the assembly had settled, the Master descended from his seat, took up the incense burner, and walked before the congregation, saying, "I offer this to the Buddhas of the ten directions," and then returned to his quarters.

A monk asked, "Setting aside the hundred negations and the four propositions, I ask the Master to exert his full strength and provide the essential framework. The Master replied, "Where does it fall?"
[The monk] said, "If that is so, then humans and devas will have someone to rely upon. The Master said, "Do not pour foul water on others.
Chan Master Xianze of Guangyan Monastery at Lingyin Mountain in Hangzhou first visited Baofu.
Baofu asked, "What is your name? The Master replied, "Xianze. Baofu said, "What would you do if you encountered a place that was parched and dry? The Master replied, "Who is parched?"
Hedu asked, "Is it I? Fufu said, "It is I. The Master said, "Preceptor, do not deceive people. Fufu said, "In fact, it is you who are deceiving me.
Later, the Master received the seal of transmission from Changqing and resided at the Guangyan Dojo (now the Fa'an Monastery). A monk asked, "What is the matter presented face-to-face?
The Master descended from his meditation seat and said, "I humbly wish that your honorable personage enjoys ten thousand blessings in your daily life. [The monk] asked again.
"Who is it that dwells as a companion to the myriad dharmas? The Master said, "The Green History Tower within the city; the high peak pagoda beyond the clouds.
[The monk] asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "The spring water in the secluded ravine is clear; the moon atop the high peak is white."
Question: "What is the house style of Guangyan? The Master said: "A grove of white clouds and three thatched huts. Question: "Ultimately, what is it? The Master said:
"Since there is no *vinaya-dhara*, there is also a shortage of *karmadāna*. Question: "What is the house style of Guangyan?
The Master said: "The numinous waters resound before Lion Rock; the white monkeys cry atop Chicken Cage Mountain."
Chan Master Huilang of Baoci Monastery in Fuzhou ascended the hall and said: "The sages of all generations have appeared in the world for the sake of the one great cause and condition.
They have passed this down to one another in mutual proclamation. Do you all understand? If you do not understand, it will not be easy.
A monk asked, "What is the one great cause? The Master said, "Do not misunderstand what has been proclaimed!"
[The student] said, "If that is so, then I have no doubts. The Master said, "How can you say that? There is still a speck in your eye.
[The student] asked, "The Buddhas of the three periods of time are all merely messengers; I wonder whose words they are transmitting? The Master said, "Listen.
[The student] asked, "I do not yet know what kind of words these are. The Master said, "You are not Zhong Qi. [The student] asked, "What is the student’s eye? The Master said:
"One must not scatter sand again. A monk asked Chan Master Changqing Changhui of Fuzhou: "The Prince has requested an audience; the Dharma heir of Yishan spoke words that lock the mouth.
I ask the Master to verify this is not in error. The Master said, "It is so. The monk said, "If that is so, then I deeply appreciate your kindness. The Master said, "Do not."
"An ordinary person is good at setting things aside. When asked, they do not violate the ancestral style, nor do they harm the meaning of things.

I ask the Master to speak from the fullness of his mouth. The Master said, "Is this not today the opening of the hall? The questioner asked, "The flame continues from Xuefeng; the seal is transmitted from Chaojue.

Not contradicting things and not failing people—this is not a matter of being 'at the head' (the immediate point). What do you say now? The Master said, "Contradiction and failure are themselves the Way. The questioner said, "If that is so..."
"In that case, you have well matched my previous words; the shallow and the deep have already been distinguished. The Master said, "Yet you must still recognize what is good and what is evil.
Chan Master Jing of Shifoyuan in Fuzhou ascended the hall and said: "If one says that the natural face is presented, it is as if adding rouge and powder."
Even setting aside the fault of redundancy, there is still a burden of contradiction. How, then, do you all understand this? A monk asked, "I, a student, wish to see the Master’s original face.
The Master said, "Dongshan has words; take it up directly. The monk said, "If that is so, then I cannot see it.
The Master said, "It is indeed so. The traveler's road is as vast as heaven; the lord's gate is as deep as the sea."

Chan Master Qinghuan of Zhenfeng Guanyin Monastery in Fuzhou ascended the hall and said: "Virtuous Chan practitioners, if you wish to discuss Chan, speak of the Way, or proclaim the ancestral style, consider this:
within the very sphere of each person, upon a single hair-tip there are immeasurable Buddhas turning the Great Dharma Wheel;
within a single mote of dust, the Jewel-King Lands appear. The Buddha speaks of sentient beings; he speaks of mountains."
The great earth and the rivers were spoken of all at once, never interrupted, like King Vaiśravaṇa who from beginning to end never sought external treasures.
Since each already possesses such a family tradition, who is lacking anything? It is not possible to seek further from others for a resolution.
A monk asked, "What is the nature of the Dharma-realm? The Master said, "Within your own body are the ten thousand phenomena. [The monk] asked, "How is this so?"
"Realizing the essence. The Master said: "The empty valley seeks sound to further investigate the beginning and the end.
Chan Master Chien-erh of Dongchan Monastery in Fuzhou ascended the hall and said: "It has never for a moment been lost; the entire body is manifest before one.
To speak in such a way is already an overstatement. Since it cannot be spoken of in this manner, how should one speak before you, my brothers?"
"Is it that where there is no Way, the Way is not received? Do not misunderstand. A monk asked, "What is the samādhi of the present moment?
The Master said, "Why wait any longer for me to speak? [The monk] asked, "My own matter is not yet clear; I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said:

"Why do you not pay your respects and offer thanks? [The monk] asked, "What is the house style of Dongchan? The Master said, "One person transmits a falsehood, ten thousand people transmit it as a reality.
Chan Master Hongbian Miaoguo of Changqing Monastery in Fuzhou ascended the hall and stood to one side before the seat, saying: "Great..."
"Has everyone returned to the hall? Do you understand? If you do not yet understand, I am deceiving you, monks.
He then ascended the seat. A monk asked, "The assembly has gathered like clouds; we pray that the Master will open the gate of expedient means and reveal the true reality.
The Master said, "This very thing is the gate of expedient means. The monk said, "If that is so, then the great assembly shall listen attentively. The Master—
[The Master] said: "Liaokong, listen closely from the side; what is it like?
A monk asked Chan Master Ke Long Liaokong of Dongchan Monastery in Fuzhou, "What is the Way? The Master said, "It is precisely the Way.
The monk asked, "What is one who walks upon the Way? The Master said, "I have told you clearly. He ascended the hall [and said]: "Very good!"
A Summary. Since you are not yet a *siddha*, if you are one who merely follows the sound [of words], it would be better for you to return to the hall and sit by the fire.
Take care. Question: "What is the first phrase of Samantabhadra? The Master said: "That would already fall into the second phrase."

Chan Master Shoubian of Xianzong Monastery in Fuzhou did not ascend the hall for a long time. When the assembly entered the abbot’s quarters to inquire after him, the Master said, "Tonight, I am taking leave together with the assembly.
I wonder, will leave be granted? "If you have not heard leave granted, then the one who spoke first is at fault.
Take care. A monk asked, "As for the person who is always present throughout the twelve periods of the day, can they still digest [the teachings]?"
[The monk asked: "Is there no one who can receive the offerings of devas and humans? The Master said, "One cannot digest them. [The monk] asked, "Why can one not digest them?
The Master said, "Because you are always present. [The monk] asked, "As for a person who is not always present—can they digest them or not? The Master said:

"In what year of the donkey's life? [The monk] asked, requesting the Master to answer the "no guest, no host" dialogue. The Master said, "Bring forth your question from the place where there is neither guest nor host.
Chan Master Huai Lie Jingwu of Yongan Temple in Fuzhou ascended the hall. Looking around at those present, he said, "Why do you suffer from stammering? He then returned to his quarters.
Ascending the hall again after a long while, he said, "Fortunately, it was already pitiable enough, yet it has been defiled once more."
[He] ascended the hall and said: "The assembly is precisely at the point where effort must be applied; do not take this lightly. A monk asked: "Yishan personally heard a single phrase;
I request the Master to speak for the sake of those who study. The Master said: "In the future, do not misrepresent it to others."
Chan Master Han of Mingshan in Fuzhou ascended the hall and said: "Requiting kindness, kindness is fully repaid; fulfilling vows, vows are perfected. He then returned to his quarters.
A monk asked, "Having reached the summit of the Wondrous Peak, who is your companion? The Master said, "Arrived. The monk asked, "Who is your companion?
The Master said, "Go drink tea. Another monk asked, "I clearly do not understand; I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said: [Go drink tea.]
"Setting aside that indication for a moment, what is your own matter of clear realization? He replied, "I do not understand.
He requested again, "I beg the Master to point it out. The Master said, "Eight blows, thirteen."
Regarding the story of National Preceptor Guishan of Silla as cited by someone: When Prime Minister Pei was inaugurating a Dharma assembly, he asked a monk, "What sutra are you studying?
The monk replied, "The *Sutra of the Silent Youth*. The official asked, "How many fascicles does it have? He replied, "Two fascicles.
The official said, "Since it is 'the silent,' why are there two fascicles? The monk had no reply. The Master [Linji] provided this substitute answer: "If one speaks of silence,"...
It is not merely these two fascicles.
Zen Master Daoyin of Ziguo Monastery in Jizhou was asked by a monk, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?

The Master said, "In the eighth year of the Putong era, I encountered a strange occurrence under the Liang dynasty; even until now, it has not been cleared away. [The monk] asked, "Regarding the thousand mountains and ten thousand mountains..."
"What is Longxu Mountain? The Master said, "A thousand mountains, ten thousand mountains. "How about the person within the mountains?
The Master said, "Facing each other across a thousand li. "Please speak, Master, without falling into 'is' or 'is not'. The Master said, "How do you ask?"
A monk asked Chan Master Chengjing of Xiangguang Monastery in Fuzhou, “What is the Way? The Master said, “On the streets of Chang’an. The monk asked, “How is it regarding the matter above this?
The Master said, “The sound of the valley arises from the ten thousand pipes; the old pines are draped with five clouds. Another asked, “What is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, “The affairs of state are discussed at the gate; how many layers of palace curtains are there?”
Chan Master Conggui of Baoci Monastery in Hangzhou was the son of the Chen family of Fuzhou. A monk asked him: "I have heard an ancient saying:
'If people today study the teachings of the ancients, they cannot avoid mental turmoil; yet if they wish to avoid mental turmoil, they must study the teachings of the ancients.'"
"What is the ancient teaching? The Master said, "Thus have I heard. [The student] asked, "What is turmoil within the mind?
The Master said, "The sound of sparrows over there."
A monk asked Chan Master Chiying Guangbian Zhouzhi of Longhua Temple in Hangzhou, "What is the realm of Longhua?
The Master said, "Green bamboos sway in the wind; cold pines lock in the moon. The monk asked, "Who is the person within the realm? The Master said:
“By no means be so presumptuous. The student asked, “What is the site of enlightenment for the Buddhas of the three periods of time? The Master said, “Do not go elsewhere to pay your respects.
The student said, “If that is so, then it has been thus from the beginningless past until the endless future. The Master said, “In what year did that happen?”

The Incense-Bearer Spirit. The Official said, "Since you are the Incense-Bearer Spirit, why did you overturn the tea?
Lang said, "To serve an official for a thousand days, yet to fail in a single morning. The Official brushed out his sleeves and departed.
Mingzhao said, "Dharma Seat Lang has finished eating the meal at Zhaoqing, yet he goes outside to hunt for wild roots. Lang asked, "How about you, Dharma Seat? Zhao said, "Not so."
People took advantage of this opportunity.

Zen Master Huirun of Yanshou Temple in Tanzhou, a successor of Zen Master Baofo Zhan, was asked by a monk: "What is it like when the precious sword has not yet emerged from its scabbard? The Master said:
[The student] said, "It is not outside. [The Master] asked, "After it has left the case, how is it? The Master said, "It is not inside. The student asked, "What is this 'one color'?
The Master said, "Blue, yellow, red, and white. The student said, "How wonderful, this one color! The Master said, "I thought there was no one; yet here is one, or perhaps half a person."
Chan Master Kechou of Baofu in Zhangzhou was asked by a monk, "What is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, "Clouds in the blue sky; water in the pitcher. The monk asked, "What is the 'blow-off-hair' sword? The Master said, "It has already slipped away.
The monk asked, "Is it still used? The Master said, "Do not speak like a ghost."
Chan Master Ruxin of Haihui Monastery in Shuzhou ascended the hall. After a long silence, he said, "Excessive ritual leads to confusion," and then descended from his seat.

A monk asked, "How should one proclaim the ancestral vehicle of the predecessors? The Master said, "It becomes increasingly solitary. The monk said, "I beg the Master for a word regarding the point of intimacy.
The Master said, "One must not listen to others even when there is no snow. The monk asked, "What is the sudden [enlightenment] of Kāśyapa?"
"Have you understood this matter? The Master said, "If you have understood me, I shall not be stingy. [The monk] said, "In that case, there will be no trouble for the Master.
The Master said, "Furthermore, one must still receive blows; how can it be that there is no trouble? [The monk] asked, "Niu-tou gave explanations both horizontally and vertically."

He still did not know the pivot of the upward path. [The student] asked, "What is the pivot of the upward path? The Master said, "Fortunately, I encountered a mother who gave birth to me with short arms.
[The student] asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s intent? The Master said, "How difficult would it be to say? [The student] said, "I ask you, Master, to speak it.
The Master said, "I thought you were quick-witted; yet you are neither a sage nor a seer."

A monk asked Chan Master Wenchin of Baoci Monastery in Fuzhou, "What is the realm of all Buddhas? The Master said: "When rain falls, clouds and mist darken;
when it is clear and dry, the sun and moon shine bright. [The monk] asked, "What is the wondrously enlightened mind? The Master said: "Now..."
"In winter, late rice is favored; it is produced by the autumn rains. [The student] asked, "What is the wondrous function that is as vast as the sands of the Ganges?
The Master said, "Clouds arise from the azure peaks; rain falls upon the blue sky. [The student] asked, "How does the ordinary mind accord with the Way?
The Master said, "Drink tea and eat rice, passing the time according to the occasion; gazing at the water and looking at the mountains truly delights the spirit."
A monk asked Chan Master Qingyun Zihua of Wannian Monastery in Quanzhou, "When the Buddhas appear in the world, they shake heaven and earth.
When you, Master, appear in the world, how is it? The Master said, "What would I say to you?
The monk said, "In that case, you are no different from the various sages. The Master said, "Do not speak recklessly. The monk asked, "What is the house style of Wannian? The Master... [text ends]

[The monk] said, "Moss soup and rice from a granary. [The monk] asked, "If a distinguished guest were to arrive suddenly, how would you receive them? The Master said, "Three rounds of tea after the meal.
[The monk] asked, "What is the realm of Wan’an like? The Master said, "A single pagoda, pines and vines, gazing at the sea’s greenness."

When Chan Master Daohui of Baoen Monastery in Zhangzhou was first delivering a letter on behalf of Baofu to Wang, the Grand Marshal of Quanzhou, the Marshal asked, "Has the Master from south of Zhangzhou been performing the work of a teacher recently?
The Master replied, "If I say he has been performing the work of a teacher..."
He then bowed to the Master. When the Master said, "The Way is not for the sake of others," the Grand Marshal (Taishou) came forward to inquire.
The Grand Marshal said, "Speak a single phrase. The Master replied, "Wait until the iron ox can chew grass and the wooden horse can breathe smoke.

The Grand Marshal said, "I spare my mouth to eat my rice. After a long silence, the Grand Marshal asked again, "Does the donkey come? Does the horse come? The Master replied, "Donkey and horse are not the same."
The Commandant said, "How did you manage to get here? The Master replied, "I specifically thank the Great Commandant for taking up this conversation.

Later, after he had settled there, a monk asked, "I do not ask about brilliant words or subtle phrases; I request that the Master speak from his own true realization. The Master said, "I shall not obstruct your purpose."
A monk asked Chan Master Congchen Hongren of Fenghuang Mountain in Quanzhou, “What is the master’s house style?

The Master said, “If one’s own style is similar to mine, there will be no obstruction; however, you are not that person. The monk asked, “What would it be like if one suddenly encountered such a person?
The Master said, “One must not scratch in anticipation of an itch. [The monk] asked, “When a student’s faculties and thoughts are slow and hesitant, just as...”

In the midst of the gate, he requested, "Please glance at me from the side. The Master said, "I glance from the side. He replied, "I have deeply grasped the Master's intent; how would I dare speak further?
The Master said, "That is too much. He ascended the hall. A monk came forward to prostrate, then rose and stepped back to stand.
The Master said, "I am not as good as you. The monk responded with an "Amen" (Āṃ). The Master said, "In a place where there is no one, let it go. He was asked, "What is the student’s own [nature]?"
[The monk asked about] his own affairs. The Master said, "The matters of calculating one's years can be known. [The monk] asked, "What is the realm of the phoenix?
The Master said, "Watching the bright moon on a snowy night. [The monk] asked, "What is the meaning of the Western Come? The Master said, "Being a person is a matter of making mistakes.
[The monk] asked, "Wherein lies being a person? The Master said, "Are you not being too self-important?"
Chan Master Minghui Ying of Yonglong Monastery in Fuzhou ascended the hall and said: "They say that when dawn approaches, there are still those traveling by night.
It may seem so, yet it is not so. Take care! A monk asked, "Why is it that for one who is non-active and without affairs, a golden lock is difficult to remove?
The Master said, "Because of severing the coarse and the subtle; what is precious is difficult to retain. The monk asked, "Why do you say this?"
"A person of no-action and no-affairs dwells in true joy and ease. The Master said, "To deal with the clamor and confusion, one must bring it to an end.
A monk came for an audience; the Master said, "There is no need for so many various ways; speak quickly, speak quickly! The monk was speechless.

He ascended the hall and said, "At the hour of the Rabbit (6–8 a.m.), when acting, there is no need to employ clever artifice," and he immediately descended from his seat. A monk asked, "What is it like to advance toward [the goal]?"
"Fundamental Source. The Master said: "Rely upon it and practice accordingly.
Chan Master Shouching of Mount Qingquan in Hongzhou was a native of Fuzhou. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "The question.
The monk asked, "What is the Patriarch? The Master said, "The answer. The monk asked, "When you, Master, met the ancients, what did you obtain?"
He then remained on this mountain. The Master said, "I knew from the start that you would not consent. [The monk] asked, "How do you know that I will not consent?
The Master said, "By observing facial expressions and discerning countenances. [The monk] asked, "At the point of intimacy, I beg for a word from the Master.

The Master said, "Nothing surpasses this. [The monk] asked, "For what purpose did the ancients face the wall? The Master said, "It is a matter of being wronged. [The monk] said, "In that case, one may save mental effort. The Master said, "..."
"Where is there such a person? I do not ask about other matters; what is the matter that transcends [the ordinary]?
The Master said, "It would consume your three prostrations; it would not consume your three prostrations."
A monk asked Chan Master Xingchong of Baoen Monastery in Zhangzhou, “What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?

The Master said, “The pestle grinds; the millstone grinds. The monk asked, “I pray that the Master will expound upon the single path of Caoxi. The Master said, “Are you not being too modest regarding Caoxi?
The monk said, “If that is so, then all living beings have someone to rely upon. The Master said, “That is just like a mouse eating salt. The monk asked, “Without involving [anything else]...”
A monk asked, "How do you speak regarding the public and the private? The Master said, "Go and drink tea. Another asked, "What was the meaning of Danxia burning the wooden Buddha?
The Master said, "The weather is cold; he burned fire for warmth. He asked again, "What was the meaning of Cuiwei welcoming the Arhat? The Master said, [Go and drink tea].

The Abbot of Mount Yue-lu in Tanzhou ascended the hall and, after a long silence, said: "In the past, it was Vairocana; today, it is Mount Yue-lu. Take care!
A monk asked, "What is the phrase beyond sound and form? The Master said, "The howling of monkeys and the calling of birds. [The monk] asked, "What is the Master’s song?"

"Whose family style is this? Whom does the patriarchal wind succeed? The Master said: "The five notes and six pitch-pipes. [The student] asked about the phrase regarding the cutting off of the tongue and requested the Master to expound upon it.
The Master said: "The sun can make it hot; the moon can make it cool."
A monk asked Chan Master Deshan Dehai of Langzhou, "At the assembly on Vulture Peak, who was it that heard? The Master said, "You, O Kalyāṇamitra, heard.
The monk asked, "I do not know what was preached at Vulture Peak. The Master said, "It is you, O Kalyāṇamitra, who understand.
The monk asked, "What is the phrase that encompasses heaven and encloses the earth? The Master said, "The ten realms tremble. The monk asked, "Regarding the ancestral vehicle..."
"What is the proof? The Master said, "Setting aside the past for a moment, how is it right now? [The monk] said, "The whole assembly sees it. The Master said, "Your words have fallen.
[Another] asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Split it open."
A monk asked Master Houzhao Qing of Quanzhou, "I ask the Master to deliberate upon the final word.
The Master said, "The person grows old amidst the dust; the moon is ever bright at the edge of heaven. A monk asked, "What is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, "One flask and one bowl; everywhere is my livelihood. A monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "Disturbance."
Disturbed and in a state of haste: the cock crowing at dawn and the bell tolling at dusk.
Chan Master Jian of Liangshan in Dingzhou asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Yaoshan.
The Master said, "Have you brought any medicine with you? The monk said, "Even your dwelling on this mountain, Master, is not without merit. The Master then ceased questioning.
A monk asked Chan Master Cheng of Jianshan in Hongzhou, “What is the sword of the Dharma King? The Master said, “How regrettable! The monk asked, “What is the sword of the Human King?
The Master said, “Dust buries the shoes beneath the bed; the wind moves the turban atop the rack.

A monk asked, “The teachings of the successive generations of time were intended to guide those of the present. I wonder, how did the Patriarchs instruct people? The Master said, “The teachings of a single generation...”
Regarding the "Teachings for the Time": someone had already asked about this, saying, "How do you instruct people, Master?

The Master replied, "I am grieved that the red amaranth tree in front of my courtyard produces leaves year after year, yet never bears flowers. [The questioner] asked, "The old year has passed; the new year has arrived."
[The monk] asked, "Is there anyone who does not observe the New Year's retreat? The Master said, "How so? [The monk] said, "In that case, one does not observe the retreat.
The Master said, "The horn for the new year has already blown atop the city walls; yet by the window, the lamp of the old year still flickers.
[The monk] asked, "What is the lamp of the old year? The Master said, "The thirtieth day of the twelfth month."

At that time, it is not manifest; there is not a single thing that can be understood by means of uncovering or veiling.

Spontaneously harmonizing with the past and the present, one is liberated from birth and death. As the ancients said: "To recognize the mind and reach the source, and to understand the unconditioned dharma—only then is one called a śramaṇa.
Now, all you officials and the great assembly must each take this to heart; do not entirely pass the responsibility onto others.

What I have just said in such great detail was merely because there was no other way. Do not say that such talk is what the ancestral school of the Gate of the Patriarchs ought to employ.

Having kept the assembly waiting for a long time, take care. He then spoke a verse on the expedient means of seated meditation: The body is the seat of meditation; The mind is the object of contemplation.

When body and mind are both forgotten, This is called the true practice of sitting. Do not seek the Way outside yourself; Seeking is itself a delusion. If you can let go of all thoughts, This is the Buddha-seal. If you wish to attain the Way, Do not rely on words and phrases. Directly point to the mind; See your nature and become a Buddha.

"What makes one a venerable elder? The Master replied, "A thousand-year-old crane is still called a 'red-crested heron'; one born this morning is already a phoenix.
Entering the hall, he said, "This matter is so easy to explain! At that time, a monk came forward and said, "I ask the Master to speak it."
The Master said: "Muzhou’s brook-moss and Jinjun’s stone-ears. He asked the assembly: "When washing gold in one's hands, who is it that obtains it? The Master said:
"Wading through sand by the stream is but a weariness for oneself; the treasure is within the house—return to it quickly. [A monk] asked:

"If that is so, then from beginning to end, it cannot be obtained from another. The Master said: "Even if you possessed the strength to lift up mountains, you would still not escape the burden upon your shoulders."
There was Danyi.
Chan Master Zhiyuan of Zifu Monastery in Fuzhou was a native of Fuzhou. He visited Jingqing and asked, "What is the place where all Buddhas emerge?
Jingqing said, "Everyone must know. The Master said, "If that is so, then the eyes of the multitude cannot be deceived."
[The Master] departed. Qing said, "Principle can bind even a leopard. Because of this, the Master attained awakening to the profound essence (*xuanzhi*).

After he took up residence, a monk asked, "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose lineage of the school's wind does he succeed? The Master replied, "The moon before the peak of Snow Ridge; the clarity within the waves of Mirror Lake.
[The monk] asked, "When the Buddhas appear in the world, the heavens rain four kinds of flowers and the earth shakes in six ways. What do you have today, Preceptor?"

An auspicious omen appeared. The Master said, "When not a single thing arises, the whole body is revealed. Who knows the radiance before one's eyes? A monk asked, "What is the single phrase that points directly?
The Master said, "What is it? The Master then said, "Do you understand? If you understand, it is settled this very moment;
if you do not understand, it will take kalpas as numerous as grains of sand. Relying solely upon the level of each of you noble ones, the mind-source of the ancient Buddhas is clear."

Manifest before you: encompassing heaven and pervading earth, the myriad phenomena stand in solemn array. This is the natural style of one's own house: Buddhas and sentient beings are fundamentally without distinction.
Nirvana and birth-and-death are merely products of illusory transformation; the true permanence of the original nature requires no laborious cultivation or realization.
Be careful! Be careful!
Chan Master Yiyuan Kaimei of Wugu Mountain in Quzhou was the son of the Xu family of Wuxing.

In the third year of the Qianfu era of the Tang dynasty, on the eve of his birth, an extraordinary fragrance filled the room and a crimson light shone as brightly as day. During the Guangqi era, while accompanying his father in the governorship of Xin’an, he was pressured into marriage;
however, the Master did not desire it and subsequently traveled through various regions. Having attained spiritual resonance with Jingqing, he returned to visit his father.

The Master’s mother then established a separate dwelling south of the city wall to fulfill the Master’s wish. Beside this house was the shrine of Minister Chen, where there was a statue of Chan Master Lin.
When the Master went to pay his respects, he lost sight of the Master’s whereabouts.

Later, while the District Magistrate was performing a sacrifice at the shrine, he saw the Master entering meditative absorption (dhyāna) amidst the thick bamboo behind the temple; ants were gnawing at his robes, and withered leaves reached his thighs. Some say it was he.
Xu Zhen was the son of Jiang. From this samādhi, he would emerge and enter it at will.

Chan Master Nü of Zihu did not yet know the depth of the Master’s realization and asked, "The concentration you dwell in is merely that of the Hīnayāna. At that time, the Master was just drinking tea;
he lifted up his tea bag and said, "Is this great or small? Nü was struck with awe. He then went to visit De of Tangshan on Mount Kuacang.
Master Yan asked, "What is your surname? He replied, "My surname is Xu. Yan asked, "Who permitted you [to become a monk]? He replied, "There is no distinction.
Yan silently recognized his potential and subsequently granted him the tonsure and ordination. Once, he ordered him to pick peaches; ten days passed without his returning.

When Yan went to search for him, he found the Master leaning against a rock beneath a peach tree, profoundly absorbed in meditative concentration (*samādhi*). Yan snapped his fingers to rouse him from it. During the Kaiyun era, while traveling to Jianglang Rock, he beheld...
At the stone grotto, he said to his disciple Huixing, "I shall enter meditative absorption within this. You must pile stones to block the entrance and do not harbor thoughts of me.

Huixing followed these instructions. The following year, Huixing felt that the Master had passed away; he opened the grotto to look at him, and the Master’s white hair fell over his shoulders, yet his chest was still warm.
He slowly rose from his concentration of his own accord, with no change in his appearance. [The Master] returned once more to Wugu, where he was attended.
When Officer Shangeng was stationed in Xin’an, he commanded the monk Shou’rong—a scholar-monk—to interrogate Master Fu regarding the characteristics of his meditative concentration.
The Master did not engage him in debate; Shou’rong, however, held him in low esteem. At that time, the people of Xin’an vied with one another to paint portraits of the Master and honored them.

Everyone obtained śarīra relics. Hui-rong, filled with shame and submission, prostrated before the image to apologize for his transgressions; he too obtained śarīra relics and sighed, saying, "From now on, I shall not dare to fathom [the Dharma] with my shallow understanding.
King Qian Zhongyi was moved by the Master’s appearance in a dream and dispatched an envoy to have an image painted.

Just as it happened, the King suffered from eye disease; when he unfurled the image and paid homage, it appeared exactly as seen in the dream, and śarīra relics rained down accordingly, curing his eye ailment.

He was immediately healed. Consequently, he was granted the honorary title "Kaimei" (Enlightened) and composed verses of praise. Thousands of precious vessels and ritual implements were offered to him.

At the beginning of the Duan-gong era, Emperor Taizong, having heard of the Master’s power of meditative concentration (*samādhi*), issued an imperial decree for the local prefecture to accord him special honors and provide transport for his journey to the capital. The Master declined the invitation with great earnestness.

The Sangha arrived again with an imperial decree, specifically ordering that he be carried in a sedan chair for an audience in the private hall. The Emperor bade him sit and granted him tea, then inquired about his meditative attainments.

His responses were concise and exhaustive, deeply resonating with the Emperor’s intent. He requested leave to return home, but was summoned back for another audience; having obtained permission, he returned to the mountain, where the carriage tracks were blocked by crowds of parting well-wishers.
In the first year of the Chunhua era, he passed away. He was one hundred and fifteen years old, with fifty-seven years of monastic seniority. His remains were cremated.

The white light belonged to the heavens; the śarīra were of five colors. The people of the region fashioned images from his bones, which are worshipped to this day by officials in the prefectures and commanderies for prayers regarding rain and sunshine, with responses as swift as an echo.
Chan Master Shihao Chuanxin of Miaoji Monastery in Tanzhou, a successor of Chan Master Baoen Yue, was asked by a monk: "To conceive [of it] is the second head;
not to conceive [of it] is the third head. What is the first head? The Master said, "Withdraw. Another asked: "The ancients cut off their arms; for what purpose did they do so?"
"What is the matter? The Master said, "I would rather cut off my arm. [The monk] asked, "What is the eye of the student? The Master said, "You must know that I have good intentions.
[The monk] asked, "What is the sword of Mount Xiangshan? The Master said, "Extraordinary. [The monk] asked, "Is it still revealed? The Master said, "[It is]."
"I cannot bear to see it. [The monk] asked, "What is the first phrase of the Pine Gate? The Master said, "By all means, do not misquote it. [The monk] asked, "What is the house style of Miaojie?
The Master said, "There are too many people on both sides. [The monk] asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, "Two mouths and no tongue. [The monk] asked, "What is the single path of Xiangshan? The Master said, "Tao."
Tao Di asked, "What is it like to 'arrive'? The Master said, "Cease your lifelong pursuit. He asked, "What is the secret word of the World-Honored One?
The Master said, "Even Ānanda did not know it. He asked, "Why did he not know it? The Master said, "Was it not because he was a *śrāmaṇera*?"
Question: "What is the treasure of Fragrant Mountain? The Master said: "The blue-eyed barbarian does not dare to determine it.

[The monk] asked: "What about that which is exposed? The Master said: "The Dragon King cannot lift it up. A monk cited the story of a clay statue of the Holy Monk being bitten by a tiger and asked the Master:
"Since he is the Holy Monk, why was he bitten by a beast? The Master said: "He has caused all the people in the world to fall into doubt. Question: "How is it?"
"This person is one who lacks shame and remorse. The Master said, "The Acharya deserves a beating.
On the day of the opening of the hall by Chan Master Shigui of Bailu in Fuzhou, a monk asked: "The stream of Xixia is no different from that of the Horse [Master]."
[The Master] said, "Head! How does White Deer Peak compare to Chicken Foot Mountain? The Master said, "Let the assembly examine this. He asked, "What is the house style of White Deer?
The Master said, "What would you have me say to you? [The monk] said, "If that is so, then one simply knows the time to depart.
The Master said, "As for a person who knows the time, what kind of state should they reach? [The monk] said, "One must not continue to chatter with the mouth. The Master—
He said, "To let it pass is not permissible. [The monk] asked, "When Niutou had not yet met the Fourth Patriarch, the hundred birds brought flowers as offerings;
why did they no longer come after he had seen him? The Master said, "All gaze toward the horizon before the dawn light has parted;
once daybreak arrives, all is as usual."
Chan Master Yicong of Luoshan in Fuzhou ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What is the lion that has emerged from its den?
The Master said, "Where would it not cause the earth to tremble and split? The monk asked, "What sound does it make? The Master said, "The deaf do not hear.
A monk asked, "When he pointed his finger at heaven and earth and declared, 'I alone am honored,' why was he rebuked by bystanders? The Master said, "It was because they said..."
Huxu said, "Red-beard! As for one who merely stands by as an onlooker, what excellence is there? The Master said, "One sees injustice on the road, and therefore grasps the sword.
The Master then said, "If there were a place to entrust it to, Luoshan would not have possessed the eye.
If there were no place to entrust it to, then it would be labor without merit. Therefore, when Vimalakīrti faced Mañjuśrī in the past, he asked: 'Suppose...'"
There is no assembly now. I take my leave; long standing, I bid you adieu.
Chan Master Conggui of An Guo Monastery in Fuzhou was asked by a monk: "The Zen palace is wide open and the Dharma companions have gathered like clouds.

Regarding the one path that transcends all, I pray the Master will provide a definitive resolution. The Master said: "I am not one of those who follow the worldly trends. Ascending the hall, he said: "As for Chan and the Way, [I] pick up..."
"Put it aside. What kind of tattered straw sandals are the Buddha and the Patriarchs? To report matters in such a way—does this not wrong the assembly?
If you say it wrongs them, then you must go on pilgrimage; if you say it does not wrong them, you must at least shut your mouth.
Adieu. [Ascending the hall: "Even if one had never encountered the Liang dynasty, An Guo would still deceive people."
"However, take care. A monk asked, "Please, Master, proclaim the essence of the School. The Master said, "Today we thresh grain; tomorrow we carry firewood.
The monk asked, "What was it like before Niu-t'ou saw the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said, "The incense burner faces the rope bed.
The monk asked, "What was it like after he saw him? The Master said, "The door leaf faces the pillar. The monk asked, "What is the Master’s family style? The Master said—
[The monk] said, "If you are asked about the family style, you answer with the family style. [The Master] said, "When a student does not ask about the family style, what then?
The Master said, "The barbarian comes; the Han goes. [The monk] said, "I do not ask about other matters; I beg for a word from the Master regarding the essential point.
The Master said, "Have you attained the essential yet? He further said, "Cunda’s offering—take care."
Chan Master Changqing Zangyong of Yishan in Fuzhou ascended the hall. When the assembly had gathered, he threw his fan to the ground and said, "The foolish call gold earth;
how do the wise regard it? The younger generation is to be feared; you must not all remain mired in ignorance.
Is there anyone who can speak on this? Come forward and say. At that time, a monk stepped forth and prostrated.
He stepped back and stood there. The Master said, "What else would you do? He replied, "I pray the Master will provide a clear mirror.
The Master said, "A peach pit from a thousand years ago. He asked, "What is the monastery? The Master said, "Changxi and Putian.
He asked, "Who is among those within the monastery? The Master said, "Xinluo and Baishui. He asked, "What is the true master of Lingquan? The Master said, "The South."
Shanbei Shan was asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "Before the midday meal, the kitchen steams rice from the South;
after the noon hour, the hearth brews tea from Beiyuan. He asked, "Does the Dharma-body still undergo suffering?
The Master said, "Is hell not heaven? He said, "In that case, it must undergo suffering. The Master said, "What offense has it committed?"

Chan Master Yandu of Yonglong Monastery in Fuzhou ascended the hall. As the assembly gathered like clouds, the Master rose from his seat and performed a dance, saying to the crowd, "Do you understand?
They replied, "We do not understand. The Master said, "I, this mountain monk, do not abandon the Way and its teachings, yet I manifest the affairs of an ordinary person.
Why do you not understand? A monk asked, "The fundamental nature is originally perfected; why then is it clearly obscured?"
The Master said: "Examine and scrutinize this for yourself.
Chan Master Zhidu of Ruipeng Monastery in Linyang, Fuzhou, was a native of that same province. Initially, he visited Anguo Monastery, where he saw a monk ask:
"What is the body revealed alone amidst the myriad phenomena? Anguo raised a finger; the monk did not realize it.
The Master then reached a profound, mystical accord with the ultimate meaning and entered the room. He said, "Just now, when I observed that monk’s dialogue, I had a moment of realization.
Guo asked, "What principle did you perceive? The Master also raised a finger and said, "What is this?
Guo approved of this. The Master bowed in thanks. Later, while presiding over the assembly in the Dharma hall, he held up a whisk and said, "Caoxi..."

That which is never exhausted—people of the time call this "the emergence of horns. When I, this mountain monk, take it up to brush away a mosquito, those who can realize it find that heaven and earth collapse.
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said, "The wooden horse gallops like smoke;
the stone man cannot catch up. The monk asked, "What is Chan? The Master said, "This year’s drought follows last year’s. [The monk] asked, "What is... [The Master said: "How is it?"
[The monk] asked about the Way. The Master said, "In winter fields, half the harvest is lost. [The monk] asked, "What is the student’s own self?
The Master gave him a kick. The monk made a gesture to receive it; the Master then gave him a slap. The monk was speechless. The Master said, "He has been cheated to death.
[The monk] asked, "What is the Buddha-dharma in a place utterly devoid of human smoke? The Master said, "A steep mountain rises sharply, its greenery fragrant. [The monk] said, "Is it thus?"
"Then the principle of the single truth is no different whether in the fields or the wilds. The Master said, "It is not this principle. A monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, "A set of bamboo chopsticks, one for each person. A monk attended the night assembly. The Master asked, "Who is there?
The monk replied, "It is I, [Name]. The Master said, "Sugar from Quanzhou; betel nuts on the ship. After a long silence, the monk remained silent. The Master said, "Do you understand?"
Mò said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "If you were to understand, you would sweep away the five aggregates and swallow up the ten directions.
In the eighth month of the first year of the Kaibao era, he left behind a verse: "In the second month of next year, on the second day, I shall part from you and leave you for a while.

My ashes shall be scattered across the four forests, so as to spare the land of the donors. On the twenty-eighth day of the first month of the following year, the local people vied with one another to enter the mountain.

[The disciples] paid their respects. The Master was still in good health, and his inquiries were as usual. On the first day of the second month, the Prefect led various officials to the mountain, where they stayed overnight to observe him closely.
On the second day, after the midday meal, he ascended the hall to take leave of the assembly. At that time, Elder Yuanying stepped forward and asked:
"Clouds grieve and dew weeps; the great assembly wails. We pray for a word from the Master before you depart. The Master lowered [his head].
Yizhu said, "The Dharma-mirror does not descend upon this land; where else, then, does the Jewel Moon shine? The Master said, "That is not within your realm.
Yizhu said, "If that is so, then as bubbles arise and bubbles perish, they return to the water; the coming and going of the Master is the fundamental constant.
The Master let out a long sigh, descended from his seat, and returned to his quarters to sit in stillness. At the hour of Hai (9–11 p.m.), he questioned the assembly.
[The disciples] asked, "World-Honored One, at what time and season will you enter parinirvāṇa? The assembly replied, "At the hour of the rat on the fifteenth day of the second month.
The Master said, "I have already spoken my final words earlier this very day; I shall now depart forever."
Master Ming of Xianzong Yuan in Fuzhou ascended the hall and said: "Fortunately, there is such a tradition of our school; why do you not propagate it with brilliant splendor?
If you can propagate it, you will not be within the three realms. If you were to leave the three realms, you would destroy the three realms.
If you were to remain within the three realms, you would be obstructed by the three realms. To be neither obstructed nor destroyed—this is to transcend the three realms. This is..."
"Transcending the triple world—when you have penetrated thus, you are fit to be a seed of the Buddha-dharma; humanity and the heavens shall rely upon you.

At that time, a monk asked, "If one grasps the clouds without depending on the power of wind and thunder, how can one penetrate through the body amidst the surging waves? The Master said, "How can you abandon the root to pursue the branches?"
Chan Master Xiang of Anguo Monastery in Fuzhou ascended the hall. After a long silence, he cried out: "This is truly groundless! Nevertheless, there is no other way.
If among you there are those who have not yet seen through this, I shall further open up a skillful means.
Do you understand? At that time, a monk asked: "Without involving skillful means, I beg the Master to bestow his compassion. The Master said: "You ask and I answer; thus..."
"This is a skillful means. [A monk] asked, "The manifestation of form according to the object is like the moon in water. What is the moon? The Master raised his whisk.
The monk said, "Why did the ancients say that the moon in water has no form? The Master said, "What do you see? [Another] asked, "What is the matter within the School of the Patriarchs?
The Master said, "After the Huai army has scattered. [Another] asked, "What is the家风 (family style) of the Master? The Master said, "After the Huai army has scattered."
The Master said: "It is difficult to deceive the eyes of the multitude.
Chan Master Shuilong Pu was a dharma successor of Chan Master Qinghuo of Baofu Monastery in Zhangzhou;
he was a native of Fuzhou. From his youth, he was intelligent and quick-witted, and he paid homage at Drum Mountain.
The National Teacher (Guoshi) shaved his head and received full ordination. Later, he visited Master Ruan of Dazhang Mountain (the dialogue is recorded in the records of Master Ruan).
Subsequently, he studied under Shuilong. Shuilong asked, "Layman Huo, which venerable masters have you visited? Have you attained awakening yet?
He replied, "I once visited Master Dazhang and gained a place of conviction. Thereupon, Shuilong ascended the hall, gathered the assembly, and called out, "Layman Huo, come forth!"

"Come forward. Burn incense before the assembly and speak of your realization; I, the old monk, shall bear witness for you. The Master stepped out from the assembly, took up the incense, and said, "The incense has already been offered.

As for realization—I have realized it, yet I have not realized it. Long was greatly pleased and granted him permission. He ascended the hall and said, "I, this mountain monk, now act as a mediator for all of you.
Those who agree, remain silent; those who do not agree, speak. After a long pause, he said, "Agreement and..."
"Inharmonious. It depends entirely on the present moment. This mountain monk carries a few matters with him. Take care. A monk asked, "What is it like when a poor household suffers a robbery?
The Master said, "He cannot empty the bottom out. The monk asked, "Why can he not empty the bottom out?
The Master said, "The thief is a member of the family. The monk asked, "If he is a member of the family, why does he instead become a family thief? The Master said, "Internally..."
[The student] said, "Since there is no response, the external cannot act. The Master said, "When suddenly seized and defeated, what then?
The student said, "When seized and defeated, where does the merit reside? The Master said, "Even the reward has never been heard of. The student said, "If so, then labor is expended without merit.
The Master said, "Merit is not non-existent; it is accomplished, yet there is no abiding in it. The student said, "Since it is already accomplished..."
Gong asked, "Why do you not remain in it? The Master said, "Have you not heard it said: 'The Great Peace was originally brought about by the generals;
we do not allow the generals to witness the Great Peace'? He asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said, "The barbarian weeps, and the Han person grieves."
The Master suddenly left his assembly, intending to enter the mountains to await his passing. He then left a verse, saying: "Let the people of the world cease speaking of the hardships of the road;
The path for birds and the sheep’s gut are but a few inches apart. Take care, O waters of the Zhu Creek bank! You shall return to the vast ocean; I shall return to the mountains.
He then went to Guihu to establish a hermitage. Not long after, he said to his disciples: "After my passing, you shall offer my remains as alms."
"Do not place any insects or ants upon the stupa. Having spoken these words, he entered Mount Hutou, sat upon a flat rock, and passed away in solemn stillness.
His disciples, following his final instructions, kept the body for seven days; yet, in the end, there was no sign of it being consumed by insects or ants.
Thereupon, they performed the cremation and scattered the remains throughout the forests and fields.
A monk asked National Teacher Jinlun, the Dharma heir of Chan Master Jinlun, “What is the first phrase of Jinlun? The Master said, “An obtuse fellow.”
Question: "What is the single arrow of the golden wheel? The Master said: "It has passed. Question: "When this one arrow is released at the opportune moment, who is there to receive it?
The Master said: "It is overturned."
Chan Master Zhihong Hongji of Mount Dailong in Dingzhou, successor to Chan Master Baizhao Yuan, was asked by a monk: "What is the Buddha? The Master said: "It is you yourself. The monk asked:
"How should one understand this? The Master said: "Do you still find fault with a bowl that has no handle? [The monk] asked: "What about how..."
"This is subtle and wondrous. The Master said: "The wind carries the sound of water to the side of my pillow; the moon shifts the shadow of the mountains onto my bed.
[The student] asked: "What is the ultimate point? The Master said: "The vexing moon of the three spring months does not equal the brilliance of the nine autumn months.
[The student] asked: "When the physical body decays, what is the solid Dharma-body? The Master said: "Mountain flowers bloom like brocade; the mountain stream water is limpid and clear."
At Lanxiang’s Baisha Mountain in Xiangzhou, Chan Master Xing’ai was asked by a monk, “What is the pure *dharmakāya*?
The Master said, “A shrimp at the bottom of the well swallows the moon. The monk asked, “What is the true eye of Baisha? The Master said, “Looking southward.”
At the Zhugan Yuan of Baidiao in Anzhou, Chan Master Huichu of Beidou was asked by a monk, "What is it that every word must travel the profound path?
The Master said, "Following the road straight to Hunan. The monk asked, "What is a lion cub? The Master said, "Virtue."
Shansu succeeded Longtan. He asked, "What is the one phrase by which the Master benefits people? The Master said, "I have no old grudge with you;
the phrase has been right here all along. Shansu asked, "In what place does it reside? The Master said, "You dull-witted fellow!"
Chan Master Qingjiao of Mount Sizhu in Qizhou was a native of the Wang family in Fuzhou.
A monk asked, "Whose song does the Master sing? To whom does the lineage of the Dharma wind succeed? The Master replied, "Auspicious clouds rise by the side of Kai-shi Cliff;

the Dharma-thunder resounds before Baoshou Peak. At the time of his death, he left this verse: "I am eighty-eight years old; my head is covered with white hair. With a solemn and dignified countenance..."
The Twin Peaks: Clearly, the moon over a thousand rivers; Huangmei propagated the ancestral teaching, and Baidiao inherited the patriarchal secret. Day after day he instructed his descendants:
"Do not allow it to be severed."
A monk asked Zen Master Zhizao of Sanjiaoshan in Qizhou, "The teachings of the Buddha are many, yet the essence returns to a single thread.
Why does the Master speak so much of 'Zhou', 'Yu', and 'Ye'? The Master said, "It is for your sake that I speak of 'Zhou', 'Yu', and 'Ye'.
The monk said, "I ask the Master to show me directly, both past and present. The Master struck his meditation seat with his hand.
A monk asked Master Puchan, the Teacher of Xingjiao in Jinzhou: "The True Exegesis fills the dragon palaces and overflows the ocean treasuries;
I do not ask about that. What is the Dharma of the separate transmission outside the teachings? The Master said, "In the eyes, in the ears, in the nose.
The monk said, "Is it just this? The Master said, "What is it? The monk then gave a shout. The Master also shouted. He then asked another monk, "Where have you recently come from?"
[The monk] said, "We have set up camp. The Master asked, "Did you encounter any bandits? He replied, "We have captured some today.
The Master said, "I grant you thirty blows of the staff."
A monk asked Zen Master Zhengan of Sanjiaoshan in Qizhou: "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral style does he succeed?
The Master said: "Suddenly, when the true command is issued, one immediately sees the descent from the hall steps."
A monk asked Chan Master Xingchong of Taiyang Mountain in Yingzhou, “What is the inexhaustible treasury? The Master remained silent for a long while.
The monk was speechless. The Master said, “Come closer. As soon as the monk drew near, the Master said, “Go.”

Chan Master Shanzhao of Zigai in Luojing, a successor in the eighth generation under Nanyue and a dharma heir of Chan Master Huanglong Ji, was asked by a monk: "What is it like when one attains life within death? The Master said: "Embrace..."
With sickles scraping their bones and incense filling the heavens, they seek rebirth within the fiercely burning coffins. When asked, "What is it like when one dies immediately upon being born?
the Master said, "Fortunately, the awakening was swift."
A monk asked Zen Master Huanglong Jida of Meizhou, "What is the *nā* (monastic robe)? The Master said, "The needle has passed through;
the thread does not return. The monk asked, "What is the *pèi* (cloak)? The Master said, "Horizontally it spreads across the four worlds; vertically it covers the one universe.
The monk asked, "When the Way arrives in full measure, what then? The Master said, "If you want soup, I give you soup; if you want rice, I give you rice. [Recorded by] Huanglong Chushi.
[The monk asked: "World-Honored One, when the garuḍas fill the sky and fly about, what is it like? The Master said, "I ask you, have those garuḍas ever been satisfied?
When Zen Master Zao-shu was in his second term of residence, he asked a monk, "Where did you set out from? The monk replied, "From Min Province. The Master said, "Excellent!"
"Ah! [The monk] said, "I thank the Master for his instruction. The Master said, "What a pity! The monk bowed. The Master said, "When I speak thus, where does it fall?
The monk was speechless. The Master said, "He has no wound himself; do not inflict one upon him. A monk came to visit.
The Master asked, "Before you arrived here, where did you establish yourself and sustain your life? The monk joined his palms and stepped forward. The Master—
The monk also joined his palms, stepped forward, and stood side-by-side with the Master. The monk said, "I have not yet reached this stage; with whom, then, does the Master stand side-by-side?
The Master pointed behind him and said, "Is it not he? The monk was speechless. The Master said, "You deceive yourself alone, and you also deceive me.
The monk prostrated himself. The Master said, "This is precisely deceiving yourself. Later, while the monk was hoeing the ground, he saw the Master.

The Realized Man Lü Yán, courtesy name Dōngbīn, was a native of Jīngchuān. During the late Tang dynasty, he failed to pass the imperial examinations three times.
By chance, while at a wine shop in Cháng'ān, he encountered Zhōnglí Quán, who bestowed upon him the arts of prolonging life; from that time on, no one could fathom his attainments.
He once traveled to Guīzōng on Mount Lúshān and inscribed these words upon the wall of the bell tower: "One day of leisure and self-mastery, the six spirits harmoniously united."

He reported his well-being, saying: "The treasure is within the *dantian*; cease seeking the Way. When facing objects, have no mind; do not inquire about Chan. Not long after, he traveled through Huanglong Mountain.

Seeing purple clouds forming a canopy, he suspected there was a person of extraordinary character there and went in to pay his respects. He happened upon Huanglong striking a drum and ascending the hall.
Recognizing him as the one with the intention [to seek the Way], Huanglong wished to entice him forward and said in a stern voice: "Beside the seat, there is a thief!"
The Dharma Master said: "Lü Yigan came forward and asked: 'A single grain of millet conceals the world; within a half-measure of a cooking pot, mountains and rivers are boiled.
Tell me, what is the meaning of this? Longzhu pointed at him and said: "This is a corpse-guarding ghost. Lü said:

"But how can one deny that there is the medicine of longevity and immortality within his bag? Longzhu said: "Even after eighty thousand kalpas, it will ultimately fall into emptiness and oblivion. Lü was slightly surprised.
He brandished his flying sword to intimidate him, but the sword could not penetrate. Lü subsequently prostrated himself twice and requested instruction on the ultimate goal.
The Dragon rebuked him, saying, "I do not ask about boiling mountains and rivers within a half-measure cauldron; how is it that a world is contained within a single grain of millet?
At these words, Lü attained sudden enlightenment and composed a verse: "I cast away my gourd-bag and smash my zither; Henceforth, I shall no longer crave mercury within gold."
"Since first beholding Huanglong, I have finally realized that my previous efforts were misplaced. Huanglong instructed him to provide protection for him.
Later, he visited Chan Master Jue of Zhidu in Tanzhou, who said: "I traveled through Shaoyang and Chenzhou and descended eastward along the Xiang River;

now I meet Master Jue. Observing his Chan studies, they are sharp and lucid; his spiritual source is pure and refined. We sat together with knees pressed close, withdrawing the light to illuminate within."
Aside from a single robe, he has no other clothing; aside from a single bowl, he has no other food.

Chan Master Xiufu Wukong of Qingliang Yuan in Shengzhou was the son of the Wang family of Beihai. He left home to become a monk in his youth and received full ordination at the age of nineteen.
He once said of himself: "If one still clings to verbal explanations, one remains stuck on the raft; if one seeks to advance toward profound stillness, one must further [transcend it]."
Fearing he would fall into emptiness, and being unable to decide whether to advance or retreat, he abandoned both paths and went elsewhere.

He then sought out a master, but for years he failed to attain realization according to the *Kṣitigarbha Sūtra*. He fell directly into illness and entered the Nirvāṇa Hall. One night, Kṣitigarbha went to visit him and asked, "Is the Senior Monk at peace?

Yangshan replied, "When a single thought arises, one does not perceive arising, abiding, change, or ceasing.

The Master said, "Why do you negate the dharmas? Yangshan asked, "What did you ask just now, Master? The Master said, "Arising, abiding, change, and ceasing. Yangshan replied, "But you just called them..."
[The Master] performed the ritual for dismissal. He asked Yangshan, "How do you understand the wondrous, pure, and luminous mind?
Yangshan said, "Mountains, rivers, the great earth, the sun, moon, and stars. The Master said, "You have grasped only its phenomena. Yangshan said, "What did you ask just now, Master?
The Master said, "The wondrous, pure, and luminous mind. Yangshan said, "Can it be called a phenomenon? The Master said, "It is so; it is so."
It was so. Two Chan practitioners arrived at Shishuang’s assembly and said, "There is not a single person here who understands Chan.
Later, during a communal labor of carrying firewood, Yangshan saw the two Chan practitioners resting and took a piece of wood, asking them, "Can you say anything about this?"
Both were without obstruction. Yang said, "Do not say that no one understands Chan.

Upon returning, Yang recounted this to the Master, saying, "Today, those two Chan guests were exposed by Huiji. The Master asked, "In what way were they exposed by him? Yang repeated the previous conversation.
The Master said, "Huiji has, in turn, been exposed by me. (Yunju Xi said: "Where is it that Muzhou exposes Yangshan? While the Master was sleeping, [Yang]...
Yangshan came to inquire after his health. The Master turned his face toward the wall. Yangshan said, "Why does the Master act like this?
The Master rose and said, "I have just had a dream; you should try to interpret it for me. Yangshan fetched a basin of water and helped the Master wash his face.
After a short while, Xiangyan also came to inquire after his health. The Master said, "I have just had a dream, Jizi."
"Please explain this for me; let us examine it further together. Yan then brought a bowl of tea. The Master said, "The understanding of these two disciples surpasses that of Śāriputra.
Once, while the Master was plastering a wall, Li Junrong arrived. Wearing his official robes and holding his tablet upright, he stood directly behind the Master.
When the Master turned his head and saw him, he immediately tilted the mud platter to make the gesture of receiving the mud.
Li then turned his ceremonial tablet and made the gesture of offering mud. The Master immediately threw down the mud tray and returned together with him to the Abbot’s quarters.
A monk asked, "If one does not make the single-layered hat of Mount Mushi, there is no way to reach Moyao Village.

What is the single-layered hat of Mount Mushi? The Master called out, "Come closer! When the monk approached, the Master gave him a kick. He then ascended the hall and said, "This old monk has [a hundred...]"
Three years later, he went down the mountain and became a water buffalo. On its left flank, he wrote five characters that said:
"A monk of Mount Gui, [Name]. At such a time as this, if one calls it "a monk of Mount Gui," it is still a water buffalo;
if one calls it "a water buffalo," it is still a monk of Mount Gui. Ultimately, what should it be called? Yangshan came forth and prostrated.
[The Master] withdrew. Yunju Ying spoke on his behalf, saying: "The Master has no other name. Zifu Bao said:
"At that time, he simply made this [circle] mark and presented it. The New Ra (Xinluo) Monk made this [circle with a 'cow' inside] mark and presented it.

A "note" (*zhù*) means a "clarification" (*liǎo*). It is well to grasp this through awakening. Thereupon he composed a verse, saying: "It is not Mount Huai, nor is it the ox;
One body with two names is truly difficult to repay. If one departs from these two extremes, one must speak: How can one speak so as to emerge from the constant flow?"
The Master propagated the religious teachings for over forty years. Those who attained realization were beyond counting.

On the ninth day of the first month in the seventh year of the Dazhong era, he washed his hands and rinsed his mouth, arranged his seat, and passed away in serene composure. He was eighty-three years old and had been a monk for sixty-four years.
His stupa was erected at his native mountain, and he was posthumously titled Chan Master Dayuan. His stupa was named "Pure and Tranquil" (Qingjing).
He was the fourth-generation descendant of Nanyue and a dharma heir of Chan Master Weishan Yuanzhuo.
Chan Master Huiji Tongzhi of Yangshan in Yuanzhou was the son of the Ye family of Huaihua in Shaoyou.

At the age of nine, he entered the Guangzhou He’an Temple to take ordination under Chan Master Tong (who was the "Silent Tong"). At fourteen, his parents took him back home, intending to arrange a marriage for him.
The Master would not comply; he subsequently cut off two of his fingers and knelt before his parents, vowing to seek [the Way].
To repay his parents' toil, he requested the True Dharma; they finally granted their permission. He went once more to the ordination platform and received the tonsure.

Before even attaining full ordination, he traveled abroad. Initially, he visited Danyuan and already realized the profound essence. Later, he studied under Guishan and eventually entered the inner sanctum.
Tanyuan said to the Master, "The National Teacher once received the ninety-seven circular diagrams (yuánxiàng) of the Sixth Patriarch.
He transmitted them to me, saying: 'Thirty years after my passing, a śrāmaṇera shall come from the south and greatly propagate this teaching;
you must transmit it in succession so that it does not cease. I now entrust these to you; you should..."
He received it with reverence and subsequently brought the original manuscript to his teacher. Upon receiving it, the teacher glanced over it once and immediately burned it with fire.
One day, Tanyuan asked, "The various forms you previously presented were quite worthy of being cherished and kept secret. The teacher replied, "I looked at them then and burned them right away.
Tanyuan said, "In this Dharma-gate of mine, no one is able to comprehend it, save for my former teacher and the various patriarchs."
"Only a Great Sage can fully comprehend this. Why have you burned it? The Master said, "Huiji read it once and already understood its meaning;
I only used what was functional and did not cling to the original text. Yuan said, "Even so, for you, it is acceptable."
Later generations could not believe this. The Master said, "If the Abbot wishes for me to record it again, it will not be difficult.
He immediately compiled another copy and presented it; there was nothing missing. Yuan said, "Indeed.

When Danyuan ascended the hall, the Master stepped forward from the assembly, drew this ○ (circle) symbol with his hand, and after presenting it, stood with his hands crossed. Danyuan then interlaced both hands and showed them as a fist.

While the Master was washing his *kāṣāya*, Danyuan asked, "At such a time as this, what is it? The Master replied, "At such a time as this, where would one see it? Later, he went to study under Guishan.

The Master said, "Where is the Master? The Teacher stepped from west to east and stood there. Muzhou was struck by this. The Teacher asked, "What is the dwelling place of the true Buddha?
Muzhou replied, "By means of the subtlety of non-thinking while thinking, one returns to the thought that the spiritual flame is inexhaustible."
"Thought ceases and returns to the source; nature and characteristics are eternally abiding. Phenomena and principle are non-dual; the true Buddha is suchness.

[The Master] stood in a low and level place. Miu then desisted. A donor sent silk to Miu-shan. The Master asked, "How will the Abbot repay such offerings from a donor?
Miu struck the meditation seat to indicate his meaning. The Master said, "How can the Abbot take the property of the assembly and use it as his own?
While the Master was at Miu-shan serving as the *zhisui* (steward), he returned from his manual labor. Miu—

The Master stuck his hoe into the ground and stood with hands clasped behind his back. Mian said, "Today on South Mountain there are many people cutting thatch. The Master pulled out his hoe and walked away. (Xuansha said, "If I had seen him, I would have kicked over his hoe.

A monk asked Jingqing, "What was the meaning of Yangshan sticking his hoe into the ground? Jingqing said, "A dog carrying an imperial pardon; the feudal lords clear the way for it. [The monk] asked, "As for Xuansha kicking it over—what was the meaning of that?"

Jingqing said, "What can be done about the boat? Break the scoop! Yunmen asked, "What is the meaning of 'cutting grass on the southern mountain'?
