When the Master was herding oxen at Mount Gui, the Venerable Tietiantai asked him, "I do not ask about the lion appearing from a single hair-pore;
but how is it when a billion lions appear from a billion hair-pores? The Master then mounted [his ox].

When Niu returned, he stood in attendance by the side of Guishan and brought up the previous conversation. Just as he finished speaking, Tai arrived. The Master said, "This is that very same senior monk.
Guishan then asked, "When a hundred billion lions appear at the tip of every single hair, is this not what you said?
Tai replied, "It is. The Master asked, "At the very moment they appear, do they appear before the hair or after the hair? Tai replied, "They appear."
At that time, he did not speak of what came before or after. Guishan laughed loudly. The Master said, "The lion’s waist has broken," and he immediately went down.
One day, the First Seat held up a whisk and said, "If a person can produce the correct principle, I shall give it to them. The Master said:
"Is it possible for such-and-such a person to attain the Way? Can they return to it? The Abbot said, "If one can simply attain the Way, then one has it.
The Master then snatched the whisk away. (Yunju Xi said: "Wherein lies Yangshan’s Way? One day, as rain was falling, the Senior Seat Tianxing said to the Master, "What fine rain!
The Master asked, "In what way is it fine? Tianxing was speechless. The Master said, "I, however, would say..."
Dexing said, "What is it that is good? The Master pointed to the rain. Dexing again had no words. The Master said, "How can one of great wisdom remain silent?
The Master went wandering in the mountains with Muzhou Daowu. Upon reaching a flat rock, they sat down. While the Master stood in attendance, a crow suddenly dropped a red persimmon before them.
Muzhou picked it up and gave it to the Master; the Master took it, washed it, and passed it back to him.
Guishan said, "From where did you obtain this? The Master replied, "This is what has been moved by the Venerable’s own virtue. Guishan said, "You, too, must have your share.
He then divided it in half and gave a portion to the Master. (Xuansha said, "How great was Guishan! He was pinned down by Yangshan with a single sitting, and to this day he cannot rise.
Later, Guishan asked the Master, "Suppose someone were to ask you, how would you respond? The Master replied, "Master Dongsi."
"If Shushao were here," [the Master] said, "I would not leave you in such solitude. Guishan said, "I grant you one offense for which you need not provide an answer.
The Master said, "Life and death depend on a single word. Guishan said, "I do not fail you in my perception; yet others would not agree."
The Master asked, "Who is it? Baizhang pointed to a pillar and said, "This one. The Master asked, "What did you say? Baizhang replied, "What did you say?

The Master said, "A white mouse passes through; the silver terrace remains unchanged. Baizhang asked Mount Guishan, "When the Great Function manifests before you, I ask the Master to discern and clarify it for me.
Guishan descended from his seat and returned to the abbot’s quarters. Baizhang followed him in. Guishan asked, "What was it you were asking just now?"
"What words? The Master raised the case again. Baizhang said, "Do you remember my reply? Baizhang said, "I remember. Baizhang said, "Try to state it for me.
Baizhang then respectfully bowed and went out. Baizhang said, "Wrong. Baizhang turned his head and said, "If the junior brother Xian comes, do not say that I had nothing to say.
Later, Baizhang asked Dongsi, "May I borrow a path to pass by?"
"May I return by the same path? The Abbot said, "Generally speaking, a śramaṇa should not rely on only one path.
Is there not another? The Master remained silent for a long while. The Abbot then asked, "May I borrow one path to go over to that side?
The Master said, "Generally speaking, a śramaṇa should not rely on only one path. Is there not another? The Abbot said, "There is only this. The Master said, "The Great Tang..."
His surname was definitely Jin. While the Master was herding oxen on the front slope of Mount Weishan, he saw a monk ascend the mountain and descend shortly thereafter.
The Master asked, "Why did you not stay in the mountains for a while? The monk replied, "It was simply because our karmic conditions did not harmonize.
The Master said, "What were those conditions? Try citing them for me. The monk said, "When the Master asked me what my name was—"
The monk replied, "Returning to the Truth. The Master asked, "Wherein lies returning to the Truth? The monk was speechless.
The Master said, "Go back and tell the Master that I have answered him. The monk asked, "How should I say it? The Master instructed, "Simply say:
'In the eye, in the ear, in the nose. The monk returned and spoke exactly as he had been taught. Baizhang said, "You deceitful liar! This is..."
While the spiritual friend Wubai was lying down, the Master dreamed that he entered the Inner Court of Maitreya. Within the assembly hall, all the seats were occupied except for the second one.
The Master then took his seat. A venerable elder struck the gavel and said, "Now, the one in the second seat shall preach the Dharma.
The Master rose, struck the gavel, and said: "The Mahāyāna Dharma transcends the four propositions and cuts off the hundred negations..."

[One] said: "All sentient beings lack Buddha-nature. Yan-guan addressed the assembly, saying: "All sentient beings possess Buddha-nature.
Two monks from Yan-guan went there to inquire. Upon arriving at Mt. Wei, they heard Wei-shan expounding the Dharma;
its depths were unfathomable, and they felt inclined toward contempt. One day, while conversing with the Master, they urged him, saying: "Master..."

having finished presenting it with his hand, he threw it behind him and then opened both hands, reaching out to the two monks to demand it back.
The two monks were at a loss. The Master said, "My brother, you must study diligently. The Buddha-dharma cannot be treated lightly," and then he rose and departed. At that time, the two monks...

Another monk traveled several more *li* further; while crossing a stream, he suddenly attained realization and sighed to himself, "Guishan said that all sentient beings..."

While Master [Baizhang] and Huangbo were herding oxen together, Huangbo asked, "Is there any Bodhisattva here? The Master replied, "There is."
Miaoyan said, "Which one do you see? Point it out for me. The Master replied, "Which one does the Master suspect is not so?
Please point it out. Miaoyan then desisted. The Master presented some fruit to Miaoyan. Upon receiving it, Miaoyan asked, "Where did you get this?
The Master said, "From my own garden. Miaoyan asked, "Is it even fit to eat? The Master said, "I have not yet dared to taste it."
He first offered it to the Abbot. Guishan asked, "Whose is this? The Master said, "Huiji’s. Guishan said, "Since it is yours, why do you ask me to taste it first?
The Master said, "The Abbot has tasted it a thousand times and ten thousand times. Guishan then ate it and said:
[The Master] said, "A lingering sourness and astringency still remain. The Master said, "As for this sourness and astringency, do you not know them yourself? Muzhou did not answer.

When the lay practitioner Chigan heard the sound of the bell, he asked, "Does one with ears strike the bell, or does one without ears strike the bell? The Master said, "Just ask; do not worry that I will be unable to answer.
Chigan said, "I have already finished asking. The Master shouted, "Go! At the end of the summer retreat, the Master went to inquire after [Muzhou’s] well-being.
Next, Guishan [asked] him: "I have not seen you for an entire summer; what have you been doing down there?
The Master replied, "Down there, I cleared a patch of fallow land and sowed a basketful of seeds.
Guishan said, "This summer you have not spent in vain. The Master then asked, "I wonder, Master, what have you been doing during this summer? Guishan—
[The Master] said, "I eat but one meal at midday and sleep but once after midnight. The Teacher said, "Master, you have not spent this summer in vain either.
Having finished speaking, he stuck out his tongue. Baizhang said, "Jizi, why do you thus harm your own life?
One day, when Baizhang saw the Master coming, he immediately crossed both hands over his chest, flicked each three times, and then held up one finger. The Master likewise [acted].
They crossed their hands and each flicked them three times, then brought them to their chests with one hand turned upward and the other downward, gazing at one another.
Guishan stopped there. Guishan was feeding crows with raw rice; turning his head, he saw the Master and said, "Today I have given him a talk in the hall.
The Master replied, "I followed the custom and heard it. Guishan asked, "What is that which you heard?"
Sheng said, "The crow caws as a crow; the magpie chirps as a magpie. Wuwei said, "What can you do about sound and form? Sheng said, "What did you just say, Master?
Wuwei said, "I simply said that for his sake, I have ascended the hall once. Sheng said, [and remained silent].
"Why do you call it 'sound and form'? Muzhou said. "Even so, there is no harm in testing it.
The Master asked, "How would you test the Great Matter? Muzhou held up his fist. The Master said, "In the end, this is merely pointing east and painting west.
Muzhou asked, "What was it you were asking just now? The Master replied, "I was asking the Master about the Great Matter. Muzhou said: [and then struck him].
"Why do you call this 'pointing east and painting west'? The Master said, "Because of attachment to sound and form, I asked about your transgression.
Muzhou said, "Neither of us has yet fully understood this matter. The Master asked, "How can one come to understand this matter? Muzhou said, "To me, sounds and forms are as they are;
to you, old monk, they are east and west. The Master said, "The moon in a thousand rivers: its essence does not divide the waters. Muzhou [nodded].
Muzhou said, "One must be like this before it can be attained. The Master said, "It is like gold and gold; ultimately there is no difference in color. How could there be different names?
Muzhou asked, "What is the principle of having no different names? The Master replied, "Vases, platters, hairpins, bracelets, contracts, bowls, basins, and pans.
Muzhou said, "Ji’s discourse on Chan is like the roar of a lion, startling and dispersing the foxes, wolves, and jackals."

Seizing their blades, they demanded, "Monk, what treasures do you possess? The Master replied, "The treasures of a monk are not suitable for you. The bandits asked, "What kind of treasure?
The Master let out a thunderous shout. The bandits did not understand and struck him with their blades.
While Wang Jingchu, the Attendant of Xiangzhou, was presiding over his official duties, Master Mi arrived. The Official then raised his brush and showed it to him.
Master Mi asked, "Can you judge the void? The Official threw the brush away and entered his residence, never to emerge again. Master Mi was left with doubts.
The next day, he relied upon the Master of Offerings at Gushan to enter and probe his intentions. Rice (Mishi) also arrived there; [Baizhang] remained hidden behind a screen, spying on him.
As soon as the Master of Offerings was seated, Baizhang asked, "Yesterday, what words did Master Mi speak that you did not see me?
The Master replied, "A lion bites a man; a low hound chases after clods of earth. Upon hearing these words, Mi was immediately enlightened.
The former [master] was mistaken. Suddenly stepping forward, Lang laughed loudly and said, "I understand! I understand! The official said, "Understanding is not non-existent;

The official said, "This man has seen through it. He then asked a monk, "Do all sentient beings possess Buddha-nature or not?"
He replied, "There is. The official pointed to a painted dog on the wall and asked, "Does this one have it too? The monk was speechless.
The official spoke on his behalf, saying, "Watch out, he’s biting you!"

[The Master] entered through the ear. [The student] asked, "How is it? The Master said, "Do you hear? He asked, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different?

He asked, "What is the meaning of coming from the West? The Master said, "You have no Buddha-nature. He asked, "What is 'sudden'? The Master made a circle.
He pointed them out to him and asked, "What is the gradual approach? The Master struck the air three times with his hand.

For twenty years I have tested people with this, yet none have reached a definitive realization. You must take responsibility for this.
Daban Shan would often point to him and say to others, "This man is a Buddha in a physical body. A monk asked, "Mañjuśrī is the seventh..."
[The monk asked: "Mañjuśrī is the teacher of the Buddha; does he himself have a teacher? The Master said: "He has one whenever conditions meet.
[The monk] asked: "What is Mañjuśrī? The Master held up his whisk. The monk said: "Is it not simply this? The Master lowered the whisk and stood with his hands folded.
[The monk] asked: "What is the single phrase of wondrous function? The Master said: "When the water arrives, the channel is formed. [The monk] asked: "Where does the True Buddha dwell?"
"Where is it? The Master said, "It is signless beneath a word; it is not elsewhere.
When Chan Master Jing Tong of Mount Huo in Jinzhou first visited Yangshan, Yangshan sat with his eyes closed.
The Master then raised his right foot and said, "Thus it is, thus it is. The twenty-eight patriarchs of the Western Heaven were likewise so; the six patriarchs of China were likewise so."
It was also like this with his preceptor; it was also like this with Jingtong. Yangshan rose and struck him four times with a rattan cane.
From this, the Master referred to himself as "The Great Zen Buddha under Mount Jiyun who received four blows of the rattan.
(Under Guizong there was also a Great Zen Buddha named Zhitong. Later, while he was residing there, an attendant asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master then prostrated.
A visitor bowed. The Master asked, "Why do you, a monk, bow to a layman? The visitor replied, "Have you not read the passage:

'Reverence your disciples'? The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk held up his sitting cloth (*kaṣāya*). The Master said, "A dragon's head and a snake's tail. He asked another, "What is the Buddha?
The Master struck him. The monk also struck him back. The Master said, "There is reason for your striking me; as for my striking you—"
"You have no reason [to stay]," the Master said; the Sangha remained silent. The Master then struck him and drove him out.

When the Master’s fundraising for funeral expenses was nearly complete, he first prepared firewood in the countryside and took leave of his patrons one by one. Having finished his meal, he went to the site of the woodpile and told his disciples, "Come and report to me at noon.
When noon arrived, the Master himself took up a torch and climbed onto the stacked woodpile. He placed his alms-bowl hat upon his head and made it into a halo.
His physical appearance was such that he stood holding a staff, making the gesture of the *vajra* for subduing Māra, amidst a final mass of red flames.
Chan Master Wuzhuo Wenxi of Hangzhou was a native of Yuxi in Jiahe. His surname was Zhu.

At the age of seven, he entered Changle Temple (now Chongfu Temple) in his home district; later, he left home at Guoqing Temple. After receiving the tonsure and the precepts, he studied the Vinaya and listened to the teachings until his time came.

During the Changzong era, the monastic system was purged, and he returned to lay dress to live in seclusion. At the beginning of the Dazhong era, following the general practice, he underwent the ritual of repentance and ordination at Qifeng Temple in Yanguan.
Later, he visited Chan Master Xingkong of Mount Daci. Xingkong said, "Why do you not travel extensively to seek instruction?
The Master went directly to Huayan Temple on Mount Wutai. Upon arriving at the Vajra Cave, he paid his respects; there he encountered an old man leading an ox as they walked along.
He invited the Master into the temple. The old man called for "Kuntī," and a young boy responded by coming out to welcome him.

The old man let loose a cow and led the Master up to the hall; the entire building was radiant with a golden hue. The old man sat upon his couch, pointed to an embroidered seat, and commanded him to sit.

The old man asked, "Where have you come from recently? The Master replied, "From the South. The old man asked, "How is the Dharma maintained in the South? The Master replied, "It is the age of the Final Dharma (*mappō*)."
The bhikṣu had observed the precepts for only a short time. The old man asked, "How large is your assembly? The master replied, "It is either three hundred or five hundred.
The master then asked in turn, "How is the Buddha-dharma maintained here? The old man said, "Dragons and snakes are intermingled; ordinary people and sages dwell together."

The Master asked, “How many people are in the assembly? The Old Man replied, “Three times three before, three times three after. The Old Man called for his attendant to serve tea, along with some *sukara* (butter-milk) and curd.
As the Master tasted them, his mind was suddenly enlightened. The Old Man picked up a crystal cup and asked, “Is there anything like this in the South?
The Master said, “No. The Old Man asked, “Then what do you usually use to drink your tea? The Master was speechless.
"Yes. As the sun was beginning to set, the Master asked the old man, "May I stay for one night? The old man said, "You still have a mind of attachment;
you may not stay. The Master said, "I have no mind of attachment. The old man asked, "Have you ever received the precepts?"
The Master said, "I have received the precepts for a long time. The old man said, "If you have no mind of attachment, what use is there in receiving the precepts?
The Master took his leave; the old man ordered a youth to escort him. The Master asked the youth, "Three times three before and three times three after—how many is that?
The youth called out, "Virtuous One! The Master responded. The youth said, "How many is that? The Master then asked, "Where is this place? The youth...
He said, "This is the Vajra Cave Prajñā Temple. The Master was moved with sadness and realized that the old man was none other than Mañjuśrī;
he could not be seen again. He immediately prostrated himself before the youth and requested a single word as a parting gift.
The youth spoke this verse: "No anger on the face is the offering vessel; No anger in the mouth is the sublime fragrance; No anger in the heart is the true treasure."
"Stainless and untainted is the True Constant. Having spoken these words, Guṇṭhi and the monastery both vanished.

Only the five-colored clouds were seen, within which Mañjuśrī rode upon a golden-maned lion, coming and going. Suddenly, white clouds arose from the east and covered them so they could no longer be seen.
At that time, monks such as Xiuzheng from Pútí Temple in Cangzhou arrived; they still heard the mountain rocks shaking and roaring.
...the sound. The Master consequently halted his travels at Mount Wutai. In the third year of the Xiántóng era, he went to Guānyīn in Hóngzhōu to visit Yǎngshān;
there, his mind was suddenly awakened through mutual resonance. Yǎngshān appointed him as the *diǎnzuo* (steward). Once, Mañjuśrī appeared atop the rice-pot.
The Master took his rice-stirring paddle and struck him, saying, "Mañjuśrī is Mañjuśrī; Wénxǐ is Wénxǐ. Mañjuśrī then spoke a verse: "Suffering..."
"The bitter melon is bitter from root to tip; the sweet melon is sweet from stem to end. Having practiced for three great kalpas, you have nonetheless incurred the old monk’s reproach.
One day, a strange monk arrived to seek alms-food. The Master reduced his own portion and gave it to him. Yangshan, having foreseen this, asked:
"A person from the stage of fruition has just arrived. Will you provide him with food? The Master replied, "I shall set aside my own portion and give it to him.
Yang said, "You will bring great benefit [to others]. Later, he returned to Zhejiang and resided at Longquan Temple. A monk asked, "What is the mark of nirvana?
The Master said, "It is verified where the incense smoke ceases. He was asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "Bring the temple steward here. This master—
A monk suffering from epilepsy asked, "What is one's own true self? The Master remained silent. The monk was at a loss for words and asked again.

The Master said, "The clear blue sky is shrouded in obscurity; it does not fly toward the moon. The King of Qian petitioned the throne to grant him purple robes, and he was titled Chan Master Wuzhuo (Non-Attachment).

As he was about to pass into *parinirvāṇa*, at the hour of midnight he addressed the assembly, saying, "When the mind within the three realms is exhausted, that is *nirvāṇa*. Having spoken, he sat in the full lotus posture.
He passed away, and a white light illuminated the chamber; the bamboo and trees took on the same color. His stupa was erected in the western valley of Lingyin Mountain.
In the second year of the Tianfu era, Tian Jun, the regional commander of Xuancheng, responded to the rebellion of the Hangzhou general Xu Si and unleashed his troops to plunder extensively.

They opened the stupa and beheld that the physical body had not decayed, with both nails and hair having grown long. Qian Wang, the King Wusu, marveled at this and dispatched his subordinate general Shao...

His will was to increase his posthumous honors and have him interred. In the *jiachen* year of the Jiading era of our Imperial Dynasty, he was moved to the left of the stupa of Chan Master Zhijue Shou at Jingci Mountain.
A monk asked Chan Master Sunji Liaowu of Mount Owan in Silla: "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey?"
The Master held up his whisk. A monk said, "Is it not this very thing? The Master lowered the whisk and asked, "It is not the character 'yi' (以), nor is it the character 'ba' (八).
What character is it? The Master drew a circle to show him. Another monk drew a five-petaled circle before the Master;
the Master struck through it and drew a single circle.
A monk asked the Master of Yangshan Dongta in Yuanzhou, “What is the King’s Sword? The Master said, “The mooring rope has fallen; no merit is claimed.
The monk asked, “How is it for one who employs it? The Master said, “It does not fall into human hands. The monk asked, “When the Dharma King and the King meet, what is it like?
The Master said, “Both palms are impartial. The monk asked, “After they have met, what is it like? The Master said, “In between.”
An extraordinary likeness.
A monk asked Master Zhiguan of Jizhou, a successor of Chan Master Xiangyan Xian, "What is the Vairocana Teacher? The Master grabbed him by the chest and gave him a shove.
Question: "What is sudden [enlightenment]? The Master said: "Neither Liang nor Chen.
Chan Master Shaozong of Shouzhou was asked by a monk: "What is the meaning of the West[ern Transmission]? The Master said: "Good things do not leave the door;
bad things travel a thousand miles. A government official said to the Master: "I have heard it said that in Jiangxi no school is established. The Master...
[The Master] said, "It is established whenever conditions meet. [The monk] asked, "What is it that is established when conditions meet? The Master said, "In Jiangxi, we do not establish a school.
Chan Master Wuran of Nanchan in Yizhou asked a monk, "Does the Master still give an answer to the 'sentence-less sentence'?
The Master said, "From the beginning, I have only clarified this very matter. [The monk] asked, "Ultimately, how is it? The Master said, "Just ask and see."
A monk asked the Master of Mount Changping in Yizhou, "What is it like at the point where even a blink of an eye cannot reach?
The Master said, "I do not have the leisure even to blink my eyes. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch's intent? The Master said, "Coming from India, going to Tang China."
A monk asked Chan Master Chengfu Yanjiao of Yizhou, “What is the word for vast emptiness? The Master said, “Attaining the Way without a mouth.
The monk asked, “What is the meaning of the Westerner’s coming? The Master said, “Today and tomorrow.”
A monk asked Zen Master Qinggan of Dajian Mountain in Anzhou, "How did all the sages of the past realize [enlightenment]?
The Master then rubbed his forehead with his hand. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "A goat-headed cart pushes the bright moon."
A monk asked the Abbot of Fengde Temple on Mount Zhongnan, "What is the master’s house style?
The Master said, "I am wall-faced when facing any matter. The monk asked, "What is the matter of original nature? The Master said, "I certainly will not ask anyone else again."
A monk asked Zen Master Huí of Foyán on Mount Wudang in Junzhou, "I have recently been afflicted by illness and further poisoned;
I beg the Master to act as my physician. The Master said, "One bowl of 'double-appropriate' soup. The monk asked, "What is the matter that lies above the Buddha?"
He said, "The one with the conch-shell topknot. He asked, "What is the matter regarding the Buddha’s descent? The Master said, "The lotus seat.
A monk from Shuangxi of Tian, a practitioner from Mount Lu in Jiangzhou, asked, "What is the mechanism of the simultaneous pecking and hatching?
The Master made a pecking gesture with his hand. He asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said, "Where did you get that question?"

The constant sayings of Master Miling of Hongzhou, a successor in the Dharma lineage of Chan Master Yizhen of Mount Lingjin, state: "There is nothing that surpasses this. A monk asked, "I do not yet understand what this is."
"Nothing surpasses this. The Master said, "It does not go beyond this. Later, a monk asked Changqing, "Why does it not go beyond this?
Changqing replied, "What do you intend to call it?"
Master Shuangfeng was a successor of the Chan Master Gu of Shuangfeng in Fuzhou.
Gu’s original vocation was lecturing on the sutras. He went to visit the former Master Shuangfeng, who asked, "Where do you dwell, Virtuous One?
Gu replied, "In the city. The Master said, "Do you often think of me? Gu replied, "I constantly think of you, Reverend."
"Furthermore, there is no way for me to pay my respects and see you. Feng said, "This very state of thinking is you, Great Virtue. From this, the Master understood the essential meaning;
he immediately ceased his lecture series and attended upon [Feng] for several years. Later, he arrived at Shishuang, where he merely followed the assembly without further seeking instruction.
The community remarked, "The former attendant once received the seal of approval from Shuangfeng," and this was often heard by Shishuang. Shishuang wished to...
He pressed him on what he had realized, yet could find no opening. The Master therefore took his leave.
As they were about to depart, Xuefeng held up his whisk and called out to him from the doorway, "Attendant Gu! The Master turned his head. Xuefeng said, "To conceive of it is already a deviation;
to grasp it is already a departure. Not to conceive of it is not it either; do not try to form a conceptual understanding. Unless one knows 'there is,' one cannot know it. Go well, go well."
The Master responded, "Yes, yes," and immediately set out. Shortly thereafter, Shuangfeng passed away, and the Master continued as the abbot.
A monk asked, "When you took your leave of Shishuang at that time, what was the meaning behind Shishuang’s words?
The Master said, "He simply told me not to cling to right and wrong" (Xuñjuo said: "Now tell me, did he understand Shishuang’s meaning or not?").

Chan Master Rubo of Zifu in Jizhou, successor to Chan Master Xita Mu of the sixth generation under Nanyue, was asked by a monk: "What is the phrase that responds to the occasion? The Master remained silent.
Question: "What is the profound principle (xuánzhǐ)? The Master said: "Close the door for me. Question: "Regarding Lu Zu’s wall-gazing, what was his intention?
The Master said: "There is no connection. Question: "What is the true eye from of old? The Master struck his breast and said:
"Heaven! Heaven! [The questioner] said: "What harm is there in asking? The Master said: "I am weary. Question: "Does this accept instruction? The Master said: "It does."

[The student] said, "There is none. The Master said, "I have never dug into the earth to plant empty space. [The student] asked, "What is the urgent matter for a patch-robed monk? The Master said, "It does not go beyond this question.
[The student] said, "Before I have even asked, I request the Master to speak. The Master said, "Aha!

[The student] asked, "What is 'a single mote of dust entering right concentration'? The Master made the gesture of entering meditative absorption. [The student] asked, "What are 'the various motes of dust'? The Master said, "Three."
[Daowei] arose. The Master asked, "Whom did you ask? [Daowei] asked, "What is the one path to the gate of nirvana?
The Master snapped his fingers once and then opened both hands. [Daowei] asked, "How do I understand this? The Master said, "It is not the brightness of the autumn moon;
you yourself wander aimlessly in eight or nine directions. [Daowei] asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "Three bowls of tea after the meal."
One day, the Master picked up his meditation cushion and showed it to the assembly, saying, "All Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and sages who have entered the principle all emerge from here.
He then threw it down, opened wide his chest, and asked, "How is this? The assembly was speechless. A student asked, "I am a novice entering the monastery;
as the summer retreat draws to a close, I have not yet received the Master's instruction. I pray you will grant me your guidance and rescue. The Master pushed him away.
He said, "Since I have been the abbot, I have never blinded a single person's eyes. At times, as the Master sat for a long while, he looked around left and right and asked, "Do you understand?
The assembly said, "We do not understand. The Master said, "If you do not understand, then I have deceived you."
One day, the Master placed a meditation cushion upon his head and said, "At a time such as this, it is difficult to converse with you all.
The assembly remained silent. As the Master was about to sit down, he added, "It is still somewhat better than that."
Chan Master Huiqing of Bajiao Mountain in Yingzhou was a successor of Chan Master Nanta Yong.
He was a native of the kingdom of Silla. Once, he ascended the hall and, holding up his staff, showed it to the assembly, saying:
"If you have a staff, I will give you a staff; if you have no staff, I will take it away from you."
[The Master] took away the monk’s staff. Relying on the staff, he descended from his seat. A monk asked, “What is the water of the banana tree?
The Master said, “Warm in winter and cool in summer. The monk asked, “What is the ‘blow-off-hair’ sword? The Master said, “Step forward three paces.

A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said, "One hundred and eight thousand li. He asked, "What is the original mind?
The Master said, "Sitting atop the crown of Vairocana, appearing and disappearing within the great void. He asked, "What is the Teaching?"...
Regarding a matter transmitted separately from the external [teachings], the Master said: "Two numinous tortoises struggle in the mud; even until now, they are exhausted and will not cease.
[The student] said, "I do not understand. The Master said: "A wooden cock runs off with an egg; swallows and sparrows fly upon a tiger. The fish in the deep pool do not appear;
the stone woman, however, gives birth to a child."
Chan Master Zhiquan of Sanjiao Mountain, Qi Prefecture, successor to Chan Master Shaor of Baoci, the eighth generation under Nanyue.
A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Quickly prostrate three times."
[The monk] prostrated. The assembly prostrated. The Master said, "A single push and it turns.
Chan Master Ciduo of Xingyang in Yingzhou was asked by a monk: "How far apart are the Buddha-realm and the realm of sentient beings?"
The Master said, "You cannot express it. [The monk] asked, "Is it truly so? The Master said, "There is something of it.
(From the *Wǔdēng Yántǒng*, Volume Nine, Phonetic Glossary: *yīn* [pronounced *yúnlún*]).
